papers.title: Align Before Aggregation: Basis-Consistent Federated LoRA under Heterogeneous Ranks
papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) under heterogeneous client capacities is increasingly important, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) with heterogeneous ranks makes it practical. Existing server-side aggregators compose local matrix updates $ΔW_i$ from client-specific LoRA factors $(A_i,B_i)$ before aggregating them. Although these matrix updates lie in the same weight space $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and can be averaged directly, the LoRA factors that generate them may expressed client-specific local basis. In the typical compose--aggregate--factorize--dispatch loop, this basis inconsistency can make the rank-$r_i$ reference prefix dispatched to lower-rank clients unstable after server-side refactorization. In this work, we propose \textbf{FedAbA}, a basis-consistent federated LoRA aggregation framework for heterogeneous ranks. FedAbA first extracts each client's local basis, aligns it to the corresponding prefix of the global reference basis, and constructs a basis-consistent reconstruction of each local matrix update before aggregation. It then aggregates these reconstructions with weights that combine client data size and consistency score, followed by exact coefficient-space SVD refactorization and gauge fixing before rank-prefix dispatch. Our theoretical analysis clarifies the role of basis consistency and supports the proposed consistency-aware aggregation mechanism. Extensive experiments show that FedAbA outperforms representative federated LoRA baselines, with the largest gains under the strongest rank heterogeneity.

papers.title: Clouded Representatives and Score Matching for Distributed Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: Quantile regression is widely used in high-stakes applications where the data are distributed across many sites and the individual records cannot be shared. The existing distributed methods for quantile regression typically require homogeneous sites, large sites, or synchronous communication, which are rarely all satisfied in practice. In this paper, we propose a new method named cloudqr. Each site summarizes its observations by a few Gaussian clouds, each given by the size, center, and covariance of a group of observations, such that the clouds match the score of the raw data exactly. A central server then fits the quantile regression on the clouds from all sites. We establish the convergence of cloudqr under mild conditions. With simulation studies and two real-world applications, we demonstrate the superior performance of cloudqr over the existing distributed methods.

papers.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
Fractal basin geometry and the limits to predictability and reproducibility in deep learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Fundamental limits to predictability are central to our understanding of many physical and computational systems. In deep learning, training outcomes are often difficult to predict and reproduce even when extrinsic sources of randomness are controlled, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here we propose riddled basin geometry as a unifying dynamical systems mechanism: every initialization leading to one solution lies arbitrarily close to initializations leading to different solutions, forming a fat fractal with structure at arbitrarily fine scales. Using a minimal neural network model, we analytically establish the classical route to riddling and derive a near-zero uncertainty exponent: even sharp increases in initialization precision yield only marginal gains in outcome predictability. In deep networks, intertwined training destinations and near-zero parameter-space exponents provide robust signatures consistent with riddling across the tested architectures, optimizers and training protocols, offering a common dynamical account of otherwise disparate empirical observations. We further introduce functional uncertainty exponents, extending these diagnostics of scale-insensitive irreproducibility from parameter space to the learned functions themselves. Together, our results support riddled basin geometry as a candidate organizing principle for irreproducibility in deep learning, with practical implications for optimization and the reliable deployment of artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture
papers.abstract: Abstract The escalating energy demands for high-performance machine learning have sparked growing interest in unconventional computing paradigms rooted in physical systems. At the core of this emerging direction is the leveraging of physical properties to design computing frameworks that integrate strong learning capabilities, efficient training strategies, and practical implementability. Here, we present a simple, efficient, and scalable framework aimed at achieving this, and validate it on an optoelectronic platform. This framework features our proposed training mechanism—state-skipping direct feedback alignment—which eliminates access to intermediate states of the system and thereby significantly simplifies the error backpropagation process, enhancing both training efficiency and practical feasibility. Compared to conventional deep neural networks, our approach substantially reduces computational costs and training parameter count while achieving comparable performance. Furthermore, we integrate our scheme into modern architectures, attaining improved performance with an approximately 40% reduction in computational resources. Notably, our approach challenges the scaling laws of conventional counterparts, underscoring its strong scalability and practical promise.

papers.title: A language model-informed minimalistic design of functional coacervate vesicles
papers.abstract: Hierarchical biopolymer interactions in nature yield intricate architectures, while synthetic biomimetics adopt a reductionist approach to create scalable and tunable systems. Inspired by intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation into membraneless, vesicle-like condensates, synthetic coacervate vesicles (CVs) have emerged for drug delivery, protocell design, and catalysis. However, a general reductionist framework for rationally constructing CVs remains challenging due to insufficient understanding of the minimal motifs required to drive coacervates into stable vesicular topologies. Here, we present a protein language model-informed design of such minimal systems, where arginine-rich oligopeptides and competing anionic oligomers self-assemble into oligo-coacervate vesicles (OCVs) without any chemical modifications or external fuels. Combining experiments and molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate an assembly mechanism governed by an electrostatic-hydrophobic balance, which enables vesiculation across a broad range of oligomer pairs. This principle further permits de novo functionalization, exemplified by OCVs engineered to selectively recognize and encapsulate DNA G-quadruplex structures. Together, these findings establish sequence-encoded design rules for the predictable construction of vesicle-like compartments. The study presents a protein language model guided design of minimal coacervate vesicles that are composed entirely of oligomeric biomolecules, with functions programmable through oligopeptide sequences.

papers.title: Genomic language models decode bidirectional promoter activity and reveal conserved regulatory patterns across plant species
papers.abstract: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs), intergenic regions that coordinate transcription of oppositely oriented genes, pervade eukaryotic genomes, yet sequence signatures remain poorly defined. Existing approaches to BDP identification rely on distance thresholds and cannot infer activity from DNA. Here, we use Evo2, a genomic language model, to predict BDP activity and uncover sequence-encoded regulatory principles across four plant species (Arabidopsis, maize, rice, and wheat). We stratify BDPs by co-expression strength and compare Evo2-derived embeddings against k-mer profiles, transcription factor binding site matrices, and convolutional neural networks trained on sequence. Evo2 embeddings outperform all baselines, demonstrating that genomic language models capture regulatory information underlying BDP activity. Models trained on one or multiple species transfer to held-out species, and in planta validation in Spartina alterniflora confirms predicted high-activity BDPs. Sparse autoencoder analysis links Evo2 embeddings to nucleosome positioning and species-specific transcription factor landscapes, providing insight into sequence determinants underlying BDP activity . This work establishes how genomic language models can extract bidirectional promoter logic from sequence and identify conserved regulatory rules across plants. Bidirectional promoters (BDPs) are intergenic regions that initiate transcription of two oppositely oriented genes. Here, the authors report a framework that employs Evo2 genomic language model embeddings to predict BDP activity directly from raw DNA sequence.

papers.title: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
papers.abstract: Quantifying enzyme kinetic parameter changes upon mutations is essential for accelerating enzyme evolution. Current methods focus on predicting absolute values of kinetic parameters (turnover numbers kcat and Michaelis constants Km), yet they fail to accurately capture mutation effects. To our knowledge, no method directly models mutation effects (Δkcat and ΔKm) due to the scarcity of such training data. Moreover, these methods haven’t fully exploited protein structural geometry. Here, we establish a high-quality enzyme mutation effect dataset by pairing wild-type and mutant kinetic parameters measured under identical experimental conditions via a semi-automatic procedure combining language model-assisted parsing and manual verification. Leveraging this dataset, we develop DeltaCata, a Siamese geometric graph neural network to directly predict the changes in kinetic parameters induced by residue substitutions. DeltaCata demonstrates substantial performance improvements over existing methods, especially for enzymes unseen in the training sets. Its utility is further validated through in silico beneficial mutation screening experiments using deep mutational scanning datasets. Finally, we apply DeltaCata to engineer the methyltransferase sGmOMT2, achieving up to a 7.0-fold improvement in catalytic efficiency for in vitro icaritin synthesis. These results suggest the high potential of DeltaCata for industrial enzyme engineering. Predicting how mutations affect enzyme catalytic efficiency remains challenging. Here the authors build a benchmark dataset and develop DeltaCata, a geometric deep learning model that predicts changes in enzyme kinetics and guides enzyme engineering.

papers.title: zk-DEAP: A Zero-Knowledge Decentralized Encrypted Aggregation Protocol
papers.abstract: Secure aggregation in domains such as federated learning, Internet of Things, and voting requires operating on private inputs while preserving confidentiality, verifying that each input satisfies constraints, and avoiding trusted parties. Existing protocols achieve at most two of these requirements. We present zk-DEAP, a protocol combining lifted ElGamal homomorphic encryption, FROST threshold cryptography, and zero-knowledge proofs (Bulletproofs, zk-SNARKs, or zk-STARKs) for fully decentralized, verifiable, privacy-preserving aggregation. Our core technical contribution is a cryptographic binding mechanism preventing substitution attacks, where a valid proof for one input is paired with a ciphertext encrypting a different, malicious value. For Bulletproofs, we bind via ciphertext-derived randomness modification. For zk-SNARKs/zk-STARKs, to bind across algebraic structures (a well-known challenge in practical cryptography), we introduce a novel blinded arithmetic hash commitment with an embedded Schnorr constraint. These binding techniques force the ZKP's private witness to equal the encrypted value, ensuring any circuit-verified constraint applies to the ciphertext. We implement three production-ready, defense-in-depth variants in Rust and evaluate across 5-500 participants. Compared to unverified aggregation, zk-DEAP adds modest overhead while providing cryptographic guarantees against input manipulation that statistical defenses cannot match.

papers.title: Server-Side Sparse Assignment for Federated Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly recognized for their remarkable capabilities; federated learning (FL) offers a promising framework for collaboratively fine-tuning LLMs on edge devices while achieving data privacy. However, edge devices are inherently heterogeneous: clients may exhibit diverse data distributions and resource constraints, including limited memory and computation budgets. Recent federated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches address these challenges by using sparse expert activation or partial expert loading. However, existing partial-expert methods rely on heuristic full-pool observations or prioritize system-wide load balance, without guarantees for recovering client-specific relevant experts from partial observations. We propose $S^3$-MoE, a server-side sparse expert assignment framework that estimates client-specific expert relevance from partial observations and refines assignments through an exploit--explore mechanism. We also establish relevance-estimation error and exact Top-$K$ recovery guarantees. Experiments using a CNN-based MoE on CIFAR-100 show that $S^3$-MoE recovers task-dependent client--expert preferences and reduces conflicts caused by correlated expert selection across clients. Compared with Full-20 FedAvg, which gives each client access to all 20 experts for local Top-5 routing, $S^3$-MoE achieves 1.31 percentage points higher mean final accuracy while loading only $5$ experts per client.

papers.title: FedFiOT: Fisher-Weighted Optimal Transport for Model Merging in One-Shot and Few-Round Federated Learning
papers.abstract: One-shot and few-round federated learning (FL) reduce communication burden by constructing a global model within one or a few communication rounds, but often achieve lower performance than conventional multi-round FL. Without frequent synchronization, client models may drift apart, causing neurons that learn similar features to occupy different positions across clients. At the same time, local data heterogeneity can cause corresponding parameters to differ in their importance to each client's predictions. Together, these challenges cause direct averaging to combine mismatched neurons and assign equal weight to parameters despite differences in their importance. We propose FedFiOT, a Fisher-weighted optimal transport framework for one-shot and few-round FL that leverages Fisher information to quantify parameter importance and guide neuron alignment and model aggregation. FedFiOT jointly optimizes neuron correspondences and global model parameters through alternating minimization of a shared Fisher-weighted objective. Theoretically, we show that FedFiOT's optimization procedure monotonically decreases the layer-wise merging objective and establish a stationarity bound that quantifies the effects of client heterogeneity and nonuniform Fisher weighting.Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over competing baselines in both one-shot and few-round federated learning settings.

papers.title: Transversal Passivity: Dissipation Relative to Input and Output Manifolds
papers.abstract: This paper introduces transversal passivity, a local dissipation property for regulating input and output signals to prescribed manifolds. Its supply rate is built from the transverse port errors induced by nearest-point projections, so that motion along the manifolds is not penalized. We give a necessary condition and a constructive sufficient condition for the property and relate it to existing passivity notions. For feedback interconnections through negative-adjoint linear channels, power conservation no longer cancels the transverse supply. The residual is governed by compatibility defects that depend only on the channels and the prescribed manifolds, so it can be assessed before any closed-loop analysis, and it falls into a hierarchy of exact compatibility, quadratic cancellation, and nonzero quadratic residuals. Since transversal storages are only positive semidefinite, port convergence is obtained by combining compact confinement, for instance by conserved quantities, with a dissipation margin, and we identify a geometric obstruction under which no quadratic margin is available near the feasible states. A federated learning case study with heterogeneous data shows that port convergence can be certified even though no server target is compatible with the interconnection, and that the obstruction arises for a natural choice of target.

papers.title: Learning From Static Context in Federated Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Time series forecasting is shifting from locally trained, per-series models to global models trained across many heterogeneous series, which requires learning what sets the series apart. When the raw data cannot be centralized, such a global model is trained with federated learning (FL), one client per data owner. State-of-the-art forecasters such as the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) tell series apart through a static input that describes each series and does not change over time. In the special case of a federated setting where each client holds a single series, this static input is constant within each client and varies only across clients. We ask whether a federated TFT can learn from it. Per-batch FedAdam, which aggregates gradients after every batch, uses the static input almost as well as central training, whereas communication-efficient schemes with local epochs (FedAvg, FedAdam+Prox) extract far less from it and gain nothing significant on either application dataset. At the same local computation, an Adam-compatible SCAFFOLD keeps the static pathway responsive on wind power and gains significantly there. On building energy its error still drops, but the static pathway falls silent, so drift and communication frequency cannot be fully separated as the cause. Only per-batch FedAdam matches or beats the per-client local models across all datasets. We confirm the effect on building-energy meter data, a wind-power dataset, and a controlled synthetic dataset. The loss is not specific to the TFT: on the synthetic and the wind data two further architectures with different static-conditioning mechanisms show it as well.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for water quality monitoring: a PRISMA-based systematic literature review, taxonomy, comparative analysis, and future research directions
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate and reliable water quality monitoring (WQM) has become increasingly important due to rapid urbanization, industrialization, climate change, and anthropogenic activities that threaten global freshwater resources. Conventional water quality assessment methods primarily rely on manual sampling and laboratory analysis, which are labour-intensive, time-consuming, costly, and unsuitable for continuous real-time monitoring of large-scale aquatic environments. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and sensing technologies have enabled intelligent, data-driven approaches capable of modelling complex nonlinear relationships, detecting contamination events, and improving predictive decision-making. This study presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of AI-based water quality monitoring using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework. A systematic search of IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink identified studies published between 2020 and 2026, of which 91 met the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Review and survey articles were excluded from the analytical corpus so that secondary literature was not pooled with primary studies. A structured taxonomy is developed to characterise the strengths, limitations, interpretability and reported applicability of these model families. Because the included studies differ in target variable, dataset, preprocessing and validation protocol, no pooled performance comparison across model categories is reported and no meta-analysis was undertaken. The review identifies key challenges, including heterogeneous datasets, limited model generalization, overfitting, computational complexity, sensor calibration issues, data inconsistency, and the lack of standardized benchmark datasets. Furthermore, emerging research directions comprising Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), Federated Learning, Edge AI, Graph Neural Networks, Digital Twins, Foundation Models, and multimodal environmental intelligence are discussed. The findings provide researchers, practitioners and policymakers with a structured reference to the current evidence base on AI-based water quality monitoring, together with the methodological limitations of that evidence, to inform the development of future monitoring systems for sustainable water resource management.

papers.title: FL-SDMN: Federated Learning-Based Software-Defined Mobile Networking for Intelligent Handover Optimization
papers.abstract: The rapid growth in mobile users and the increasing adoption of data-intensive applications have created high network demands for low-latency and reliable mobility management in mobile communication networks. However, the traditional handover approaches are rule-based and rely solely on signal strength thresholds with hysteresis margins, which are prone to ping-pong effects and limiting their ability to adapt to dynamic network conditions. Machine Learning (ML) models have been integrated for handover prediction, but their centralized architecture compromises user data privacy, potentially conflicting with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). The centralized ML approaches also introduce scalability constraints that limit their effectiveness in dense network deployments. To address these challenges, this work proposes a Federated Learning framework for Software-Defined Mobile Networking (FL-SDMN) that combines privacy-preserving federated learning with centralized network coordination to enable intelligent handover optimization in 5G and beyond networks. The framework leverages a lightweight federated ExtraTrees ensemble model with weighted tree-based aggregation and SDMN controller to provide global network coordination. The federated learning framework has a three-layer decision pipeline that transforms handover control from a reactive threshold-based mechanism into a predictive, A3-derived optimization process without TTT persistence. The model was trained using real-world 5G mobility data, while handover performance, controller decision latency and scalability were evaluated separately using a discrete-time system level simulator. The findings demonstrate that integrating FL, Extra Trees, and SDMN provides a scalable and deployment-oriented approach to intelligent mobility management for 5G and beyond networks.

papers.title: Physics-Attested Federated Learning: Securing Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Critical Water Infrastructure
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables industrial operators to train shared intrusion detection models without disclosing proprietary operational telemetry. However, existing defences operate strictly in update space, leaving aggregators blind to data poisoning; model updates derived from fabricated telemetry remain indistinguishable from honest contributions. We repurpose process invariants, physical relations that always hold in normal operation, such as the conservation of mass, from runtime detection heuristics into a verifiable admission requirement for federated updates, mined automatically from clean operational data. We evaluate this admission gate across two physical water testbeds (SWaT and WADI) and a distribution benchmark (BATADAL), testing seven aggregation rules against telemetry fabrication, exposure-only replay poisoning, and an invariant-aware adaptive adversary. Across three testbeds, the mined invariants reject none of 25 honest shards except every cross-channel fabrication on SWaT and BATADAL, including optimised perturbations that the similarity-based FoolsGold admits in full. On real telemetry, five mined invariants detect 12 of SWaT’s 35 attacks, while nine invariants detect 20. With nine invariants, the admission gate removes 78% of the targeted-attack recall lost to replay poisoning (95% CI 57–97%, p<0.001 over 20 seeds) across five standard aggregators and 82% under FedAvg. To reconcile physical admission control with federated data privacy, we show invariant compliance using zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) to allow clients to prove batch adherence without revealing operational telemetry.

papers.title: MF-EFLJD: Multi-faceted ensemble federated learning for jamming detection in private 5G-enabled IIoT networks
papers.abstract: Wireless network security is a growing concern in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) as jamming attacks disrupt communication of IIoT entities in Private 5G networks. While machine learning (ML) algorithms detect jamming attacks effectively, centralized data collection from entities compromises sensitive information and privacy in distributed IIoT environment. This article presents a multi-faceted ensemble federated learning-based jamming detection framework, MF-EFLJD, to detect and further improve detection performance. To address the issue of non-independent and identical distribution (non-IID) and high-dimensional wireless channel data persisting across femtocells, this framework proposes sequential integration of Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) values to obtain optimized and structured data. Moreover, the framework trains 1D-CNN-based Federated Learning (FL) component on optimized data of entities to detect jamming attacks under non-IID conditions at each femtocell. Furthermore, to boost the performance detection of FL under non-IID, we propose Random Forest (RF)-based stacking ensemble component with an unweighted majority soft voting approach. Under non-IID setting α = 0.7 , the proposed system demonstrates that FL achieves accuracies of 0.9376 ( ± 0.0134 ) , 0.8806 ( ± 0.0178 ) , and 0.9576 ( ± 0.0169 ) for femtocells F 1 , F 2 , and F 3 , respectively, in detecting jammed and non-jammed signals. Additionally, the ensemble component achieves 0.9963 ( ± 0.0031 ) accuracy, depicting improvement in performance across femtocells.

papers.title: AI-Driven Membrane-Integrated Wastewater Biorefineries for Resource Recovery and Hydrogen Production: A Critical Review
papers.abstract: Wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are being reconceived as biorefineries that recover water, nutrients and energy, and membrane processes are central to this transition. This critical review examines how artificial intelligence (AI), and in particular, its data-driven subset machine learning (ML), is applied across membrane-integrated wastewater biorefineries: aeration control, membrane bioreactor fouling prediction, membrane-based nutrient recovery (membrane contactors, forward osmosis, electrodialysis, membrane distillation), struvite crystallisation, biohydrogen production by dark fermentation and microbial electrolysis, thermochemical sludge conversion, and hydrogen purification by gas-separation membranes. Reported model accuracies are high (coefficients of determination, R2, above 0.9 for several resource-recovery tasks), but they measure model fit rather than reactor performance and were obtained mostly on small laboratory or literature-compiled datasets (municipal, industrial, mixed or synthetic wastewaters and other organic feedstocks) with heterogeneous validation schemes and are, therefore, not directly comparable. Documented full-scale evidence is concentrated in aeration control (19.8% lower total operating cost than fuzzy-logic (knowledge-based AI) control at one plant; 26–30% lower aeration energy in a vendor-reported case) and membrane fouling forecasting. Validation practice, cross-plant transferability, the gap between explainable-AI attribution and mechanistic understanding, and the scarcity of techno-economic evidence are identified as the main barriers. A research agenda based on hybrid mechanistic–ML models, federated learning and a proposed plant-wide “resource ledger” is outlined for pilot-scale validation.

papers.title: Lightweight adaptive split federated learning for patient-independent ECG arrhythmia classification
papers.abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram monitoring in the Internet of Medical Things requires arrhythmia classifiers that run on resource-constrained devices and learn across hospitals without pooling patient data. We propose FedIoMT-RPM, a split federated learning framework in which each device trains only a 28.4 KiB client-side network, 6.8 times smaller than in full-model federated learning, while a bounded adaptive weighted aggregation adjusts each client''s contribution to its smoothed validation performance. Under the patient-independent inter-patient protocol of the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, with five clients holding complete patient records and six seeds per method, its detection performance was statistically comparable to that of the best federated baselines, with an accuracy of 93.97 ± 1.72%, a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.731 ± 0.039 and a macro-F1 score of 60.07 ± 2.41%. This macro-F1 reflects limited detection of supraventricular beats, with a sensitivity of 64.8%, and near-zero detection of fusion beats, and 1,381 of the 1,781 supraventricular test beats come from a single record. Among the split methods, FedIoMT-RPM averaged 18.9% less communication than SplitFed. Zero-shot INCART and PTB-XL benchmarks gave results comparable to the federated baselines. Reconstruction attacks recovered the ECG from the transmitted activations, which need protection before clinical use; membership inference stayed near chance.

papers.title: Mathematical modelling of ensemble-based federated learning framework for false data injection attacks detection in artificial intelligence of things
papers.abstract: Abstract Rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) has allowed intelligent data-driven decision-making under several cyber-physical systems (CPS) like smart cities, smart grids, industrial automation, and healthcare monitoring. AIoT incorporates artificial intelligence (AI) methods with IoT devices to develop large volumes of sensor data and improve system efficacy, automation, and predictive proficiencies. Among different forms of attacks, the false data injection attack (FDIA) has proven that high-priority cyber-related problem and has received more attention recently. The FDIA detection is an important security process in the smart grid controller system and is resolved by data-driven machine learning (ML) algorithms. Now, Federated Learning (FL) is a well-known ML method that assists in addressing data privacy problems by permitting users to collect its raw data locally and transferring it local model parameters only to the aggregator server to collectively train a shared global model. This paper develops a Federated Learning-Based Framework for Detecting Attacks Using an Ensemble Classification Model (FLFDA-ECM) in distributed cybersecurity systems within the Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) environment. The major intention of the FLFDA-ECM paper is to propose an FL-based cybersecurity framework for detecting and classifying FDIA in AIoT- enabled distributed systems while preserving data privacy. At first, the data pre-processing contains dual levels, such as handling missing data and feature scaling to regularize the input data. In the feature selection stage, the hybrid approach integrates minimum redundancy maximum relevance and ReliefF techniques to recognize the most appropriate attributes. Furthermore, an ensemble-based weighted majority voting approach incorporating bi-directional gated recurrent unit, variational autoencoder, and temporal convolutional network models is employed for attack detection. Finally, the parameter fine-tuned model has been executed by the Adan optimizer to enhance the classifier solution. The performance evaluation of the FLFDA-ECM technique occurs using a benchmark dataset. The empirical outcomes specified the boosted performance of the FLFDA-ECM model in comparison with recent techniques.

papers.title: AI-Powered Hybrid Healthcare Surveillance and Emergency Response System for Next-Generation Smart Cities
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of smart cities has increased the demand for intelligent healthcare systems that can provide continuous patient monitoring, early disease detection, and efficient emergency response. Conventional healthcare surveillance systems often face challenges such as delayed emergency services, fragmented medical data, limited interoperability, and inadequate real-time decision-making. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an AI-Powered Hybrid Healthcare Surveillance and Emergency Response System (AI-HHSERS) for next-generation smart cities. The proposed framework integrates the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Edge Computing, Cloud Computing, Federated Learning, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), Digital Twin technology, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to provide intelligent healthcare monitoring and emergency management. Physiological data collected from wearable sensors, medical devices, Electronic Health Records (EHRs), smart cameras, and environmental sensors are analyzed using hybrid AI models to predict disease risks, detect health anomalies, and generate early warning alerts. Edge computing enables low-latency processing for real-time decision-making, while cloud computing supports large-scale data storage and long-term analytics. Federated Learning ensures privacy-preserving collaborative model training without sharing sensitive patient data, and Explainable AI enhances the transparency and reliability of clinical decisions. In emergency situations, the GIS-enabled response module identifies the nearest ambulance, optimizes routing based on real-time traffic conditions, and automatically notifies hospitals to improve patient care. The proposed framework is expected to improve disease prediction accuracy, reduce emergency response time, enhance healthcare interoperability, and strengthen data security. Furthermore, it supports smart hospitals, remote patient monitoring, elderly care, epidemic surveillance, and disaster management, making it a scalable and reliable healthcare solution for future smart city ecosystems.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: Federated and GAN-Augmented Deep Learning Frameworks for Brain Tumor Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.abstract: Deep learning has transformed brain tumor detection and segmentation, yet clinical translation is impeded by data scarcity, class imbalance, heterogeneous imaging protocols, interpretability gaps and heavy computational demands This review brings together recent developments and highlights Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Federated Learning as central elements in practical applications. GANs expand limited datasets with high‑fidelity synthetic images that improve diversity, robustness and resolution for training, while federated learning enables privacy‑preserving, multi‑institutional model development that enhances generalization without exchanging raw patient data. We contrast GANs with VAEs and diffusion models, highlighting trade-offs among fidelity, interpretability, stability and efficiency, and examine hybrid CNN-transformer architectures, multimodal fusion, radiomics and optimization strategies that bolster performance. Key future directions include hybrid generative frameworks, explainable AI for transparent grading, fine‑grained tumor staging, multimodal integration, scalable architectures for resource‑limited settings and standardized benchmarks for reproducibility. By situating GANs and federated learning within an ethical and reproducible framework, AI systems may be developed to support clinical reliability, safeguard privacy and prioritize patient needs by helping to connect research with practical application.
papers.venue: ADCAIJ ADVANCES IN DISTRIBUTED COMPUTING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE JOURNAL

papers.title: Threat adaptive trust weighted federated learning for Byzantine resilient cybersecurity across healthcare edge networks
papers.abstract: The rising adoption of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices, edge computing, and distributed healthcare platforms brings with it a host of cybersecurity threats, whereas the centralized learning approach also brings with it privacy, communication, and single point of failure concerns. This study introduces the threat-adaptive Trust-weighted Federated Optimization (TrustFedHealth) framework for Byzantine-resilient healthcare cybersecurity, which combines the multi-signal client reliability estimation, temporal trust updating, norm clipping, error-feedback Top-k compression, and threat-guided Multi-Krum aggregation, with trust-weighted FedYogi optimization. The experiments were run on 15 k healthcare records with 52 attributes, with 12 k of them used for training and 3 k of them being future-held-out for testing, in 60 edge-node clients. Three tasks were assessed: security-risk classification, health-risk classification and health-risk regression. FedAdam showed the best security classification, with 93.67% accuracy, 0.9028 Macro-F1, 0.8867 MCC and 0.9898 ROC–AUC, while FedYogi attained the best ROC–AUC of 0.9904 and regression performance with 0.0516 MAE, 0.0651 RMSE and an R 2 of 0.6562. Multi-Krum has 0.8892 ROC–AUC and 75.77% security-classification accuracy when the attack rate is less than 20% malicious-client participation. A gender Macro-F1 gap of 0.0089 was achieved in the subgroup analysis and the expected calibration error was reduced from 0.0274 to 0.0185 by temperature scaling. The highest compressed checkpoint's accuracy is 90.46% and the highest Macro-F1 score is 0.8480, with a 22.25% cumulative communication reduction. The results show the promise of TrustFedHealth for secure, calibrated, equitable and communication efficient collaborative intelligence in the healthcare domain.

papers.title: PBS-FL: Anonymous Federated Learning with Verifiable Update Inclusion
FLHyHE: Federated Learning with Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables distributed and collaborative training while keeping sensitive data on clients' devices. This approach is considered more privacy-preserving since only model updates are shared with an aggregator. However, several studies have shown that these updates can still leak private information, making them vulnerable to various attacks. Privacy-preserving techniques, such as Differential Privacy and Homomorphic Encryption, can be combined with FL to enhance security. However, these methods often introduce a loss in accuracy and increase computational and communication overhead on the network. Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption (HHE) is a relatively recent type of cryptographic primitive that has been experimentally applied to FL to mitigate client-side overhead while preserving privacy. In this work, we propose a general construction for FL systems employing HHE, denoted FLHyHE, and analyse its security. We instantiate this construction on top of the Flower framework using the PASTA/FV HHE scheme and evaluate it experimentally. Experiments conducted on two well-known datasets, MNIST and CIFAR-10, using two convolutional neural network models show that model accuracy is mainly preserved for MNIST (≈2% drop), while performance on CIFAR-10 is noticeably affected by the use of HHE (≈20% drop). On the other hand, it is clear that a solution of this kind is significantly more efficient for clients in terms of computational and communication costs compared to solutions relying solely on Homomorphic Encryption, since it uses Symmetric Encryption as the main encryption tool. Especially as models get more complex and consist of more parameters.
papers.venue: Workshop on Encrypted Computing & Applied Homomorphic Cryptography (WAHC)

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Transferability and Sparse Observations in Federated Learning for Discrete Optimization
authors: Safa Mohamed , Reem Mohamed , Yasser Ali
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Medical Image Diagnosis using Federated Learning and Vision Transformers
papers.abstract: Deep learning model training is a central approach, which poses risks to patient data privacy and hampers data sharing for medical image classification, essential for computer-assisted diagnosis. In this study, a privacy-preserving medical image classification system is presented that combines Vision Transformers (ViTs) with Federated Learning (FL) for the classification of four categories of white blood cells: eosinophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, and neutrophils. The framework uses model training on local data in three simulated clients and uses Federated Averaging (FedAvg) to merge model updates without sharing raw images. A conventional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a centralized ViT are used as baseline models. The preliminary results indicate that the centralized ViT can attain an accuracy of 58.50% and a macro-F1 score of 51.82%, which is better than the CNN baseline (53.50% accuracy). The overall performance of the federated ViT can be seen as good with an accuracy score of 49.50% and a recall score of 96.00% for the class of monocytes, which suggests good class-specific recognition and, simultaneously, room for improvement at the overall level. An additional enhancement that can help prevent information leakage from model updates is proposed as differential privacy. Additional rounds of communication, larger sets of training data, hyperparameter optimization and formal guarantees of privacy will be explored in further work. This is a framework to give a basis for co-operative privacy-aware medical image classification.

papers.title: Federated Learning for Wind Turbine Fault Detection on CARE to Compare: code and results
papers.abstract: First archived release of the code and committed results accompanying Federated Learning for Wind Turbine Fault Detection on CARE to Compare (P. Mundhra, D. Poojary, A. Sharma, P. K. Loharkar; in preparation). Contents Leak-free client construction for CARE to Compare Wind Farm C (22 turbines) Local training, FedAvg, FedPer, FedProx and private (DP-SGD) federated strategies Matched centralised comparators CARE scoring, turbine-level bootstrap and Table I / Fig. 4 reproduction Committed run files for all reported experiments (results/paper/) Reproduce See the README's Quick start and Reproducing the paper sections. Citation Please cite the paper (see CITATION.cff) and the CARE to Compare dataset. Licensed under MIT.

papers.title: ALGORITHMIC BIAS, DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY, AND LIABILITY IN CLINICAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE A Critical Integrative Research Thesis on the Ethical, Legal, and Socio-Technical Implications of AI Deployment in Modern Healthcare Systems
papers.abstract: The rapid development and integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) algorithms into clinical medicine promise a profound transformation in diagnostic speed, triage efficiency, and individualized treatment planning. However, the real-world deployment of predictive and diagnostic AI models exposes systemic vulnerabilities regarding algorithmic bias, diagnostic generalizability, health equity, and legal liability.Modern clinical AI systems often mirror, amplify, or encode historical health disparities present within training data, resulting in unequal diagnostic performance across demographic, racial, and socioeconomic lines. This research provides a comprehensive integrative analysis of the intersection between clinical efficacy,algorithmic equity, and liability frameworks in AI-assisted diagnostics. The paper examines how data selection biases, measurement errors, and proxy target misalignments deteriorate diagnostic reliability in underrepresented populations. Furthermore, it investigates the legal "duty bearer" dynamic under current medical malpractice jurisprudence, where clinical AI lacks independent legal personhood, leaving human clinicians to bear the sole liability burden for algorithmically induced diagnostic errors. Finally, this thesis proposes a multi-tiered socio-technical governance framework—encompassing mandatory external validation protocols (TRIPOD-AI, STARD-AI), explainable AI (XAI) integration, federated learning architectures, and strict clinician-in-the-loop oversight—to ensure clinical AI serves as a trustworthy, equitable,and legally sound instrument of medical advancement.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: VeFed: a virtual epidemiological environment for federated training of clinical language agents
papers.abstract: Introduction Federated learning (FL) lets hospitals train shared clinical models without pooling patient data, yet FL is almost always tested on static, pre-split datasets. In the real world, cases arrive as a stream whose volume and disease mix follow each site's epidemic phase, and new diseases can appear that no site has seen. Methods We built VeFed, a testbed that couples stochastic SIR epidemics or controlled case-arrival schedules with LLM-generated patient-clinician dialogs across hospital silos. Each silo fine-tunes a LoRA-adapted DistilBERT classifier, and we compared six aggregation rules (FedAvg, FedProx, FedSGD, FedAdam, FedNova, SCAFFOLD). Fictional diseases ruled out prior knowledge from pre-training. We replicated key tests on MIMIC-IV-ED and MIMIC-IV-Note text and tested each claim against five controls fixed before they were run. We also introduce PrototypeBank, a federated nearest-centroid method that detects and names new diseases without retraining. Experiments used 10 seeds unless noted. Results Case-arrival shape changed time to competence (round-10 accuracy 0.557–0.920 across five shapes) but not final accuracy on synthetic text. On real clinical notes, the ramp schedule also lowered final accuracy (0.721 vs. 0.885 for burst). Staggered epidemic peaks across silos caused no detectable penalty. With ample data, federated and isolated training reached the same clustering quality and detected a new disease at the same round. With scarce data, prior federation raised novel-disease recall to 0.991, compared with 0.704 for isolated training ( n = 3 seeds). Softmax-based detection flagged known diseases as novel 92% of the time, and PrototypeBank cut this to 16%. kNN detection still recovered more novel cases (recall 0.954 vs. 0.444). Detection latency held from 3 to 10 silos (10.9 vs. 11.2 rounds). LLM paraphrasing cut the mutual information between text and disease label about 15-fold. Discussion Federation value depends on data volume. It adds little when silos have enough cases alone and helps silos where cases are still scarce. PrototypeBank gives up some recall in exchange for a smaller privacy footprint than calibration-set detectors. The proposed simulation provides a reproducible testbed for studying methodological and systemic aspects of FL in healthcare AI, supporting the development of secure, adaptive, distributed clinical intelligence systems.
papers.venue: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics

papers.title: Rainfall-Adaptive Graph Transformer Framework with Federated Edge Deployment for Multi-Label Waterborne Disease Risk Classification
papers.abstract: Abstract Waterborne diseases have become a continuous problem across India’s groundwater-dependent states. Predicting them has become a challenge because water’s chemical composition data sits scattered across concerned departments of state, and privacy regulations prevent sharing. This paper introduces the Biochemical Weather Groundwater Network (BWG-Net), a federated deep learning framework that brings intelligence to where the data exist and removes the need to transfer sensitive records to a central server. The framework is trained on 11,240 Central Ground Water Board station records from five Indian states, combining 16 biochemical water quality parameters with 6 meteorological variables fetched via station coordinates from the India Meteorological Department archives. It classifies contamination into 7 health risk categories based on World Health Organization and Bureau of Indian Standards limits. The architecture combines a rainfall-adaptive dynamic graph, which updates how stations are connected based on precipitation intensity, with a cross-modal attention module that learns how weather conditions amplify the danger of specific chemical contaminants. Federated learning lets each state train on its own data and share only model weights. On held-out test data, BWG-Net achieved 90.4% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.939, outperforming extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and a convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) model by 16.6 and 9.5 AUC-ROC points, respectively. The system also runs on a Raspberry Pi 4 at 73 ms per inference, making it deployable in field settings.

papers.title: FedXCrop: Privacy-Preserving Crop Disease Detection via Federated Learning with Post-Aggregation Explainability under Non-IID Farm Distributions
papers.abstract: Deep learning can classify crop diseases accurately from benchmark leaf images, but centralized training requires farms to share raw data, and predictions without explanations offer limited support for treatment decisions. We present FedXCrop, a federated crop disease classification pipeline that quantitatively evaluates explanations of the aggregated global model. A MobileNetV2 model trained centrally on PlantVillage achieved 99.38% test accuracy (standard deviation 0.05 over three seeds) on a fixed test set of 5,428 images across 38 classes. Federated models initialized with ImageNet weights were trained for 30 rounds across five clients. FedAvg achieved 98.81% accuracy with identically distributed clients and 98.81%, 98.59%, and 97.78% under Dirichlet label skew (alpha = 1, 0.5, and 0.1, respectively). FedProx was not significantly different from FedAvg at any heterogeneity level (McNemar p > 0.3). Grad-CAM and SmoothGrad explanations were evaluated on 380 test images. Both attributed more energy to the leaf than chance (0.70-0.78 versus 0.60), while Grad-CAM maps from federated and centralized models showed Spearman correlations of 0.74-0.76. Agreement decreased as heterogeneity increased, lesion localization was only modestly above chance, and a model-randomization test indicated that SmoothGrad maps depended substantially on image structure rather than learned parameters. In this setting, label skew reduced federated accuracy by 0.6-1.6 percentage points relative to centralized training. FedAvg largely preserved Grad-CAM behavior, while FedProx provided no measurable benefit.

papers.title: Analisis Kinerja dan Komunikasi Federated Learning pada Commodity PC Cluster
papers.abstract: Penelitian ini mengevaluasi kinerja dan efisiensi komunikasi Federated Learning (FL) pada Commodity PC Cluster di lingkungan nyata. Meskipun FL menjaga privasi, penerapannya sering terhambat oleh communication overhead dan heterogenitas data pada sistem bersumber daya terbatas. Studi ini mengevaluasi skalabilitas FL dan ambang batas efisiensinya dibandingkan Centralized Learning (CL) menggunakan 2 hingga 20 PC dengan berbagai kompleksitas dataset. Hasil menunjukkan skalabilitas FL membentuk kurva U akibat bottleneck jaringan. Peningkatan klien memicu lonjakan transfer data secara kuadratik, terutama pada kondisi Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (IID). Sebagai solusi, penelitian ini mengusulkan tabel pencarian heuristik yang memetakan ukuran model dan dataset terhadap jumlah klien FL yang optimal. Selain itu, sebuah persamaan analitis diformulasikan untuk menentukan kelayakan awal penggunaan FL dibandingkan CL, dengan mempertimbangkan batasan dan kondisi arsitektur tertentu. Kontribusi ini secara langsung membantu praktisi dalam mengidentifikasi titik optimal di mana komputasi terdistribusi FL terbukti lebih efisien daripada CL
papers.venue: Universitas Kristen Satya Wacana Institutional Repository (Universitas Kristen Satya Wacana)

papers.title: CARE-FL: Federated Fine-Tuning of Multimodal LLMs in Resource-Constrained Edge Networks
papers.abstract: Domain-specific adaptation of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in privacy-sensitive edge environments requires federated fine-tuning, yet client selection remains challenging due to heterogeneous multimodal data and modality availability, dynamic system conditions, and evolving client utility during training. We propose Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Federated Fine-Tuning (CARE-FL), a constrained online client-selection framework for federated MLLM Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning. CARE-FL formulates client participation as a sequential decision process and employs Q-value decomposition to address the large combinatorial joint action space through scalable client-level long-term utility estimation. These utilities are learned online using a modified Double Deep Q-Learning (DDQL) scheme, while constraint-aware $ε$-greedy execution selects feasible client subsets under per-round latency and bandwidth constraints. Complementing client selection, an adaptive aggregation mechanism further controls potentially unstable global updates and places greater weight on the previous model when needed. Experiments on the CrisisMMD disaster-response task in emulated heterogeneous wireless edge environments show that CARE-FL achieves higher and more stable test accuracy than the compared client-selection baselines across different system settings, while satisfying the imposed latency and bandwidth constraints.

papers.title: Vision Paper: Why Distributed LLM Post-Training and Decentralized Alignment Are Now Essential
papers.abstract: This vision paper argues that distributed learning, including federated and decentralized, should become a first-class paradigm in LLM post-training, not merely a privacy add-on. Current methods like RLHF and DPO rest on an invisible assumption: preference data should be centralized. We contend this assumption is scientifically unjustified, practically unsustainable, and ethically problematic. As LLMs deploy into healthcare, law, finance, and multilingual communities, preference data originates from populations that cannot or will not centralize. We develop a three-pillar argument grounded in (1) privacy and data sovereignty, (2) pluralism and representational equity, and (3) robustness and scalability. We formalize key technical challenges unique to this intersection, reference drift, preference heterogeneity, and the DP-utility trade-off for contrastive losses, and propose concrete algorithmic directions, and sketch a research agenda. Our analysis shows distributed post-training is not only necessary but tractable, and ignoring it risks AI that is legally noncompliant, representationally narrow, and brittle at scale.

papers.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
papers.abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment 1–8 , suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear 9–13 . Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)—a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution—and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

papers.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract RNA language models have achieved strong performances across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by its hierarchical structure, making the integration of structural information into pre-training essential. Existing methods often depend on noisy structural annotations or introduce task-specific biases, limiting model generalizability. Here, we introduce structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model that is pre-trained on millions of RNA sequences and secondary structures data by integrating base pairing interactions into masked language modeling through a novel pair matching operation. The structure-guided mask and nucleotide-level mask are further balanced by a dynamic masking ratio. structRFM learns joint knowledge of sequential and structural data, producing versatile representations, including classification-level, sequence-level, and pairwise matrix features, that support a broad spectrum of downstream adaptations. structRFM ranks among the top models in zero-shot homology classification across fifteen biological language models, and sets new benchmarks for secondary structure prediction. structRFM further derives Zfold, which enables robust and reliable tertiary structure prediction, with consistent improvements in estimating 3D structures and their accordingly extracted 2D structures, achieving a pronounced 19% performance gain compared with AlphaFold3 on RNA Puzzles dataset. In functional tasks such as internal ribosome entry site identification, structRFM achieves a whopping 49% performance gain in F1 score. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight a promising direction for developing multi-modal RNA language models in computational biology. To support the broader scientific community, we have made the 21-million sequence-structure dataset and the pre-trained structRFM model fully open-source, facilitating the development of multimodal foundation models in biology.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Abstract Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour 1–5 . However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Consistently, using a new deep-learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ, we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue microenvironments. We validate this cellular trajectory by using somatic mutation-based hierarchies in vivo and an experimental patient-derived organoid model ex vivo. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalized myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

papers.title: Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation
papers.abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. The translation of circRNAs is mainly driven by internal ribosome entry site (IRES) or IRES-like elements, which is tightly regulated by various trans-acting RNA binding proteins (RBPs). Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. These translation activators are involved in a broad range of biological processes including RNA processing, ribosomal biogenesis, and translation initiation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans-acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology. Circular RNAs are promising therapeutics due to their stability. Here, the authors identified 68 RNA-binding proteins that enhance circRNA translation, built a predictive machine learning model, and showed these activators promote IRES-driven translation in a context-dependent manner, expanding tools for circRNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific discovery across diverse fields. Yet scientific AI remains constrained by data curation, which demands substantial manual effort and deep domain expertise, creating major cost and scalability barriers. Here we present the Agentic Intelligent Data Engine (AIDE), a multi-agent framework that automates data curation for scientific AI. AIDE collects, selects, and organizes data in three stages, providing an end-to-end pipeline that turns a data request into training-ready datasets. We benchmarked AIDE on 14 tasks across biomedical and chemical domains. Scientific AI models built with AIDE-curated datasets matched or outperformed those built with manually curated data, and AIDE’s fully automated preparation delivered significant gains in efficiency and data utilization without compromising quality. These findings provide consistent evidence of AIDE’s applicability across scientific domains and usage paradigms and demonstrate its potential to accelerate scientific AI development and democratize access to scientific AI. Here, authors develop AIDE, a multiagent framework that automates scientific data curation, and demonstrate across biomedical and chemical tasks that its automatically curated datasets can match or outperform manually curated data while improving efficiency.

papers.title: FedSharp: Byzantine Robust Decentralized Federated Learning Under Noisy Channel
papers.abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) eliminates the central aggregation server but remains vulnerable to data heterogeneity, Byzantine attacks, and channel noise. We show that noise accumulates as models propagate across nodes, becoming increasingly significant as the learning rate decays. Moreover, accumulated noise enables Byzantine attackers to exploit loss-based model selection by mimicking honest model averages. To address these challenges, we propose screened, hop-aware, ranked, proximal averaging, a robust DFL framework (FedSharp). In this approach, each node maintains models from its 2b predecessors, ensuring at least b honest candidates when at most b nodes are Byzantine. FedSharp screens suspicious models using coordinate-wise median deviations, averages the b lowest-loss candidates to reduce fresh channel-noise variance by a factor of b, and applies noise-adaptive gradient-norm regularization and proximal training to mitigate accumulated noise and non-IID drift. Experiments on a 100-node ring with 33 Byzantine nodes show that FedSharp achieves 93.5-94.9% accuracy on MNIST, compared with 29.4-38.1% for a state-of-the-art single-model-selection benchmark, and 32.8-48.8% on CIFAR-10, compared with 10.0-30.5%, across Gaussian and hidden attacks under IID and non-IID data. On MNIST, FedSharp also achieves accuracy within approximately one percentage point of the benchmark operating without channel noise.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Training-Dataset Aggregation and Exact Machine Unlearning via Gibbs Probability Measures
papers.abstract: In this paper, three operations on Gibbs probability measures are studied: renormalization, normalized log-linear combination, and nesting. The resulting measures are shown to be Gibbs probability measures with explicit expressions for their objective functions, reference measures, and regularization factors. These measures are further characterized as unique solutions to optimization problems involving linear combinations of the original objective functions, subject to either relative entropy regularization or relative entropy constraints. When the reference measures are probability measures, geometric interpretations of these three operations are established involving Pythagorean identities and exponential geodesics.A central result is the equivalence between nesting and normalized log-linear combinations of Gibbs probability measures. These results are then applied to supervised machine learning with Gibbs algorithms, which are represented by Gibbs probability measures. In this context, either through nesting or log-linear combinations, Gibbs algorithms trained on local datasets are used to form new Gibbs algorithms trained upon the aggregation of all local training datasets. Interestingly, the parameters of such operations, determine the weights of each training data point on the aggregated dataset. %Operations on local Gibbs probability measures are shown to control the contributions of training data. This observation is leveraged for achieving: (a) exact machine unlearning in centralized, decentralized, and federated learning systems; and (b) centralized-equivalent performance, in the sense of producing algorithms trained on the aggregation of all local datasets in decentralized and federated learning .

papers.title: Federated Transfer Learning for Medical Image Classification under Mixed Skew
papers.abstract: Deep learning in medical imaging is constrained by data scarcity and by privacy regulations that make centralizing patient data across institutions impractical. Federated Learning (FL) addresses these constraints by keeping data local, but its distributed nature exposes training to strong statistical heterogeneity. Multicentric medical data is particularly affected, exhibiting a mixed skew that combines feature, label, concept, and quantity shifts across centers. Personalized FL mitigates heterogeneity by tailoring a model to each client, yet most methods assume training from scratch, which is unrealistic given the high dimensionality of medical features relative to the limited data available. We propose the Personalized Aligner Federated Pretrained (PAFP) framework, a personalized FL approach built on a pre-trained backbone. PAFP inserts client-specific Feature Alignment modules before the fine-tuned blocks to realign hidden feature distributions toward a server-aggregated target. On the FedISIC benchmark, PAFP attains the highest unweighted balanced accuracy while reducing inter-client performance variance roughly six-fold relative to the strongest baseline, yielding accuracy and cross-client equity jointly. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Alexandre-Leclercq/PAFP.

papers.title: FedCSGA: Evolutionary Client Selection with Joint Statistical and System Heterogeneity in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of machine learning models across distributed clients while preserving data privacy. In practical deployments, FL relies on selecting a client subset in each communication round to reduce communication cost, mitigate stragglers, and improve training efficiency under heterogeneous data and system conditions. In heterogeneous edge computing environments, both statistical heterogeneity and system heterogeneity significantly affect convergence efficiency and model performance. However, existing client selection methods often address these factors independently, overlooking their coupled and dynamic impact across communication rounds. To address this limitation, we propose FedCSGA, a Client Selection method for Federated learning based on Genetic Algorithm. FedCSGA encodes client subsets as chromosomes and evaluates these subsets through a non-linear fitness function that jointly integrates resource-aware metrics and history-aware participation weighting. This design captures subset-level interactions, mitigates persistent selection bias, and balances statistical utility with system efficiency. Extensive experiments on FMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet demonstrate that FedCSGA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse heterogeneity settings, achieving accuracy improvements of up to 7.0% and faster convergence with fewer communication rounds. These results validate the effectiveness of jointly modeling statistical and system factors to achieve robust and efficient learning in heterogeneous federated environments.

papers.title: Optimal Communication for Distributed Sparse Histogram Aggregation
papers.abstract: Histogram estimation is a fundamental primitive in distributed data analysis, with applications in counting queries and federated learning. In many settings, the universe of categories is enormous, yet each user's data involves only a small subset, yielding sparse local histograms. This raises a natural question: To what extent can local sparsity reduce the communication needed to estimate the global histogram? We answer this question by characterizing the communication complexity of distributed sparse histogram estimation under prescribed $\ell_1$ distortion and failure probability constraints. Our upper bound is achieved by a randomized covering scheme that optimizes how accurately each user represents its local histogram to reduce communication. By exploiting the distortion budget directly rather than imposing unbiasedness, the scheme achieves lower communication costs than standard unbiased sampling and hashing constructions. We establish the scheme's first-order optimality through a lower bound based on local support identification. The key step is to relate communication cost directly to the number of active coordinates revealed by each user's message, rather than to bound information about the aggregate via distance-based Fano's inequalities. This characterization further quantifies how the communication advantage of heterogeneous over homogeneous encoders varies across parameter regimes.

papers.title: Graph-Augmented LLMs (GaLM): Bridging Language and Structured Knowledge
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language processing and other adaptable domains, yet they often struggle with knowledge grounding and reasoning. Integrating graph structures, such as knowledge graphs and graph neural networks offer a promising avenue to enhance LLMs with rich relational information. Our workshop Graph-Augmented LLMs. https://galm-workshop.github.io explores the synergistic convergence of LLMs and graph-based methodologies and its applications with its transformative potential. This integration facilitates advancements in areas such as enhanced reasoning, improved contextual understanding, and robust generalization. We aim to foster discussions on leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and graph representation learning to augment LLMs, as well as investigating the application of federated learning and unlearning techniques to address privacy and ethical concerns in this rapidly evolving field. This workshop aims to foster discussions on how graph structures can empower LLMs to achieve improved reasoning, knowledge integration, and data privacy in diverse applications, including but not limited to biomedical, environmental and social-economic systems, with highly structured knowledge. The proposed workshop is the second iteration of GaLM 2025 workshop. https://iitbhu.ac.in/cf/jcsic/activities/workshops, which was successfully organized at ICDM 2025 in Washington DC, USA.
papers.venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)

papers.title: FedMCS: Federated Multi-Granularity Chemical-Semantic Distillation for Molecular Graph Learning
papers.abstract: Federated molecular learning enables collaborative molecular property prediction across distributed institutions while keeping raw molecular graphs decentralized. However, most existing federated molecular methods transfer knowledge through shared parameters, whole-molecule representations, or label-dependent prototypes. This makes collaboration vulnerable to scaffold, domain, endpoint, and label-space heterogeneity. These coarse or task-bound signals struggle to capture chemical patterns that can be reused across clients while remaining consistent with each client's local prediction objective. To address these issues, we propose Federated Multi-granularity Chemical-Semantic Distillation (FedMCS), which builds a reusable substructure-level channel regularized by a fixed fingerprint prior. FedMCS summarizes client-side substructure embeddings as compact Gaussian prototypes, allowing recurring chemical motifs to serve as transferable carriers while raw molecular graphs and task heads remain local. A gate conditioned on a client-local task embedding selectively reuses refined global mean prototypes when the same fragment has different relevance across endpoints. On the server, Soft Chemical Distillation regularizes prototype relations with fingerprint-derived similarity, encouraging the shared prototype space to preserve a fingerprint-induced neighborhood structure. Experiments on eight MoleculeNet benchmarks show that FedMCS consistently outperforms federated baselines in intra-dataset scaffold non-IID settings and obtains the best weighted average among collaborative methods in the cross-dataset setting. These results support substructure prototypes as an effective transfer granularity for federated molecular learning.
papers.venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)

papers.title: Edge-deployed graph learning for real-time telecom and financial fraud detection: a systematic survey and reference architecture
papers.abstract: Abstract Cross-domain telecom and financial fraud (attack chains that begin with a fraudulent SIM swap, intercept a one-time password, and clear an unauthorized transfer) now dominates high-value losses globally. Defenders restricted to a single layer see only half of the chain and routinely miss the relational coordination that characterizes modern fraud rings. Graph Neural Networks have closed the relational gap, but they are almost universally evaluated in centralized, offline settings, a regime structurally incompatible with the 100-millisecond latency budget of card-present payment authorization. This article systematically surveys 22 primary studies (2017 to 2025) at the intersection of graph-based fraud detection, multi-access edge computing, federated training, and blockchain audit, drawn from both the telecommunications venues and the broader machine-learning venues, and organized along a five-dimensional taxonomy. A coverage matrix exposes that no published system addresses all five dimensions simultaneously. We propose a reference architecture and identify five open research challenges. A two-experiment pilot implementation on the standard Sichuan Mobile CDR benchmark validates the spatial GAT backbone (F1 = 0.7737, AUC = 0.8039) and a FedAvg-based three-operator federated variant (F1 = 0.8622, AUC = 0.9263, Precision = 0.9364), with the federated configuration outperforming the centralized baseline on every metric, an outcome we attribute to implicit ensemble averaging and to cleaner per-silo graph structure. The result establishes that the regulatory and competitive obstacles to cross-operator data sharing need not be regarded as obstacles to high-accuracy cross-operator fraud detection.

papers.title: Dynamic Feature-Embedding Communication via Codebook Distillation for Federated Recommendation
papers.abstract: Federated recommendation systems commonly protect user privacy by keeping user parameters on local devices, while exchanging item parameters for collaborative model training. However, such item parameters usually model items independently and suffer from both efficiency and effectiveness challenges, making communication costs grow with the item space and limiting cross-item generalization and robustness to noisy feedback. To address these limitations, we propose to model items via shared latent feature embeddings for communication. Residual Quantization (RQ) provides a natural way to instantiate this communication by representing each item with a short sequence of discrete code IDs, i.e., Semantic IDs (SIDs).
