papers.title: Semi-asynchronous federated learning in Flower: Framework extension and performance assessment
papers.abstract: This paper presents an extension of the Flower federated learning framework to support Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning (SAFL). The proposed approach adapts the traditional synchronous paradigm to better handle client heterogeneity and straggler effects. By introducing a semi-asynchronous training strategy, the system allows partial synchronization among clients while maintaining training efficiency and scalability. We implement and evaluate the proposed modification within Flower, instantiated as the FedSaSync strategy, demonstrating improved robustness and reduced idle time compared to fully synchronous baselines in heterogeneous environments. The results show that SAFL can balance convergence stability and system efficiency in heterogeneous environments typical of edge and distributed learning scenarios.

papers.title: Over-the-Air Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Mobile Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Over-the-air computation has emerged as a scalable and efficient solution for deploying federated learning algorithms in wireless networks by exploiting waveform superposition for simultaneous model aggregation. Most existing work struggles with heterogeneous fading channels. These approaches either enforce unbiased updates from all devices or allow partial device contributions, requiring careful tuning of the convergence bound to mitigate bias under specific fading models. However, the former significantly amplifies receiver noise due to the weakest channel, whereas the latter is sensitive to fading model mismatch and converges only to a biased objective. To tackle these challenges, we propose FedOAG, which employs algorithmic components to automatically satisfy energy constraints via gradient normalization and evenly mix devices' updates through implicit gossiping. Importantly, FedOAG does not require transmission from all devices, nor does it rely on a specific fading model or knowledge of time-varying statistical channel distributions. We show that FedOAG converges to a stationary point of an unbiased non-convex objective at the best possible rate O(1/T) for any stochastic first-order method. We corroborate our analysis with numerical experiments over dynamic wireless conditions on real-world datasets.

papers.title: Reliable V2X-Enabled Autonomous Driving with Explainable Federated Neuro-Symbolic Intelligence
papers.abstract: Connected and autonomous vehicles rely on vehicle-to-everything (V2X) cooperation when local sensing is incomplete or delayed, as often occurs in dense traffic, occluded intersections, and roads with constrained communication. Yet many data-driven driving models remain difficult to interpret, and centralized learning requires large raw sensory data transfers that raise communication and privacy concerns. This paper proposes an explainable federated neuro-symbolic intelligence framework for reliable V2X-enabled autonomous driving. The framework combines neural perception, symbolic rule-based reasoning, fuzzy uncertainty modeling, and reliability-aware federated learning. Each vehicle trains a local decision agent from local driving and communication-context observations, while an edge or roadside unit aggregates model updates without collecting raw sensory data. The local agent also produces an interpretable rationale, including activated rules, uncertainty indicators, and risk factors associated with the selected decision. Simulation-based V2X results show that the proposed method improves decision quality, reduces missed safety-critical states, and converges faster than standard Federated Averaging (FedAvg) under vehicle-side data that are not independent and identically distributed (non-IID).

papers.title: Efficient Secure Federated Learning via Information-Theoretically Secure Key Distribution: A Medical Imaging Case Study
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of models across institutions without centralizing sensitive data, making it well-suited for privacy-concerned applications, such as medical imaging. To protect FL model updates during secure aggregation, additive masking is commonly employed. However, its underlying classical key establishment is only computationally secure. On the other hand, physics-based Information-Theoretically Secure (ITS) key exchange introduces practical constraints: finite key generation rates and time-limited storage severely limit throughput and sustained training of uncompressed models. In this work, we address this bottleneck by developing an FL framework that integrates frozen backbones, knowledge distillation, and quantization. These techniques reduce communication payload and, consequently, key material consumption. Moving beyond simulation, we benchmark this framework on a real physics-based key distribution testbed involving a chest X-ray classification application. Our results show that key usage can be reduced by ~35× while maintaining predictive accuracy. This prevents buffer depletion and key expiration, enabling sustainable FL training under physical key generation constraints.

papers.title: Efficient TEE-assisted robust aggregation for Byzantine-majority federated learning
Federated attention-driven client selection and aggregation for privacy-preserving human activity recognition
papers.abstract: Abstract Human Behavioral Context Recognition (HBCR) aims to identify user activities in real-world environments and has critical applications in assistive living, healthcare, and industrial automation. A major challenge in this field is achieving high model performance while ensuring user privacy, which is difficult for traditional centralized systems. Federated Learning (FL) addresses this by enabling decentralized model training directly on user devices. However, its success depends heavily on effective client selection and aggregation strategies. In this paper, we propose FAAM (Federated Averaging with Attention Mechanism), a novel framework that enhances FL by identifying and prioritizing the most relevant clients during each communication round using an attention-based approach. FAAM optimizes client selection and communication efficiency, resulting in faster convergence, reduced communication overhead, and equivalent model accuracy. We evaluate FAAM on four newly collected Human Activity Recognition (HAR) datasets, demonstrating that it outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in convergence speed and accuracy. Our results show that FAAM achieves optimal performance with fewer clients and communication rounds, making it an efficient and privacy-preserving solution for real-time HBCR systems.

papers.title: Rethinking Health Care Regulatory Sandboxes Under the European Union AI Act
papers.abstract: Abstract AI models have enabled substantial advances in health care. Since the entry into force of the European Union (EU) AI Act in 2024, these systems have become subject to a common regulatory framework in the EU intended to harmonize AI governance across all member states. One of the act’s distinctive features is that it accommodates existing economic, technological, and regulatory differences among European countries by leaving certain implementation responsibilities to national authorities. This is evident in regulatory sandboxes, supervised environments for developing, testing, and validating AI systems before deployment. In this viewpoint, we provide a policy-oriented analysis of health care regulatory sandboxes under the EU AI Act and propose recommendations for their design. These recommendations address the need to document model compression techniques that may affect the classification of large high-risk systems above the 10 25 floating point operations per second threshold, incorporate explainability into AI systems from the design stage, identify and document biases in health care datasets, clarify the treatment of federated learning parameter updates under the General Data Protection Regulation, and strengthen the oversight of AI agents in clinical environments. The implementation timeline makes this discussion particularly timely given the approaching deadline of August 2, 2027, by which all member states must have established at least one national regulatory sandbox.

papers.title: FedCRA: Client Risk-aware Aggregation via Update Reconstruction for IoT-based Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables distributed model training without sharing raw data, making it particularly suitable for Internet of Things (IoT) environments. However, FL remains vulnerable to poisoning attacks, where malicious clients manipulate local updates to corrupt global model optimization. Existing defenses mainly focus on updates within a single round and may confuse heterogeneous benign updates with malicious ones. In this paper, we propose FedCRA, a client risk-aware aggregation framework that exploits historical trajectories and trusted reference updates to reconstruct updates. Furthermore, the risk-aware aggregation jointly considers reconstruction gap, reference gap, and historical trajectory information to adaptively suppress suspicious updates. Extensive experiments under multiple poisoning attacks and heterogeneous data distributions demonstrate that FedCRA achieves stronger robustness than several representative aggregation methods while maintaining good scalability in large-scale FL.

papers.title: From expansion to intelligent governance: structural transformation and regulatory paradigm reconstruction in China’s health insurance reform: a systematic literature review on the evolution and future trajectories of health insurance fund supervision
papers.abstract: Background Over the past quarter century, China has undergone three transformations in healthcare financing: from employer-sponsored coverage to universal enrollment, then toward quality- and intelligence-oriented governance. This review examines the evolution and future of medical insurance fund supervision in China. Methods Five databases were searched on June 15, 2025. Included publications addressed fund supervision, payment reform, intelligent technology, sustainability, equity, or anti-corruption in China. MMAT and AMSTAR-2 criteria were used for quality appraisal. Each publication was independently assessed by two reviewers using the MMAT screening questions and domain ratings; disagreements were resolved through consensus discussion, with an independent third assessor arbitrating unresolved cases. Inter-rater reliability on a 20% random subset yielded substantial agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.82). PRISMA 2020 guidelines were followed; no PROSPERO registration was made. Results Three core findings emerged via the Intelligent Supervision Integration (ISI) framework (data, algorithm, institution layers). First, fund supervision evolved through three phases, with the 2018 NHSA establishment as pivotal. Second, DRG/DIP reforms contained costs but generated upcoding and cost-shifting. Third, ML-based and blockchain-based fraud detection have transitioned to operational deployment. Conclusion The ISI framework explains China’s transition to intelligent governance. Six prospective trends are identified: (1) data-driven supervision, (2) federated learning for privacy-preserving analytics, (3) blockchain-based full-chain supervision, (4) intelligent actuarial early warning systems, (5) institutionalized integrity governance, and (6) localization-optimized payment reform.

papers.title: Expression of Concern: Nuclei segmentation and classification from histopathology images using federated learning for end-edge platform
Strategic Client-Level Defense Placement in Mobile Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables mobile and edge devices to train jointly without centralizing private data, but compromised clients can poison the global model. When client-level protections cover only part of the population, a rational attacker can exploit predictable placement. We introduce SGDP-FL (Stackelberg Game-Based Defense Placement for Federated Learning), a budget-constrained Stackelberg game between a defender and an attacker. Before each round, the defender decides which clients to protect. The attacker observes this placement only through noisy reconnaissance, updates its belief about which clients are protected, and then chooses which clients to attack. We model the noisy observation as a Binary Symmetric Channel, and we model imperfect defenses by letting each protection block an attack only with a fixed probability. Monte Carlo estimation and a greedy knapsack oracle make the resulting bilevel problem tractable. We evaluate SGDP-FL on EMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 under IID and non-IID partitions. The evaluation covers single- and multi-client attacks, with attack targets either fixed or periodically reshuffled. In every tested setting, SGDP-FL achieves the highest mean accuracy among Random, Highest-Value, and UCB allocation. Under multi-client attacks with periodic reshuffling, it raises CIFAR-10 IID accuracy from 55.68% for the strongest baseline to 59.78%, and CIFAR-100 IID from 32.42% to 34.49%. It also transfers to label-flipping and backdoor attacks and complements robust aggregation.

papers.title: HIV-PrivFed: Privacy–Utility–Fairness-Aware Federated Learning for HIV Risk Stratification and Testing Prioritization Under Non-IID Clinical Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: HIV screening from routinely collected behavioral data could help to prioritize testing across clinics that cannot centralize sensitive records; however, the utility, privacy, and client-level fairness of federated models on real non-IID data are poorly characterized. Methods: Using Sialon-II, a cohort of men who have sex with men in 13 European cities (13 natural clients; horizontal federated learning), we benchmarked ten conventional classifiers and a centralized residual MLP, compared local-only, FedAvg, and FedProx baselines, and evaluated HIV-PrivFed, a differentially private FedProx-based algorithm with client-by-client Rényi accounting and client-level fairness auditing (fairness is audited, not enforced); secure aggregation overhead was benchmarked in simulation. Results: The best conventional model reached an AUROC of 0.696 (AUPRC 0.235), statistically indistinguishable from logistic regression on the original partition. Federated learning exceeded local-only learning (AUROC 0.607 versus 0.565). Achieved worst-client privacy budgets (ε = 22.1–224.1) were far looser than the nominal targets and give no meaningful guarantee; accuracy was retained at these budgets (AUROC 0.629–0.650) but fell to 0.553 and 0.524 at ε=8 and 4. Client-level estimates were highly uncertain. Conclusions: Useful accuracy and a meaningful privacy guarantee did not coexist in this small-cohort setting; larger cohorts and external validation are needed before deployment.

papers.title: Multimodal prediction of chronic ankle instability and exploratory treatment response using longitudinal delta-radiomics, wearable biomechanics, and conformal prediction
papers.abstract: Background Chronic ankle instability (CAI) develops in about 40% of patients after a lateral ankle sprain, yet no validated tool separates rehabilitation responders from surgical candidates at initial presentation. Methods In a multicenter cohort of 1420 patients (development: n = 1040; external test: n = 380), we combined baseline and 6-week MRI (delta-radiomics), 7-day free-living IMU biomechanics, and patient-reported outcomes. A Feature Tokenization Transformer (FT-Transformer) was compared with LightGBM, XGBoost, logistic regression, and TabPFN v2 using nested 5-fold cross-validation. A federated model (Fed-GBDT; ε = 1.0 differential privacy) enabled privacy-preserving deployment, and a conformal prediction nomogram provided 90%-coverage uncertainty intervals. Results On external testing, the FT-Transformer achieved an AUC of 0.869 (95% CI: 0.843–0.895) and an accuracy of 80.0% for CAI diagnosis, and an AUC of 0.838 (95% CI: 0.789–0.887) for treatment-response stratification (exploratory). Delta-radiomics (ΔAUC +0.023, 95% CI: 0.013–0.033) and IMU features (ΔAUC +0.015, 95% CI: 0.005–0.025) added independent value. The federated model matched the centralized model (ΔAUC −0.003), and the imaging + IMU-only variant (AUC 0.843) exceeded two radiologists (AUC 0.803 and 0.779; different rating scales). Nomogram coverage was 91.4%. Conclusions This framework combines longitudinal delta-radiomics, wearable biomechanics, and federated learning with calibrated uncertainty for CAI prediction. Treatment-response stratification is hypothesis-generating and needs prospective multicenter validation before clinical use.

papers.title: Code, data and results for "Robust aggregation scores can rank a free-rider first: Limits of Verification in Prototype-Based Federated Learning"
papers.abstract: Code, measured results, prototype trajectories and model checkpoints for the article "Robust Aggregation Scores Can Rank a Free-Rider First: Limits of Verification in Prototype-Based Federated Learning" by Ali Mohammadi Ruzbahani, Abbas Yazdinejad and Hadis Karimipour. The record contains two archives:Robust-Aggregation-code.zip: the Python implementation (prototype-based federation with FedProto and FedTGP servers, identity protocol, payload auditor, attacks and robust aggregation rules), the experiment and analysis scripts, the measured results as JSON, the exported result tables and figures, tests, and a reproduction notebook (notebooks/reproduce.ipynb) whose job catalogue lists the command of every experiment. In archived mode the notebook regenerates every result table and figure and checks the recorded values from the JSON results, without the data archive. Replay mode recomputes the detector, geometry and attack analyses from the trajectories and checkpoints; fresh mode retrains the federations on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, which are downloaded from their original sources. Installation and usage are described in README.md. The code and the measured results are released under the MIT License.

SolidFL demonstration: ontology-driven federated learning over Solid pods for cross-laboratory bovine respiratory disease surveillance (DECIDE Work Package 1)
papers.abstract: This video demonstrates SolidFL, a working implementation of horizontal federated learning over Solid pods, developed in the EU Horizon 2020 project DECIDE (Work Package 1) to forecast the monthly positive sample rate of bovine respiratory disease (BRD) pathogens across veterinary diagnostic laboratories. The demonstration shows the complete pipeline running in containers: six laboratories, each with its own Solid pod (Community Solid Server) and a sidecar agent; laboratories opting in to federated learning through a flag in their own pod; local training of a hybrid graph convolutional network and gated recurrent unit (GCN-GRU) model, with features and graph structure derived from the Livestock Health Ontology (LHO); exchange of model weights only, through the pods; asynchronous federated averaging (FedAvg) at a central aggregator; and a live dashboard of federated validation performance. Raw diagnostic records never leave the laboratory pods. This video is supplementary material to the manuscript "Ontology-driven federated learning for cross-laboratory livestock disease surveillance: a bovine respiratory disease case study" (Noor et al.).

papers.title: Applying AI to Road Infrastructure Monitoring and Management: A Vision for Predictive Maintenance and Safety Management
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across the road infrastructure lifecycle, highlighting state-of-the-art technologies and real-world applications. It examines the use of predictive modelling, digital twins, and knowledge graphs in planning; computer vision and deep learning for defect detection during construction; and edge computing, federated learning, and multi-agent reinforcement learning for adaptive traffic management. In maintenance, AI-driven inspections using drones, LiDAR, and vision transformers enable predictive upkeep. Novel approaches such as neuro-symbolic AI, explainable AI (e.g., SHAP, LIME), and two-stage knowledge frameworks enhance transparency and context-awareness. Considering regulatory frameworks (like GDPR, EU AI Act), organisational challenges, and best practices for implementation such as embedded influence into governance and infrastructure strategies can significantly improve resilience, safety, and efficiency in transport systems. The paper proposes such a complete AI system for European road networks (both primary and secondary roads) today, considering the real-world management of infrastructure in the EU today, identifying the gaps. The paper argues that overcoming these challenges requires a holistic framework that integrates technological innovation with robust regulatory compliance and societal engagement and concludes by proposing a strategic pathway for EU-wide adoption.

papers.title: Federated learning approach with Graph convolutional deep feature optimization and parallel attention Network for leaf disease classification
PRISM: Reinforced Semantic Communication for Decentralized Federated Anomaly Detection in Vehicular Networks
papers.abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) enables collaborative learning that preserves privacy, but faces critical communication challenges in bandwidth-constrained environments such as vehicular networks. We propose Policy-driven Representation and Information Selection Method (PRISM), a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based method that optimizes semantic communication in DFL through adaptive representation selection and intelligent topology management. Our dual-model architecture separates task learning (autoencoder-based anomaly detection) from communication control (Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based decision making), enabling agents to dynamically select between transmitting full model weights or compressed trajectory embeddings. We formulate this as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and train using a Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. We demonstrate our method through a digital twin monitoring scenario where vehicles collaboratively detect trajectory anomalies in neighbors' behavior in real time, and the logged detections support forensic analysis, insurance claims, and fleet auditing. Experiments on Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) generated Barcelona traffic data show an F1-score of 0.90, scaling from 2 to 128 agents with graceful degradation past N = 32, Byzantine-robust aggregation, and validation on Next Generation Simulation (NGSIM) US-101 real traces (F1 0.82). The learned policy exhibits emergent temporal behavior: transmitting weights early during training when model divergence is high, then shifting to embeddings as models converge, with the weight-to-embedding mix derived as the equilibrium of the communication budget constraint. The method generalizes to other bandwidth-limited collaborative learning domains.

papers.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Cybersecurity Complexity in Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: The growth and integration of cloud computing with other advanced technologies (such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other security technologies and architectures) have introduced different cybersecurity challenges and opportunities that require academic investigation. This research conducts a bibliometric analysis of 1,583 papers from Scopus database between 2010 to 2026 trying to address four main research aims: (1) publication growth and productivity, (2) active contributors in the field, (3) themes and evolution of cloud security, and (4) emerging and research directions. The findings reveal an exponential growth, with annual output rising from 3 papers in 2010 to 358 in 2025, highlighting an annual growth rate exceeding 30%. Keyword analysis also reveals technical security evolutions: from cloud architecture and basic security (2010–2015), through threat, privacy, risk and intelligent detection (2016–2020), to current state dominated AI-driven approaches and other cutting edge technologies such as blockchain, edge computing, quantum cryptography and decentralized security (2021–2026). The results also show increased security complexity due to the integration of advanced technologies and secure architectures with the cloud such as decentralized security (e.g. federated learning also known as distributed AI models), AI driven cybersecurity, zero-trust architectures, privacy-preserving computation and advanced cryptography such as post-quantum cryptography. These technologies are among the most challenging emerging research areas, yet they are the most promising regarding cloud computing. Finally, as cybersecurity technologies evolve, security complexity of the cloud will continue to grow.

papers.title: Joint Optimizing Federated Learning and Unlearning over Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: In this paper, a communication and energy-efficient federated learning (FL) and unlearning (FU) co-designed framework is proposed. In the considered model, multiple edge devices collaboratively train a model. Users are allowed to quit the FL training and remove their data impacts on the trained model. Hence, an FU training is performed after the FL training. To reduce the energy and time consumption of FU, the users are grouped into multiple clusters such that the users in a group will retrain a deep learning model when the users in the group request to quit the FL training. The base station (BS) needs to determine the number of clusters, the users in each cluster, and the resource block (RB) allocated to each user, according to the probability that each user requests to quit the FL, data distribution, wireless channel conditions, and time and energy constraints. This problem is formulated as an optimization problem whose goal is to minimize the expected loss by determining the number of clusters, user cluster assignment, and RB allocations. This problem is challenging to solve since 1) the BS cannot predict which users will request data deletion in advance and 2) no explicit equation exists to capture the relationship between the number of clusters, user cluster assignment, and the expected FU loss. To solve the formulated problem, we first analyze the convergence rate of FU to build an explicit relationship among the FU training loss, the number of clusters, and the users in each cluster. Based on this relationship, the original problem is simplified to a mixed-integer optimization problem which can be divided into the user cluster assignment and the RB allocation optimization subproblems. These two problems are alternately solved by the designed Dinkelbach's method and the fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (Dinkelbach-FISTA) and the standard Hungarian algorithm. Simulation results show that our method improves classification accuracy by up to 11.1% and achieves up to 3× faster convergence compared to gradient-based and ISTA-based methods.

papers.title: FEdgeNAV: Edge-Based Federated Learning Framework for Wheel Odometry Fault Detection in Industrial AGV Fleet Navigation
papers.abstract: Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) rely on accurate wheel odometry for reliable navigation; however, wheel slip and varying terrain conditions introduce positioning errors that degrade navigation performance. This paper presents FEdgeNAV, a lightweight edge-based federated learning framework for collaborative wheel odometry fault detection in heterogeneous industrial environments. The proposed framework employs a lightweight 1D CNN-GRU model trained collaboratively across distributed edge clients using Federated Averaging (FedAvg), while keeping raw navigation data local by exchanging only model parameters. Wheel odometry faults are identified through residual analysis between the estimated and measured vehicle speeds. Experimental evaluation on the NavINST dataset demonstrated accurate vehicle-speed estimation and residual-based wheel-odometry fault detection across heterogeneous operating conditions. Furthermore, the proposed framework achieved computationally efficient inference on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, demonstrating its suitability for real-time deployment on resource-constrained edge platforms for industrial AGVs.

papers.title: Differential Privacy and Federated Learning Technologies in Privacy Protection for Medical Big Data
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of big data technology, the value of data in various industries has become increasingly prominent, but the problem of privacy leakage has also received more and more attention. How to protect user privacy while mining the value of data has become an important problem that urgently needs to be solved in the field of big data analysis. This paper reviews and summarizes research related to privacy-preserving big data analysis from three levels: the algorithm level, the framework level, and the application level. First, the application and optimization methods of differential privacy (DP) in deep learning model training are introduced, including key technologies such as the differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) framework, gradient clipping, and privacy budget optimization. Then, the problem of improving model efficiency under the federated learning (FL) framework is discussed, with a focus on communication efficiency optimization and personalized FL methods under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. Finally, taking medical big data as a typical scenario, the research status and challenges of privacy protection systems are discussed. At the end of the paper, the existing problems in current research and future development directions are also preliminarily prospected.

papers.title: A Co-Evolutionary Game-Theoretic and Deep Learning framework for adaptive intrusion detection in IoT networks
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of interconnected devices in the Internet of Things (IoT) has significantly increased the cyber-attack surface, exposing networks to complex and evolving threats. Conventional intrusion detection systems (IDSs), which rely on static signatures or non-adaptive models, often fail to address dynamic adversarial behaviors. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a Co-Evolutionary Game-Theoretic and Deep Learning (CDL) framework for adaptive intrusion detection in IoT environments. The proposed framework integrates a replicator-dynamics-based co-evolutionary game-theoretic model with a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM-Attention architecture to jointly capture adaptive attacker-defender interactions and spatiotemporal traffic features. The game-theoretic component employs payoff-driven utility updates to model evolving adversarial strategies and continuously refine optimal defense mechanisms, while the deep learning module extracts discriminative features for accurate intrusion classification. Furthermore, a federated learning extension is incorporated to investigate privacy-preserving collaborative intrusion detection across distributed IoT environments without requiring the sharing of raw data. Experimental evaluation on the CICIoT2023 dataset demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves a detection accuracy of 98.11%, a Macro-F1 score of approximately 0.67, and latency below 100 ms. The comparatively lower Macro-F1 score is primarily attributed to severe class imbalance and the presence of minority attack categories, which are inherently more challenging to classify despite the high overall detection accuracy. Furthermore, the observed increase in defender utility and reduction in attacker utility validate the effectiveness of the adaptive co-evolutionary strategy. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a robust, scalable, and adaptive intrusion detection solution for dynamic IoT environments, with potential applicability to distributed and privacy-preserving deployment scenarios.

papers.title: PQ-FL-IDS: A Post Quantum Safe Federated Edge Intrusion Detection Scheme underlying 6G
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables Intrusion Detection System (IDS) models to be trained across Sixth Generation (6G) edge nodes without transferring sensitive traffic records to a central server. However, the model updates exchanged during FL-based IDS (FL-IDS) training remain exposed to interception and harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks by quantum-capable adversaries. This paper presents PQ-FL-IDS, a post-quantum (PQ) FL-IDS scheme for 6G edge networks. It protects model-update exchange using a real, non-simulated Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM-512, NIST FIPS 203), the Advanced Encryption Standard in Galois/Counter Mode with a 256-bit key (AES-256-GCM), and per-round forward secrecy through ephemeral key pairs. Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) with Rényi DP accounting further bounds record-level leakage from local updates. In each round, clients train locally with calibrated DP noise, encrypt the model update, and send only the protected payload for server-side aggregation. We evaluate PQ-FL-IDS on ToN-IoT with a 1D-CNN and FedAvg, and on CICIoT2023 with MobileNetV2-1D and FedProx, under baseline, PQC-only, and PQC+DP settings. ML-KEM-512 with AES-256-GCM adds less than 0.003% computational overhead relative to per-round training time and at most 3.5 KB of payload expansion, with no accuracy loss, and remains stable from 2 to 5 clients. The privacy analysis shows predictable ε growth with the subsampling rate and characterizes the privacy-utility frontier: formal budgets of ε = 0.9-2.4 are obtained for σ = 0.8-1.1, with a utility cost that depends strongly on task complexity.

papers.title: Time to Protection in Federated Intrusion Detection on Jetson Orin Nano Clusters
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) allows IoT devices to improve a shared intrusion detector without exchanging raw data. A device, however, can only learn from attacks that reach it, and because federated detection is evaluated as a whole for the fleet of IoT devices or averaged over attack classes, it is not reported how long a device that has never observed an attack class remains exposed to it without protection. The aim of this paper is to measure that exposure window, round by round, and to determine how it depends on the share of the fleet that already holds the class. We deployed a federated system with nine clients on two Jetson Orin Nano clusters connected over a WAN. As the main dataset, we used N-BaIoT, which covers two devices that were never infected by the mirai attack. It was tested with one to seven attacked clients and validated on CWRU and PAMAP2 datasets. The results showed that new class arrival depends on the share of the fleet that already knows about it, reaching 0.827 on mirai after one round when trained from the start with mirai data on seven out of nine clients, and reaching protection thresholds after 4, 17, and 39 rounds for seven, three, and two of nine clients attacked, when the model was initially trained without knowledge of mirai. Our findings show that federation delivers recognition of an attack class quickly when much of the fleet already holds it, and slowly or not within our horizon when only a few devices have been hit, which is the case a defender is most concerned with.

papers.title: Federated Hybrid Deep Learning with Adaptive Nature-Inspired Optimization for Privacy-Preserving Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks
papers.abstract: We “Internet of Things (IoT)” networks has made this need even more pressing, with an ever-growing need to have trustworthy and privacy-preserving IDS systems that detect advanced cyberattacks without revealing sensitive network data. To tackle this issue, this work introduces a “Federated Hybrid Deep Learning with Adaptive Nature-Inspired Optimization (FHDL-ANIO)” framework, which combines “Federated Learning (FL)” with “Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization (APSO)”, “Adaptive Ant Colony Optimization (AACO)”, and Hybrid CNN–Attention–BiGRU architecture, to support distributed intrusion detection. To optimise features and hyperparameters, the system employs APSO and AACO, while federated learning trains a model independently of raw data. The UNSW-NB15 dataset is used to test the suggested model of 175341 training and 82332 testing samples with nine attack types. Results show that “the hybrid approach achieves the accuracy of 92.92%, precision of 93.67%, recall of 93.45%, F1 score of 93.56%, and ROC-AUC of 0.9827”. APSO then filters the feature space bringing this down from 194 to 114 features (41.24% reduction) reducing the computational complexity of the system, yet maintaining a high rate of detection. The outcomes demonstrate that the suggested architecture for implementing intelligent intrusion detection in dispersed IoT systems is accurate, scalable, effective, and privacy-preserving.

papers.title: AI-Based Multimodal Phishing Detection Using Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Phishing is one of the most common cybersecurity threats where attackers trick users through fake emails, websites, or links to steal sensitive information. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, phishing attacks are becoming more realistic and harder to detect using traditional methods. Earlier systems relied on blacklists, rules, and URL features, but recent research explores deep learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), and multimodal approaches. Explainability and privacy-aware techniques such as federated learning are also gaining importance. The increasing sophistication of phishing campaigns highlights the need for advanced detection frameworks that can analyze diverse information sources simultaneously. Mul-timodal systems leverage text, URLs, visual webpage content, and embedded scripts to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of suspicious activity. Large Language Mod-els further enhance semantic understanding, enabling detection of subtle manipulations in phishing messages. By combining multimodal analysis with explainable and privacy-preserving AI, researchers aim to build adaptive, transparent, and trustworthy solutions that can effectively counter evolving phishing threats in real-world cybersecurity environ-ments.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: Federated Learning for Early Cancer Detection: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Early detection of cancer remains one of the most effective strategies to reduce cancer mortality. Artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance existing cancer screening across modalities by improving testing performance (e.g., accuracy, sensitivity, specificity), reducing false positives and negatives, automating workflows, and enabling risk-based care. However, accurate, robust, generalizable AI requires large, diverse, well-annotated datasets that are difficult to centralize because of privacy regulations, institutional governance, and heterogeneous infrastructure. Federated learning (FL) addresses this constraint by training models across institutions without transferring patient data. Through secure aggregation and differential privacy, FL preserves confidentiality while enabling collaboration. Early studies in breast, lung, and cervical screening report that FL can approach centralized performance and improve cross-site generalization; however, most rely on simulated clients, few participating sites, and limited external validation, so these findings should be regarded as preliminary rather than established. Critically, FL is not a shortcut to rigorous results, and heterogeneous, variably curated data demand intensive cleaning and quality control, which are central barriers to reliable implementation. In this review, we synthesize the state of FL for early cancer detection across imaging, digital pathology, multi-omics, and clinical data; outline core FL concepts and privacy technologies; and summarize applications by cancer type. We critically examine regulatory, operational, and translational barriers that currently limit clinical adoption. Finally, we propose a practical roadmap, which is centered on multimodal and longitudinal FL, foundation-model-enabled adaptation, prospective evaluation within clinical workflows, and equitable participation of community and low-resource sites, to advance privacy-preserving, generalizable AI for population-scale cancer screening.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for precision nephrology: current evidence to clinical translation and future prospects
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across nephrology, with potential applications spanning disease prediction, diagnosis, treatment optimisation, and clinical decision support. However, reported model performance varies substantially across clinical domains, and high predictive performance does not necessarily demonstrate clinical utility or readiness for deployment. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the applications of AI in nephrology and critically evaluates the methodological maturity, validation, interpretability, fairness, and translational readiness of AI systems across major nephrology domains. Methods A structured literature search of PubMed was conducted using terms related to AI and nephrology, with the primary eligibility period restricted to studies published from 2020 to 2025. The search strategy incorporated artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, natural language processing, large language models, generative AI, computer vision, reinforcement learning, federated learning, and related terms, together with nephrology and kidney-disease terms. Title/abstract and full-text screening were performed independently by the first and second authors, with disagreements resolved by the third author. Two foundational pre-2020 studies identified through citation chaining were retained because of their importance to the subsequent development of AI applications in nephrology. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively according to study design, validation, predictive performance, interpretability, fairness, prospective evaluation, and translational readiness. Results AI applications were identified across acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, nephropathology, kidney transplantation, haemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, large language models, reinforcement learning, and federated learning. Across these domains, many models demonstrated promising discrimination, but evidence maturity varied considerably. External validation was present for some applications, whereas prospective evaluation and evidence of clinical utility remained limited. The literature also highlighted challenges related to calibration, generalizability, interpretability, algorithmic fairness, data governance, and integration into clinical workflows. Large language models and federated learning represent emerging areas, but nephrology-specific evidence remains comparatively limited. Conclusions AI has substantial potential to support precision nephrology, but technical performance should not be equated with clinical effectiveness or deployment readiness. Future research should prioritize external and prospective validation, assessment of clinical utility and patient outcomes, transparent reporting, fairness, regulatory oversight, and effective human–AI integration.

papers.title: Less Federation, More Personalization: One-Shot Multi-View Clustering for Federated Fall Detection
papers.abstract: Federated learning is a natural fit for sensor-based fall detection, where data are privacy-sensitive and highly non-IID across subjects. A two-stage framework is proposed in which each client first learns label-free representations using FMMVCC, a multi-view clustering encoder that combines reconstruction, cross-view consistency, contrastive learning, and prototype-based objectives. The resulting encoders are then aggregated via a single round of FedAvg into a shared frozen feature extractor, decoupling representation learning from downstream classification. Experiments are conducted on the FallTL dataset, a wearable sensing benchmark evaluated under both binary (Fall/ADL) and 16-class (activity × Fall/ADL) granularities. Results show that FMMVCC achieves strong representation quality, outperforming four self-supervised baselines in binary classification (84.15% ACC) and providing competitive performance in the fine-grained setting. On top of these representations, the personalized closed-form classifier consistently outperforms FedAvg, FedProx, and shared analytic baselines by 8-13pp, and matches or exceeds FedProto in the 16-class setting while requiring no communication during inference. Finally, cross-client alignment metrics are shown to be weak predictors of downstream performance, while class-separability measures correlate more reliably with accuracy.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Multimodal Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Video Anomaly Detection (VAD) has emerged as a critical research area in intelligent surveillance, public safety, industrial monitoring, and smart city applications. Traditional supervised approaches rely on frame-level annotations, which are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and expensive to obtain, thereby limiting their scalability in large-scale surveillance systems. Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection (WSVAD) addresses this challenge by utilizing only video-level labels while enabling effective temporal anomaly localization. In recent years, multimodal learning has significantly improved detection performance by integrating complementary information from visual, audio, and semantic modalities. This paper presents a comprehensive review of multimodal WSVAD techniques, emphasizing recent advancements in Multiple Instance Learning (MIL), vision-language models, audio-visual learning, knowledge transfer, and semantic alignment strategies. Representative methods are systematically analyzed and compared with respect to their methodologies, benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, strengths, and limitations. Furthermore, major research challenges, including modality imbalance, limited multimodal datasets, computational complexity, and domain generalization, are discussed. Finally, emerging research directions involving foundation models, multimodal large language models (MLLMs), self-supervised learning, federated learning, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) are highlighted to support the development of scalable, robust, and interpretable anomaly detection systems.

papers.title: Impact of DDoS Attacks and Mitigation Strategies in Cloud Applications
papers.abstract: This resource presents the research findings and literature review for the paper titled "Impact of DDoS Attacks and Mitigation Strategies in Cloud Applications" by Rabin Kumar Chhatkuli (2026). It examines the evolving landscape of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks in cloud environments and evaluates traditional, AI-driven, and hybrid mitigation approaches. The study highlights CNN-LSTM-based detection, federated learning, and blockchain-assisted security, while discussing challenges related to detection accuracy, scalability, latency, and ethical AI governance. It aims to contribute to the development of adaptive, transparent, and resilient security frameworks for next-generation cloud applications. Citation: Rabin Kumar, C. (2026). papers.title: An IoMT-Based Circadian-Mood Digital Twin for Pre-Symptomatic Mental Health Prediction via Federated Learning and Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Continuous mental health monitoring using wearable sensors in the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) offers a paradigm shift toward pre-symptomatic clinical intervention. However, prevailing predictive models rely on empirical correlation rather than physiological dynamics and face severe data privacy obstacles under healthcare regulations. This paper presents a biologically grounded, privacy-preserving IoMT framework that models patient-specific sleep homeostatic pressure (S) and endogenous circadian drive (C) via the Two-Process Model to construct an individualised Circadian-Mood Digital Twin. Features extracted from 30-day longitudinal records across 10 virtual patients—encompassing heart rate variability, sleep-stage architecture, voice spectral envelopes (13 Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients), and ambient photic exposure—are applied to forecast depressive (PHQ-9) and anxiety (GAD-7) trajectories over 24-h, 36-h, and 48-h horizons. Decentralised model training is executed across five virtual clinical nodes using Federated Averaging (FedAvg) combined with L2 gradient clipping and Gaussian Differential Privacy (DP). Empirical evaluation demonstrates a predictive Mean Absolute Error of 7.891 points for PHQ-9 and 6.071 points for GAD-7 at a 24-h horizon. The early warning scoring mechanism attained an episode detection sensitivity of 90.0% with an average clinical lead time of 71.1 h, while threshold tuning reduced hourly false alarms to 7.2%. Global convergence occurred within 10 communication rounds under a cumulative privacy budget of ε ≈ 96.1. The results validate the feasibility of combining computational chronobiology with privacy-preserving distributed learning for proactive psychiatric monitoring.

papers.title: RAFO-V2: Analysis and Results Verification Materials for Selective Resilience-Aware Federated Energy Forecasting
papers.abstract: This repository provides supporting software, experimental manifests, statistical analysis scripts, and derived results associated with the study "Selective Resilience-Aware Federated Optimization for Energy Forecasting under Communication and Cyber Stress". The research investigates selective resilience-aware federated optimisation (RAFO-V2) for electricity-load forecasting under communication impairments and cyber-related disturbances. The experimental campaign comprises 500 runs across two publicly available electricity datasets (UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014 and Ausgrid), three federated optimisation algorithms (FedAvg, FedProx, and SCAFFOLD), and multiple protection policies and disturbance conditions. The deposited materials document the experimental campaign and support independent inspection and verification of the reported statistical and protection-activation results. The principal reported results include 120 matched comparisons between static federated learning and the main RAFO-V2 supervisor, with 100 improvements, 20 ties, and no deteriorations. The main supervisory policy achieves a mean protection duty cycle of approximately 26.31% and a mean normalised intervention intensity of 9.87%. The statistical analysis uses paired comparisons, bootstrap confidence intervals, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Holm correction for multiple comparisons. The repository is intended to facilitate verification of the reported results and provide a foundation for further research into selective resilience mechanisms in federated energy forecasting. Reproducibility scope: The available analysis materials support verification of the consolidated results. Full end-to-end reproduction of model training requires the original training implementation, environment specifications, and dataset preparation procedures. These capabilities should not be assumed unless they are explicitly included in the published release. The original public datasets are not redistributed; they should be obtained from their respective providers. Author: Manuel J. C. S. Reis Institution: University of Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro (UTAD), Portugal; IEETA, University of Aveiro, Portugal.

papers.title: An IoT-Based Healthcare Monitoring and Surveillance Framework for People with Special Needs
papers.abstract: People with special needs, such as frail older adults and people living with Parkinson’s disease (PD), heart-rhythm disorders or dementia, are often alone when a critical event happens. We present IoT-CARES, a four-layer Internet of Things (IoT) framework with one lightweight edge pipeline for five services: fall detection, activity monitoring of adults aged 70+, freezing-of-gait (FoG) detection, single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) arrhythmia monitoring and camera-free cognitive-health surveillance. A dual-view ensemble (a fixed average of gradient-boosted trees on physiological descriptors and a linear model on random-convolution features) runs without a deep-learning runtime. A subject-level conformal calibration bounds a new person’s false-alarm rate by a carer-chosen budget with probability ≥90%, provided that new and calibration people are exchangeable, and federated learning trains shared models without moving raw data. On five open datasets (438 people), evaluated on held-out people, the framework reached an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.9998 for simulated falls and 0.908 for FoG, and a macro-F1 of 0.778 for activity; federated training matched centralised training. Personalisation helped only when the onboarding data contained the target events: five labelled ECG minutes raised arrhythmia macro-F1 from 0.667 (best global model) to 0.932, whereas fine-tuning on routine activity lowered activity macro-F1 (0.766 to 0.683) unless only the output layer was adapted (0.795). Conformal calibration kept 16 of 17 young volunteers (94.1%; 95% confidence interval 71.3–99.9%) free of false fall alarms during their activity protocol while detecting 94.6% of simulated falls (window-optimal threshold: 76.5% free of false alarms), and kept 9 of 10 people with PD within four false cues per hour; with so few people, these estimates are imprecise. In free-living data of 18 adults aged 70–95 years, a fall threshold calibrated on the volunteers raised no false alarms in 12.6 h, but calibration on the older adults’ own data detected more of the volunteers’ simulated falls (99.1% vs. 92.1%). Ambient sensors detected dementia (AUROC 0.962) but not reliably mild cognitive impairment (0.523). Inference took ≤ 24.3 ms per window on one processor core, and data leaving the home fell 219–759-fold.

papers.title: FrozenSFL: Model-Frozen Split Federated Learning for Resource-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning over Heterogeneous Edge Devices
papers.abstract: Collaborative fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) at the network edge enables privacy-preserving and personalized generative intelligence, but is constrained by the limited memory and compute resources of edge devices. Traditional approaches, such as split federated learning (SFL), partition models between devices and a server, requiring iterative exchanges of activations/gradients while the server manages multiple submodels. This leads to substantial communication overhead, high activation storage costs, and severe server-side memory pressure when scaling to massive heterogeneous devices. In this paper, we propose FrozenSFL, a resource-efficient SFL framework for collaborative fine-tuning of LLMs across heterogeneous edge devices. At its core, FrozenSFL strictly freezes device-side submodels to eliminate both deviceside backpropagation and server-to-device gradient transmission, thereby removing on-device activation storage requirements and downlink communication overhead. Building upon this design, we improve the framework in two aspects. First, we design a layerwise LoRA aggregation strategy to handle structural heterogeneity introduced by device-specific model partitioning and enable efficient server-side updates. Second, we introduce a server-side feature caching mechanism that reuses invariant features, allowing subsequent training epochs to proceed offline and reducing redundant computation and communication. We implement the FrozenSFL system as an asynchronous multi-threaded pipeline, which serves as our real-world testbed for evaluation. On the device side, forward computation and data transmission are decoupled via a producer-consumer mechanism. On the server side, a first-in-first-out scheduling strategy serializes fine-tuning tasks across devices. A hybrid memory-disk streaming mechanism further buffers incoming data and ensures stable training under network variability. Extensive evaluations with representative models, including BERT-Base (0.11B), ViT-Large (0.3B), and LLaMA-2-7B (7B), validate the effectiveness of FrozenSFL. In particular, for LLaMA-2-7B, FrozenSFL can reduce device/server VRAM footprint by up to 14%/82.7% with only 1% accuracy loss, while achieving up to 6.7× fine-tuning speedup.

papers.title: H-PRISM: Hilbert parameter representation for inspection of structural malice for stealthy poisoning detection in medical federated learning
Demo: Multimodal Stress Monitoring with Split Federated Fine-Tuning on Mobile Devices
papers.abstract: We present an end-to-end mobile system for proactive stress monitoring from wearable signals. The framework is supported by an extensible split federated learning system that enables on-device LoRA fine-tuning of large language models. By analyzing physiological data, the application distinguishes emotional states, summarizes recent trends, and provides brief, actionable suggestions. Upon detecting a negative emotional state, the paired smartwatch or smartphone proactively delivers notifications to users to encourage mindfulness. The on-site demonstration will showcase real-time sensing-inference on smartwatch-phone pairs, alongside a recorded split federated learning process that continuously learns from user private data. Our code has been open-sourced at: https://github.com/HKU-WILL-Lab/Multimodal-Stress-Monitoring-with-Split-Federated-Fine-Tuning-on-Mobile-Devices.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Adversarial Attacks on IoT Networks: Defending Intelligent Systems Against AI-Driven Cyber Threats
papers.abstract: The expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) have transformed modern cybersecurity. While AI enables intelligent threat detection, predictive analytics, automated incident response, and adaptive security mechanisms, it also introduces new vulnerabilities that can be exploited by sophisticated adversaries. AI-enabled cyberattacks, adversarial machine learning, data poisoning, evasion attacks, model manipulation, and intelligent attack automation pose significant challenges to the security, reliability, and trustworthiness of interconnected IoT environments. This book provides a comprehensive exploration of AI-driven cybersecurity and adversarial threats affecting IoT networks. It presents the fundamental concepts of AI-based cybersecurity, adversarial machine learning models, attack taxonomies, and intelligent intrusion detection systems. The chapters examine adversarial attacks against AI-powered security mechanisms, AI-assisted malware, intelligent attack automation, and the role of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in improving transparency and trust in cybersecurity decisions. The book further explores defensive adversarial machine learning techniques, privacy-preserving AI, trustworthy intelligent systems, autonomous cyber defense frameworks, intelligent threat intelligence, digital twins, and cyber resilience. It discusses emerging approaches such as adversarial training, robust optimization, federated learning, blockchain-assisted security, Zero Trust Architecture, autonomous threat hunting, and self-healing networks. Particular emphasis is placed on developing resilient, explainable, privacy-aware, and adaptive security mechanisms capable of addressing evolving cyber threats in heterogeneous and resource-constrained IoT environments. By connecting foundational concepts with defensive strategies, emerging technologies, and future research directions, this book offers valuable insights into the challenges and opportunities associated with securing AI-enabled IoT infrastructures. It is intended for undergraduate and postgraduate students, research scholars, academicians, cybersecurity professionals, AI researchers, network engineers, and industry practitioners interested in intelligent cybersecurity and adversarial machine learning. Ultimately, this book aims to support research, education, and professional practice in building secure, robust, and trustworthy IoT ecosystems capable of resisting increasingly sophisticated AI-driven cyber threats.
