papers.title: AI-powered framework for advancing 5G and 6G wireless communication
papers.abstract: A shift to 5G to 6G networks would provide better connectivity, transmission capacity, security, and latency, but there are still challenges such as dynamic resource allocation, energy consumption, network optimisation, and cybersecurity issues. This research presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-based approach to enhance the accuracy, efficiency and security of 5G and future 6G wireless networks. Adaptive spectrum and resource allocation is done using deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and AI traffic forecasting and dynamic beamforming helps reduce latency, boost throughput and ensure quality of service (QoS). Federated learning (FL) trains models at the distributed sites while minimizing the amount of raw data transmission, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) create representative samples of data for network and cybersecurity analysis. The anomaly detection feature powered by AI, along with the blockchain-based authentication, helps enhance access control and threat detection. The framework was tested and analyzed in a simulation environment built in Python and in comparison to traditional optimization. It performed an F1-score of 0.94, versus 0.82; AUC–ROC of 0.96, versus 0.86; and resource-allocation success rate (91% versus 75%). These results represent the relative increases of 14.6%, 11.6% and 21.3%. The results suggest that AI-driven coordinated optimisation could lead to a more adaptive management of resources, threat detection, and efficient operation of networks compared with traditional methods, paving the way for intelligence, security and energy-efficient 6G communication systems.
papers.venue: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)

papers.title: FED DERM-SLA INVESTIGATING CONFLICT-AWARE SEMANTIC KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER FOR FEDERATED SKIN LESION CLASSIFICATION UNDER LABEL-SPACE AND DOMAIN HETEROGENEITY
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative medical image analysis while keeping patient images decentralized. However, heterogeneity in diagnostic label spaces and image distributions presents substantial challenges for effective knowledge sharing across participating institutions. In particular, transferring class-level semantic information between clients may introduce negative transfer when local feature representations are insufficiently compatible. This study investigates Fed Derm-SLA, a federated skin lesion classification framework integrating a shared ResNet-18 feature encoder, client-specific classification heads, semantic class prototypes, and similarity-dependent knowledge transfer. Three controlled configurations are examined: federated learning without semantic transfer (A0), ungated semantic transfer (A1), and similarity-gated semantic transfer (A2). Experiments are conducted using 10,015 HAM10000 dermoscopic images partitioned into four heterogeneous clients with lesion-disjoint training, validation, and testing sets. Model performance is assessed across three matched random seeds and further evaluated using 1,077 curated ISIC 2019 images. On the internal test set, A0, A1, and A2 achieve mean macro-F1 scores of 0.6682, 0.6590, and 0.6665, respectively. Gated transfer consistently improves internal macro-F1 relative to ungated transfer across all three seeds, although it does not exceed the no-transfer baseline. External macro-F1 decreases to 0.3698, 0.3658, and 0.3625, respectively, indicating substantial generalization challenges. Transfer diagnostics also indicate that the similarity gate accepts all observed candidate transfers, providing little evidence for effective conflict rejection. These results suggest that semantic transfer weighing alone does not necessarily lead to better classification or cross-dataset generalization in the heterogeneous federated setting. The study offers a controlled empirical evaluation of prototype-based transfer and points out significant limitations for the design of more discriminative conflict-aware federated learning mechanisms.

papers.title: FROM INTELLIGENT SYSTEMS TO TRUSTWORTHY AGENTS: A COMPREHENSIVE SURVEY OF AGENTIC AI IN SMART HEALTHCARE
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming Smart Healthcare Systems (SHS) from conventional data-driven infrastructures into intelligent ecosystems capable of autonomous perception, reasoning, collaboration, adaptation, and clinical decision support. The emergence of Agentic AI represents a significant transition toward autonomous healthcare intelligence, in which AI agents can dynamically perceive clinical contexts, plan and execute tasks, interact with heterogeneous medical resources, collaborate with other agents, and continuously adapt to changing healthcare conditions. Despite this potential, the adoption of Agentic AI in healthcare remains constrained by critical concerns involving patient privacy, cyber security, explainability, reliability, accountability, trust, and safe continual learning. This survey reviews recent advances in trustworthy Agentic AI for healthcare, focusing on Federated Learning, Zero Trust Security, Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning, and Privacy-Preserving Intelligence. It analyzes how these technologies support secure collaboration, protect sensitive medical data, enhance interpretability, and enable continuous learning in distributed healthcare environments. The paper also highlights key limitations in existing approaches, particularly the absence of unified frameworks that jointly address autonomy, security, privacy, and trust. Finally, it outlines open research challenges and future directions toward building reliable and explainable Agentic AI systems for Smart Healthcare.

papers.title: A GWO-OPTIMIZED HETEROGENEOUS FEDERATED LEARNING FRAMEWORK WITH WEIGHTED SOFT VOTING FOR CYBERSECURITY CLASSIFICATION
papers.abstract: This study proposes a heterogeneous federated learning framework for cybersecurity classification by integrating Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM with the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and weighted soft voting. The CICIDS2017 and TON_IoT datasets were integrated into a unified dataset containing 511,043 samples, 96 features, and 11 classes, using a stratified 70:30 training–testing split. GWO was employed to optimize both local model hyperparameters and aggregation weights. The centralized XGBoost baseline achieved 96.95% accuracy, while the Baseline Federated Model achieved 99.48%. The Proposed GWO-Optimized Federated Model achieved 99.51% accuracy and an F1-score of 99.53%. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining heterogeneous federated learning, GWO optimization, and weighted decision-level aggregation for multiclass cybersecurity classification.

papers.title: NEURO-SYMBOLIC FEDERATED INTELLIGENCE FOR SELF-HEALING 6G NETWORKS USING INTEGRATED SENSING AND COMMUNICATION
papers.abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to operate as highly heterogeneous, distributed, and autonomous infrastructures in which communication, sensing, computing, and intelligence are tightly integrated. Such networks must continuously adapt to dynamic radio environments, hardware degradation, mobility, malicious interference, traffic fluctuations, and service-level disruptions while satisfying stringent latency, reliability, energy, and privacy requirements. Conventional artificial-intelligence-based network management approaches, although effective for pattern recognition and prediction, remain limited by their dependence on centralized data, weak interpretability, susceptibility to distribution shifts, and inability to explicitly enforce operational constraints. Conversely, rule-based self-healing systems provide interpretability and deterministic control but have limited adaptability to previously unseen faults. This paper proposes Neuro-Symbolic Federated Intelligence for Self-Healing 6G Networks using Integrated Sensing and Communication (NS-FedHeal-ISAC), a privacy-preserving closed-loop architecture that combines neural fault perception, federated learning, symbolic reasoning, and ISAC-derived environmental awareness. The proposed framework transforms distributed communication and sensing observations into a unified network-state representation, learns fault and degradation patterns collaboratively without transferring raw telemetry, and employs a symbolic knowledge plane to reason over fault dependencies, service intents, operational policies, and candidate healing actions. A constrained action-selection mechanism then selects the safest recovery operation, while post-healing observations are fed back into the federated learning process for continual adaptation. A formal optimization model is developed to jointly minimize service disruption, healing latency, communication overhead, energy consumption, and policy violations. The paper further introduces a hierarchical knowledge graph for representing network entities, faults, causal dependencies, service-level objectives, and recovery actions; a heterogeneity-aware federated optimization mechanism; and a risk-aware neuro-symbolic healing policy. The proposed architecture is evaluated through a reproducible simulation methodology against centralized deep learning, conventional federated learning, rule-based healing, deep reinforcement learning, and federated learning without symbolic reasoning. Evaluation dimensions include fault-detection F1 score, root-cause accuracy, healing success rate, mean time to recovery, service-level agreement violation, communication overhead, energy cost, explanation fidelity, robustness under non-IID data, and resilience against malicious clients. The central hypothesis is that combining learned representations with explicit symbolic constraints and distributed intelligence can achieve a more reliable and explainable self-healing mechanism than purely neural or purely rule-based approaches. The resulting framework provides a pathway toward trustworthy, privacy-aware, and context-aware zero-touch network automation for future 6G systems.

papers.title: Resource-Aware and Energy-Efficient Machine Learning for Distributed Edge-Cloud Systems: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.abstract: The vast proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices with constrained resources led to the adoption of distributed edge-cloud computing systems.Machine learning (ML) has become an important source for deploying intelligent services across many environments.But deploying and training ML models in resource-constrained edge devices presents significant challenges, including limited computational capability, restricted memory, energy constraints, and communication overhead.In this work a systematic survey of latest research in the design and deployment of resource-aware and energy-efficient machine learning models in distributed edge-cloud systems are presented.The survey categorizes existing approaches into model optimization methods, including pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, and lightweight architecture design, as well as system-level strategies such as federated learning, task offloading, and collaborative inference.Furthermore, the paper analyses trade-offs among accuracy, latency, energy consumption, and communication cost, highlighting the impact of these techniques on real-world deployments.Recent advancements in adaptive and contextaware learning frameworks are also examined, emphasizing their role in dynamic resource management.In addition, open challenges such as heterogeneity of edge devices, scalability, privacy preservation, and robustness are critically discussed.Finally, the paper identifies limitations and future scope to lead future research directions aimed at enabling sustainable and scalable edge intelligence.
papers.venue: International Journal of Computer Networks And Applications

papers.title: Современные методы федеративного обучения: сравнительный анализ эффективности и устойчивости
papers.abstract: This article examines methods and algorithms used in the Federated Learning model and provides a comparative analysis under conditions of heterogeneous data during training. Particular attention is paid to algorithms and their extensions, including FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedNova, FedOpt, FLTrust, and LoRA-FL. The study employs the following evaluation metrics: training accuracy, convergence speed, resistance to Byzantine attacks, and performance efficiency under heterogeneous data conditions. The results of the study identify the advantages of the considered algorithms and outline promising directions for the further development of federated learning models.
papers.venue: Journal of the Ural Federal district Information security

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Healthcare Cybersecurity: A Comprehensive Survey of Threat Detection and Defense Mechanisms
papers.abstract: The increasing digitalization of healthcare systems has improved patient care, data management, and clinical decision-making, but it has also expanded the cybersecurity threat landscape. Healthcare organizations face growing risks from ransomware, phishing, malware, insider threats, supply-chain attacks, and vulnerabilities in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices. These threats can compromise sensitive patient information, disrupt essential services, and affect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of healthcare data. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers promising capabilities for strengthening healthcare cybersecurity through intelligent threat detection, behavioral analysis, anomaly identification, and automated response. This survey examines major cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities in healthcare environments and reviews AI-based techniques, including machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, for identifying suspicious activities and potential attacks. It also discusses AI-integrated healthcare security architectures, cloud security, zero-trust principles, and privacy-preserving techniques such as homomorphic encryption, differential privacy, secure multiparty computation, and federated learning. Furthermore, the survey highlights challenges related to legacy systems, data privacy, access control, and secure deployment. This review provides an overview of AI-enabled detection and defense mechanisms for developing more secure, reliable, and privacy-preserving healthcare infrastructures.
papers.venue: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)

papers.title: Attention-Guided Sparse Aggregation and Hetero GeneityAware Optimization for Federated Wireless Traffic Prediction
papers.abstract: In cellular networks, wireless traffic forecasting is essential for proactive communication system adaptation. Wireless traffic prediction at the edge using Federated Learning (FL) has garnered a lot of attention due to its improved privacy protection and exemption from raw data transmission. However, existing FL-based traffic prediction methods still require substantial gradient exchange between local customers and a central server, and it remains unclear how to model the spatial dependencies among local customers within the FL architecture. To address this, we propose an FL framework, built on a Distributed Autonomous Network (DAN) architecture for 6G wireless communication, that proceeds through four stages, local modelling, gradient clipping and compression, path-level accumulation, and global optimization, to minimize communication load while maintaining forecasting accuracy. At each customer, an L2-norm gradient clipping step is followed by Top-K sparsification and 1-bit quantization to substantially shrink the size of the uploaded gradients. To offset the information lost through this compression, a Path Attention Aggregation Module learns customerspecific attention weights from each customer's upload trajectory, combining gradient-stability indicators with local performance measures, so that consistent, high-quality updates are weighted more heavily during aggregation; three customized aggregation strategies, all-correlated, δ-threshold, and krelevant, further use gradient correlation to capture the spatial interdependence among customers. A Heterogeneity-Aware Adaptive Optimizer, built on Adam, additionally tunes each customer's learning rate, momentum, and weight-decay settings to its own traffic characteristics and enforces cross-round consistency, mitigating the effects of non-IID data across customers.

papers.title: Privacy-aware federated learning for pneumonia detection in chest X-Ray images using MobileNetV2
papers.abstract: Pneumonia is the main cause of morbidity and mortality on the planet, and correct diagnosis based on chest radiographs is vital for timely intervention. Nonetheless, medical imaging deep learning models have commonly been limited by strict privacy policies that do not allow the central aggregation of sensitive patient information. This paper presents a privacy-preserving federated learning (FL) Python framework for pneumonia detection in the Kaggle Chest X-Ray dataset that seeks to address data governance, institutional autonomy, and non-IID data heterogeneity issues. The lightweight MobileNetV2 network was initialized with ImageNet weights and executed on four simulated hospital clients in the Flower (FLWR) framework. All clients had two epochs of local training per round, and all knowledge was synchronized through the Federated Averaging (FedAvg) algorithm. The data were divided according to a Dirichlet non-IID distribution to simulate realistic cross-hospital variations. The results of the global model over ten communication rounds reached 0.9924 accuracy, 0.9949 F1-score, and 0.9998 AUC, which indicates convergence and resistance to non-homogeneous client distributions. The findings validate the hypothesis that federated learning can perform diagnostic tasks as well as centralized training while maintaining privacy and minimizing patients' computational requirements. The research provides an experimentally verified FL pipeline that can be applied to low-resource clinical environments and provides a basis for the future integration of differential privacy, secure anonymization, and multi-task medical imaging.

papers.title: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
papers.abstract: Abstract Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations.

papers.title: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
papers.abstract: Abstract Although machine learning has transformed protein structure prediction of folded protein ground states with remarkable accuracy, intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse and dynamical structural ensembles that are predicted with low confidence by algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold. We present a machine learning method, IDPForge ( I ntrinsically D isordered P rotein, FO lded and disordered R egion GE nerator), that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP ensembles and IDR ensembles that maintains the folded domains. IDPForge does not require sequence-specific training, back transformations from coarse-grained representations, nor ensemble reweighting. The created IDP/IDR conformational ensembles show good agreement with both NMR and SAXS solution experimental data, and options for biasing with experimental restraints are available if desired. IDPForge with these diverse capabilities facilitates integrative and structural studies for proteins that contain intrinsic disorder, and is available as an open source resource for general use.

papers.title: A motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification
papers.abstract: Early identification of scoliosis is important for timely clinical intervention. However, conventional static screening methods rely on subjective assessments, resulting in limited accuracy and insufficient continuity. Here, we propose a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification. We engineer a highly anisotropic mesh with orderly aligned conductive fibers, enabling the motion sensors to precisely perceive motion amplitude and direction. The suit integrates motion sensors positioned at symmetrical body locations to quantify 3D spinal motions bz capturing skin-surface deformation amplitude and direction. We achieve dynamic scoliosis identification through machine learning-powered evaluation of spinal kinematic symmetry. We test performance on a multi-center cohort comprising four hospitals and one school-based screening program, demonstrating 92.63%, 71.05%, and 82.76% accuracy for scoliosis detection, curvature degree quantification, and curvature location identification, respectively. This radiation-free alternative has the potential to support longitudinal follow-up and reduce repeat radiographs in scoliosis management. Early detection of scoliosis is critical for timely intervention, but current screening lacks accuracy. Here the authors develop a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for accurate, intelligent scoliosis identification.

papers.title: Performance of artificial intelligence-assisted cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus testing for cervical cancer screening
papers.abstract: Evidence comparing cervical cancer screening strategies that combine artificial intelligence-assisted liquid-based cytology (AI-LBC) and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing in large-scale populations is limited. This study includes 284,002 women who underwent AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping in community-based screening in Wuhan, China. We evaluate the performance of nine hypothesized screening strategies in detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and their colposcopy referral rates. After correcting for verification bias, HR-HPV testing alone (Strategy 4) demonstrates higher sensitivity (94.93% vs. 83.88%) and a higher Youden’s index (0.864 vs. 0.789) than AI-LBC alone (Strategy 1), but requires a higher referral rate (9.05% vs. 5.49%). Among the triage-based strategies, Strategy 3 (AI-LBC with reflex HR-HPV) achieves a sensitivity of 82.90%, a referral rate of 2.67%, and a Youden’s index of 0.807. HR-HPV genotyping with reflex AI-LBC (Strategy 7) demonstrates a sensitivity of 92.68%, a Youden’s index of 0.899, and a referral rate of 3.34%. Co-testing of AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping (Strategy 9) achieves the highest Youden’s index (0.932), with a sensitivity of 96.37% and a referral rate of 3.70%. These findings suggest that AI-LBC performs well as a standalone screening method, triage tool, or a component a co-testing strategy in cervical cancer screening. When HR-HPV genotyping is available, Strategy 7 or Strategy 9 may be considered, depending on the trade-off between detection performance and referral burden. The authors prove AI-assisted cytology effective for cervical cancer screening. When combined with HPV testing, it detects more precancerous lesions and maintains low referral rates.

papers.title: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis
papers.abstract: It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

papers.title: Sequence Display generates large-scale sequence–activity datasets for reprogramming SlugCas9 toward difficult-to-access PAMs
papers.abstract: Protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirements constrain the targeting scope of CRISPR-Cas9 systems and limit genome editing applications that require precise nuclease positioning. Although broad-PAM and near-PAMless Cas9 variants have expanded the editable genome, robust targeting across certain PAM families remains difficult, particularly at NNAN PAMs. Here, we apply Sequence Display to generate multiplexed, large-scale sequence–activity datasets for Staphylococcus lugdunensis Cas9 (SlugCas9) across the NNAN PAM family, including NNAA, NNAT, NNAC and NNAG. These datasets quantitatively resolve how individual and combinatorial mutations reshape nuclease activity across distinct PAM contexts. By integrating Sequence Display-derived datasets with protein language models, we construct fine-grained activity landscapes and identify SlugCas9 variants with enhanced and broadened activity across NNAN PAMs. The resulting variants reprogram PAM recognition beyond the native G-compatible landscape of SlugCas9 and enable improved base editing at selected endogenous NNAN-constrained sites in cultured mammalian cells, including disease-relevant sites in APOC3 and PCSK9. Together, our results establish a strategy for reprogramming PAM preference in compact Cas9 nucleases and highlight Sequence Display as a general platform for evolving genome editors toward specific and difficult-to-access PAM spaces. Compact CRISPR-Cas9 enzymes are easier to deliver but recognize few targets. Here, authors use Sequence Display to generate large-scale SlugCas9 sequence–activity datasets and apply protein language models to engineer variants that recognize difficult NNAN PAMs and edit selected human genomic sites.

papers.title: Liquid-metal physical unclonable functions resistant to both physical and digital cloning
papers.abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) leverage device-specific randomness for hardware security, yet their static, persistently accessible responses allow attackers to collect sufficient data for digital cloning. We present a liquid-metal PUF (LM-PUF) that integrates physical unclonability with material-driven resistance to digital attacks. Randomly mixed, visually indistinguishable LM particles form thermally unique microstructures, ensuring physical unclonability. Digital protection arises from two concealment mechanisms: time-limited accessibility restricts meaningful data collection, while decoy obscuration prevents reliable key identification. At equilibrium, the device remains cryptographically silent, but heating through a transient non-equilibrium window reveals thermal patterns convertible to cryptographic keys. Outside the predefined temperature range, misleading thermal patterns conceal the authentic key among decoys. LM-PUF supports scalable patterning, demonstrated in secure labels and QR codes, highlighting its potential for secure supply chains and physical unclonable authentication. Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) secure hardware identity but can be digitally cloned by machine-learning attacks. Here, authors report a liquid-metal PUF whose thermal keys appear only briefly during heating and are hidden among decoys, resisting both physical and digital cloning.

papers.title: Characterizing Recoverable Expert-Utilization Signatures in Fine-Tuned Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
papers.abstract: As Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models are increasingly deployed in distributed environments, from federated learning to edge-cloud systems, their architecture harbors an underexplored landscape of security vulnerabilities. Moving beyond textual analysis, we uncover structural memorization: a novel vulnerability where a fine-tuned model memorizes not only its training data but also the internal pathway used to process it, creating a characteristic routing fingerprint unique to the training process. We provide comprehensive empirical evidence that structural memorization emerges consistently even from a few samples, and that its intensity is directly influenced by the choice of trainable modules. We show that these memorized expert pathways can be stealthily recovered through the model's unconditional generation, using only routing and output logits, with no knowledge of the fine-tuning data or procedure. In distributed deployments, this vulnerability is amplified as routing information is exposed at multiple trust boundaries, including federated aggregation points, edge-cloud interfaces, and multi-tenant monitoring systems. Recovery exposes a critical blind spot: traditional membership inference metrics, viewed through the lens of expert routing, fail to identify memorized data corresponding to these structural pathways. To close this gap, we devise composite metrics combining reference model tail likelihood with complexity-aware normalization, significantly improving detection of memorized routing structures. This enables adversaries to pinpoint critical experts shaped by fine-tuning, whether dominant or dormant, and execute targeted attacks such as router manipulation or backdoor injection in realistic distributed settings where attackers lack training data but can observe routing patterns across system components.

papers.title: FedMaJ: Ordinal Meta-Aggregation for Federated Learning Using Majority-Judgment Voting
papers.abstract: Federated learning traditionally relies on a fixed aggregation rule despite shifting client state and wireless dynamics. We present FedMaJ, a framework that dynamically selects aggregation rules via Majority Judgment voting. During voting rounds, clients evaluate candidate models across performance, resource utilization, channel condition, and fairness metrics. The server adopts the majority-preferred rule and retains it until the next vote, scheduled dynamically based on accuracy trends. Evaluated in over-the-air federated learning with explicit energy and resource cost modeling, synthetic and Fashion-MNIST experiments show that FedMaJ achieves competitive learning performance and superior aggregation-influence fairness. Under extreme-evaluation perturbations, Majority Judgment yields significantly more stable rule selections than mean-based scoring, establishing ordinal voting as a robust control layer for adaptive aggregation.

papers.title: Device-Induced Mobility Heterogeneity and Its Impact on Federated Next-Location Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting human mobility is central to network management, urban planning, and location-based services, yet privacy concerns are increasingly pushing such tasks toward federated learning. A key challenge in this setting is the strong heterogeneity of mobility data across users, which leads to non-IID data distributions and can significantly impact model performance and fairness. In this paper, we present a large-scale measurement study of device-level mobility heterogeneity using data from a major MNO in a dense European capital. Our dataset comprises mobility traces derived from network events, covering over 50,000 UEs across 178 smartphone models. We group devices into tiers based on their market segment and show that mobility characteristics, such as spatial range and regularity, vary systematically across these tiers, revealing a previously underexplored source of bias in mobility data. We investigate the implications of this heterogeneity on the use case of federated next-location prediction. In particular, we find that balancing device tiers across silos through tier-aware client selection yields the best results, improving fairness by up to 34.49% without degrading accuracy. In contrast, a FedProx-only approach achieves a 21.46% fairness improvement, offering a reasonable alternative when device information is unavailable, though with lower overall gains.

papers.title: Does Federated Training Degrade Explainability? A Comparative Analysis of Grad-CAM Faithfulness in Centralized vs. Federated Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Automated detection has become the essential safeguard against realistic synthetic media, but deploying it at scale requires training on sensitive data from multiple organizations, putting privacy and the transparency demanded by forensic review in direct conflict. Federated learning resolves the privacy side by sharing only model updates rather than raw data, but whether this comes at the cost of trustworthy gradient-based explanations, which analysts rely on to decide whether or not to trust a flagged clip, has not been studied. We present the systematic study of Grad-CAM explanation faithfulness under federated deepfake detection, evaluating an EfficientNet-B4 detector on FaceForensics++ across five federated clients under varying degrees of data heterogeneity. We find that the relationship between federation and explanation quality is non-monotonic: at near-IID (Independent and Identically Distributed Data) and moderate heterogeneity, federated models match or exceed the faithfulness of a centralized baseline, but at extreme heterogeneity, explanations break down entirely, becoming spatially incoherent and, on average, causally misleading. This degradation is not a general cost of federated training but a threshold effect tied to client heterogeneity, and we offer practical guidance for identifying when privacy-preserving deepfake detection can be deployed safely and when its explanations can no longer be trusted. Code and data partitions are available for reproducibility.

papers.title: DICE: Decentralized Incentive-driven Federated Learning for Efficient & Scalable Customization of Pretrained Models in Web3
papers.abstract: Customizing Pretrained Models (PMs) for downstream tasks demands task-specific data, which burgeoning Web3 applications provide abundantly. Blockchain-powered federated learning (BCFL) offers a secure and privacy-preserving paradigm to customize PMs among self-interested and untrusted Web3 participants. Yet, existing BCFL algorithms face severe efficiency and scalability challenges when applied to large PMs, due to their substantial computational and memory requirements and the hardware constraints of many participants. This paper introduces DICE, a novel BCFL algorithm that addresses the efficiency and scalability challenges of customizing large PMs in Web3 via two sets of synergistic techniques: (i) a dynamic progressive learning scheme and a model slice verification scheme to enable a wider range of honest participants, including those unable to deploy the full model, to engage in customizing PMs, while preserving model utility; (ii) a tree-structured committee consensus protocol and an efficiency-driven incentive scheme to address the dominant bottleneck that hinders existing BCFL algorithms from scaling to a larger number of data holders for customizing data-hungry large PMs, while maintaining security. Theoretical analysis and extensive experimental results on customizing vision and language PMs demonstrate DICE's efficiency, effectiveness, and security.
papers.venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)

papers.title: Trust-Aware Adaptive Searchable Encryption Using Federated Graph Neural Networks for Secure Healthcare Blockchain Systems
papers.abstract: Hospital insiders such as doctors, patients, and administrative staff who access records without clinical justification are hard to detect under fixed access rules. Doctors, patients, and bedside medical devices form relationships that flat machine learning features do not capture, and clinics cannot easily share raw data. TA-ASE-FGNN combines federated graph neural networks (GNNs) with adaptive searchable encryption and Hyperledger Fabric audit logs. Each clinic builds a heterogeneous trust graph from consultations, prescriptions, and Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) monitoring, and a federated GNN estimates trust locally without sharing patient sequence data. Trust scores set the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) key strength and keyword search scope. On a synthetic benchmark and on MIMIC-III, the F1 scores were 0.99 and 0.92, above those of a centralized graph convolutional network (GCN). Adaptive encryption reduced the insider detection latency from 18.4 h to 6.8 h. Federated averaging (FedAvg) gave consistent agreement across sites.
papers.venue: International Engineering Data Analytics and Management Conference (EAMCON)

papers.title: CroSSFed: Prototype-guided server-side finetuning with client-server reweighting for cross-domain semi-supervised federated learning
papers.abstract: Semi-supervised Federated Learning is a form of distributed deep learning in which multiple data centers (clients) collaboratively train a shared neural network under the coordination of a central server. The training process is performed without the exchange of private data and utilizes a mix of labeled and mostly unlabeled data. In the labels-at-server context, the server has a small, labeled dataset, while the participating clients possess no labels at all. Thus, there is a risk of server domain bias during server-side training, particularly in common real-world scenarios in which the server and client data come from different domains and thus have different distributions. To address this issue, the present study proposes a Prototype-Guided Server-side Finetuning mechanism that uses client prototypes to guide the update of the server model during the training process in such a way as to prevent overfitting to the server domain. A Local-Global Model Reweighting mechanism is additionally proposed to combine the client-aggregated model and the fine-tuned server model dynamically as training proceeds such that the client-aggregated model is gradually assigned increasing importance, thereby further decreasing the server domain bias. The experimental results obtained on a CIFAR10 -CINIC10 dataset show that the proposed method, designated as CroSSFed, achieves a 7% improvement in the classification accuracy over the state-of-the-art SemiFL method, which considers a similar data arrangement but does not address the cross-domain scenario.

papers.title: Evaluating federated learning under data heterogeneity with analysis of failure modes and practical mitigations
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) allows for collaborative model training across decentralized clients while maintaining data privacy; yet real-world deployments always include heterogeneous and non-identically distributed (non-IID) client data. Existing FL research primarily assesses system performance using aggregate metrics like global or average accuracy, which can hide differences in client behavior. This study provides a thorough empirical evaluation of federated learning under controlled data heterogeneity, with a major emphasis on worst-client performance as a measure of client-level robustness. Experiments are carried out on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 utilizing normal FedAvg training and commonly accepted baselines, such as FedProx and q-FedAvg, at various levels of Dirichlet-based label skew. The results show that, as heterogeneity increases, worst-client accuracy falls quickly, revealing silent errors that were previously disguised by aggregate evaluation. A comparison of mitigation options reveals that server-side client re-weighting improves worst-case performance under modest heterogeneity but becomes unstable and damaging under strong non-IID situations. In contrast, simple client-side data balancing reliably improves worst-client accuracy across all heterogeneity regimes without requiring additional infrastructure or algorithmic complexity. These findings emphasize the limitations of aggregate evaluation in federated learning, as well as the need of client-aware metrics and mitigation measures that increase local update quality while dealing with client-level inequalities in the face of true data heterogeneity.

papers.title: MarkCE: Watermark-based contribution estimation for federated diffusion models
Federated learning based liver tumor detection with hybrid optimization enabled deep learning using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCES: A MINI REVIEW
authors: Dr. Remya R S, Dr. K. Dhunmati., Mrs. E. Sankari
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT:Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in pharmaceutical sciences andpharmacy practice, enabling the transition from conventional trial-and-error approaches to data-driven,predictive, and personalized healthcare solutions. This review critically examines the applications of AIthroughout the pharmaceutical and pharmacy continuum, encompassing drug discovery, formulationdevelopment, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modeling, clinical decision support, supply chainmanagement, pharmacovigilance, and patient-centered care. Advanced AI methodologies, including machinelearning, deep learning, natural language processing, large language models, and computer vision, facilitatethe analysis of complex biomedical datasets, accelerate target identification, optimize molecular design,predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties, and supportprecision medicine initiatives. In clinical and community pharmacy settings, AI-driven systems enhancemedication safety, automate dispensing processes, improve inventory management, strengthen adverse drugreaction surveillance, and promote medication adherence through intelligent monitoring technologies and telepharmacy services. Despite these advantages, significant challenges remain, including data quality andinteroperability issues, algorithmic bias, limited model interpretability, concerns regarding privacy andcybersecurity, and evolving regulatory and ethical considerations. These barriers highlight the need for robustgovernance frameworks, transparent and explainable AI models, and rigorous validation strategies.Furthermore, AI is redefining the role of pharmacists by shifting professional responsibilities toward clinicaldecision-making, data analytics, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continuous patient care management.Future developments are expected to focus on explainable AI, federated learning, edge computing, hybridintelligence systems, and the integration of AI competencies into pharmacy education. Overall, the successfulimplementation of AI, coupled with human expertise and ethical oversight, has the potential to enhance theefficiency, safety, and personalization of pharmaceutical development and healthcare delivery, ultimatelyimproving patient outcomes and advancing the future of intelligent pharmacy practice.

papers.title: Enabling Sustainable Smart Grids With Programmable Networking and Federated Learning: A Phasor Measurement Unit Missing-Data Recovery Case Study
papers.abstract: As electric grids integrate more renewable generation, distributed resources, and data-driven control, sustainability increasingly depends on reliable communication and high-quality measurement data. Modern smart grids rely on continuous streams from devices, such as phasor measurement units (PMUs), to support real-time monitoring, renewable integration, energy efficiency, and grid stability. However, communication failures and cyberattacks can delay, corrupt, or interrupt critical measurements, degrading situational awareness and forcing more conservative operation. In renewable-rich grids, this loss of visibility can reduce the effective use of flexible and low-carbon resources. This article explores a sustainable and resilient smart grid intelligence architecture that combines programmable networking with federated learning. The Programming Protocol-Independent Packet Processors (P4) language enables the network to observe and react to selected traffic behaviors in real time, while federated learning improves models across distributed sites without transferring all measurement data to a central location. Together, they provide responsiveness, adaptability, and data locality for future smart grid communication systems. We use PMU missing-data recovery as a representative case study. A central controller coordinates model distribution and aggregation across 12 PMU measurement sites, while each site fine-tunes the shared model using local PMU data. This design preserves data locality, enables early awareness of communication-side disruptions, and supports collaborative model improvement. Experimental results show that the federated learning neural network (FLNN) achieves lower recovery errors than comparison methods, particularly for longer continuous gaps. More reliable PMU continuity can support state estimation, event detection, earlier corrective action, and more confident integration of variable renewable generation. Overall, this article shows how programmable data planes and distributed learning can support measurement continuity, communication resilience, and sustainable smart grid operation.

papers.title: Intelligent Cloud-Based Risk Assessment and Fraud Detection
papers.abstract: Workforce behavior, organizational culture, and the vulnerability of employees are highly entrenched in the areas of financial fraud and operational risks. Conventional fraud tools used in fraud detection pay attention to any transactions between the outside customers but do not consider the threat posed by employees, vendors, and HR functions. In this chapter, the implementation of a smart risk assessment model is expressed as a cloud-based model in which Human Resource Management (HRM) is incorporated in ensuring financial integrity is upheld. The model identifies HR-based frauds, such as payroll fraud, ghost employees, commission fraud, and expense fraud, and insider trading with the help of AI, real-time analytics, and scalable cloud computing. The chapter is free of ethical issues like explainable AI and employee privacy, but blending transactional data with behavioral HR metrics and using federated learning would help resolve issues related to algorithmic bias.
papers.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series

papers.title: Multi-Persistence Integrated Model Using Federated Learning for Big Data Analytics
papers.abstract: Scalable storage, privacy assurance, and distributed intelligence are needed in the Big Data applications in healthcare, finance, IoT, and smart systems. The limitations of centralized machine learning methods include high cost of communication, violation of privacy and poor scalability. Federated Learning (FL) is decentralized training without data sharing and multi-persistence storage strategies are a combination of relational, NoSQL and distributed file systems for efficient heterogeneous data management. The Multi-Persistence Integrated Model proposed in this paper is a joint optimization of storage, computation, and privacy, based on Federated Learning (MP-FL). The system combines a federated deep learning system with Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), MongoDB, and SQL databases. The experimental outcomes show that it is more scalable (32% faster training), has lower latency (27%), and provides greater protection to privacy than centralized learning. The suggested architecture offers an efficient implementation of secure, large-scale analytics.

papers.title: Distributed training and optimization of college English listening recognition model based on federated learning
papers.abstract: Aiming at the problems of scattered speech, limited privacy and strong noise interference in college English listening, a distributed listening recognition model based on federated learning is constructed. The system adopts a Conformer acoustic coding and CTC-Attention hybrid decoding structure, and achieves end-to-end recognition through spectral enhancement and robust feature modeling. To deal with Non-IID data, an improved FedAvg aggregation algorithm is designed, and the distribution consistency constraint and joint loss function are introduced to improve the global convergence stability. At the same time, gradient quantization and sparsity are adopted to reduce communication overhead, and differential privacy is combined to achieve secure parameter interaction. The experimental results show that this framework significantly optimizes the convergence speed and word error rate under multi-terminal conditions, verifying its engineering effectiveness.

papers.title: JayQuery: per-channel differential privacy in cross-institution split vertical federated learning
papers.abstract: A two-silo split vertical federated learning system carrying three differential privacy mechanisms simultaneously: cut-layer Gaussian noise on each silo's embeddings, DP-SGD on the coordinator's top model, and prior-based randomized response on the labels. Each mechanism has its own accountant and an explicitly stated neighboring relation, and the label budget is reported beside the composed Gaussian total rather than inside it. Includes Diffie-Hellman private set intersection over ristretto255, an embedding-inversion attack using a noise-matched learned inverse, loss-threshold membership inference, non-DP cut-layer defense baselines for comparison, and the sweep, backfill and analysis tooling used to produce the reported results.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Face Recognition Using Deep Learning - A Review of Models, System Design, Applications and Challenges
authors: Prof. Sanghesh Bele and Sakshi R. Haramkar
papers.abstract: Face recognition has become one of the most widely deployed applications of artificial intelligence, supporting smartphone unlocking, attendance management, banking and border control. Deep learning has replaced hand-crafted features with representations learned directly from large collections of face images, producing large gains in accuracy under unconstrained conditions. This paper presents a structured review of artificial intelligence-based face recognition using deep learning. It explains the stages of a recognition pipeline, compares the main families of deep models and training objectives, proposes a modular system architecture with a liveness check, and summarizes datasets and evaluation measures. Application areas, including education and financial services, are discussed together with the main challenges: pose and occlusion, spoofing, demographic bias, adversarial attacks and privacy. The paper closes with emerging directions such as self-supervised learning, synthetic training data, federated learning and privacy-preserving matching, and offers practical recommendations for responsible deployment
papers.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

papers.title: Federated Learning Approaches for Anomaly Detection in IoT Environments: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices is driving significant data generation—and, consequently, a crucial demand for reliable, privacy-centric anomaly detection (AD). Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing sensitive data, addressing fundamental constraints encountered by conventional, server-oriented approaches. Adhering to the PRISMA 2020 framework, we rigorously examined 60 well-documented studies (2017–2026) on FL-oriented AD in IoT. We scrutinize architectures, learning paradigms, datasets, applications, privacy mechanisms, communication efficacy, and evaluation metrics, and systematically classify the domain into a taxonomy encompassing architectural frameworks, privacy-preserving strategies, communication protocols, and detection algorithms. In scholarly publications, FL methodologies frequently align with centralized references while preserving data confidentiality, yielding detection accuracy metrics ranging from 80% to 99.89%, with the majority of approaches exceeding 90%. Simultaneously, unresolved challenges persist: non-IID and heterogeneous data, communication and energy expenditures, resilience under adversarial circumstances, and real-world scalability. Emerging hybrid methodologies that amalgamate FL with complementary techniques (e.g., model compression, secure aggregation, and multi-modal fusion) demonstrate promise. This review delves into the contemporary landscape, exposes inadequacies, and charts explicit research directions to enhance the security and reliability of IoT environments.
papers.venue: Sakarya University Journal of Computer and Information Sciences

papers.title: Decentralized federated learning with dynamic client selection based on particle swarm optimization
Review on Optimized Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Enhanced Classification of Medicinal Plant Leaves Using Metaheuristic and Score Voting Techniques
papers.abstract: MPC (Medicinal Plant Classification) has significance in drug discovery, herbal and biodiversity conservation. Conventional ways of identification tend to be sluggish and inaccurate, novel AI-powered systems are required. This survey presents hybrid deep models that use CNNs including methodologies, like metaheuristic optimization and score voting of ensemble-forming. Different deep learning models are studied in performance of feature extraction and classification, i.e., ResNet, DenseNet, EfficientNet, and Vision Transformers (ViT). These papers have utilized metaheuristic e.g. Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Grey Wolf Optimiser (GWO) etc., as an aid to optimising the performance of a model by using hyperparameter and feature selection methods. Some of the most applicable techniques are ensemble methods and they combine two or more classifiers to enhance the reliability of decisions with the most popular one being score voting. Arguments on the most critical issues in applying these algorithms (i.e. computational complexity, overfitting, data availability, etc.) are presented relative to the provision of future research directions like quantum/computing, federated learning, and multi-modal classification. It illustrates how hybrid AI systems can be used to identify medicinal plants with a power that has never been explored before to use in botany and health care with efficient, accurate and scalable classification tools.

papers.title: FedHPR: Poisoning-robust federated learning adapted to fully homomorphic encryption under data heterogeneity for wind power forecasting
Precision Medicine Using Artificial Intelligence and Genomics: A Comprehensive Review
papers.abstract: Precision medicine is an emerging healthcare paradigm that tailors prevention, diagnosis, and treatment to individual patients using genetic, clinical, environmental, and lifestyle information. Advances in next-generation sequencing, bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) now allow clinicians to analyse genomic variants, stratify disease risk, and select therapies at a level of individual detail that population-averaged medicine cannot provide. This paper reviews AI-enabled precision medicine, synthesising landmark and recent peer-reviewed literature published between 2004 and 2026, and tracing the field from early blood-group stratification through the Human Genome Project to national precision medicine programmes and the multimodal AI of the present day. A conceptual framework is proposed that integrates electronic health records, genomic sequencing, laboratory tests, and wearable-device data in a secure platform where AI models identify biomarkers, predict risk, and recommend treatment for clinician validation; it is synthesised from literature-reported practices rather than experimentally validated. Applications in oncology, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, rare genetic disorders, pharmacogenomics, and remote monitoring are examined, followed by the main challenges, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, unrepresentative genomic datasets, cost, interpretability, and ethics, together with mitigation strategies. Emerging directions, including digital twins, federated learning, multimodal AI, and CRISPR-assisted therapies, are discussed. This review highlights the role of AI and genomics in moving healthcare from reactive to predictive and personalised, and identifies priorities for future research.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: FedMann: A Manually Coordinated Federated Learning Framework Applied to Multiple Myeloma—A Feasibility Study
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Federated learning (FL) enables multi-institutional model development in oncology without sharing patient-level data, but automated FL infrastructures typically require dedicated servers, firewall modifications, and substantial IT support to deploy. These requirements may be prohibitive for smaller institutions or consortia with limited IT resources or stringent information security requirements. We developed FedMann, a manually coordinated FL framework, and demonstrated its feasibility by applying it to prediction of suboptimal multiple myeloma (MM) treatment across two clinical sites with substantially different patient populations. Methods: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health record data from patients newly diagnosed with MM at the Veterans Affairs (VA) Healthcare System or Boston Medical Center (BMC) between 2012 and 2022. Demographic, clinical, and geographic predictors were used to predict non-receipt of guideline-concordant primary therapy, defined as not receiving a frontline triplet or quadruplet regimen or autologous stem cell transplant when eligible. FedMann was implemented as a four-stage cycle of local training, parameter sharing through an access-controlled repository, sample-size-weighted parameter averaging at a coordinating site, and federated model redistribution. Models were evaluated on site-specific held-out test sets using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with bootstrap-resampled 95% confidence intervals. Results: VA and BMC contributed 4887 and 261 cases, respectively, with substantial demographic differences across all measured characteristics including sex distribution (96.3% male at VA vs. 58.6% at BMC; p < 0.001). The BMC-only model achieved an AUC of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.56–0.81) on the BMC test set. The federated model achieved 0.68 (95% CI, 0.55–0.80) on the BMC test set and 0.70 (95% CI, 0.67–0.72) on the VA test set. Conclusions: A manually coordinated FL framework can support multi-institutional model fitting in oncology without exchanging patient-level data and without requiring dedicated FL infrastructure. In a two-site MM application, performance was comparable between the federated model and each site’s own local model, and the VA only model showed no apparent loss of discrimination when externally validated at BMC, with no statistically significant differences in AUC on the BMC test set. Although absolute AUCs were modest, reflecting limited cohort size and a small predictor set, this application demonstrates the feasibility of the framework as an alternative when automated FL deployment is impractical.

papers.title: Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Explainable AI-driven Clinical Decision-Making

papers.title: A federated learning-based collaborative demand forecasting framework for multinational oil companies
papers.abstract: This study discusses the difficulties of energy effectiveness, device Variability, and privacy of data in distributed demand forecasting systems for the Industrial Internet of Things enabled by 5G(IIoT). Federated Education (FL)-based collaborative framework is proposed, enhanced with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize client selection, task scheduling, and energy consumption in highly dynamic oilfield environments. The framework uses multi-agent DRL to balance energy efficiency and prediction accuracy, so as to realize real-time decision-making and adaptive orchestration of IIoT devices. Gradient compression techniques are used to minimize communication overhead without affecting model performance. Experimental validation on a synthetic oil production dataset shows that the proposed framework reduces energy consumption by 60% while maintaining prediction accuracy, with a tradeoff rate of only 5% compared to traditional FL methods. The framework improves the convergence speed, and the number of training cycles is reduced by more than 50% compared with baseline models such as FedAvg and FedProx. These findings confirm the effectiveness of DRLdriven optimization in meeting the special needs of Internet of Things (IIoT)-based oilfield operations. This study provides a reliable and scalable method to predict collaborative demand in distributed Internet of Things (IIoT) systems. The potential of the framework in improving operational efficiency and data privacy is significantly demonstrated due to the integration of multi-agent DRL and energy-aware orchestration mechanism, allowing intelligent decision-making in complex oilfield environments.

papers.title: Personalized and differentially private federated learning for mobility data mining via the TrajectoryGuard framework
papers.abstract: This paper presents TrajectoryGuard, a personalized and privacy-preserving federated learning framework for secure and efficient mobility data mining. The framework integrates differential privacy, secure multiparty aggregation, and adaptive gradient compression to ensure that raw location traces, such as GPS logs or geo-tagged user activities, remain confined to user devices, thereby minimizing privacy leakage risks. Unlike conventional approaches, TrajectoryGuard introduces a dynamic noise-aware optimization mechanism and personalized aggregation scheme to enhance both model accuracy and robustness under non-IID and heterogeneous client scenarios. Experimental evaluation on the GeoLife dataset and the T-Drive Beijing taxi trajectory dataset demonstrates competitive performance, achieving 92.5% accuracy and 30% reduction in total per-round communication overhead (comprising gradient payload, model broadcast, and encryption metadata) while maintaining strong privacy guarantees (ε = 0.9 at σ2 = 1.0). Comparative results against FedAvg, FedProx, AdaptFL, and Fed-Ensemble confirm TrajectoryGuard's superiority in convergence stability, privacy resilience, and predictive utility. The framework's practical viability is illustrated through a real-world case study in urban trajectory forecasting, highlighting its relevance for applications in smart transportation and behavior modeling. The accuracy metric specifically corresponds to next-destination classification, a multi-class problem where the model predicts a destination category (e.g., home, workplace, or shopping location) from partial GPS trajectories. Evaluation follows an 80/20 time-based train/test split per user to prevent data leakage across temporal boundaries.

papers.title: Research on personality rights risk profiling and clinical governance pathways in brain-computer interface neurosurgery scenarios
papers.abstract: Federated learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and reinforcement learning are increasingly shaping the landscape of neurosurgical brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. To address the major issue of personality rights protection, this study proposes a data-based, privacy-preserving BCI neurosurgical risk analysis and clinical governance framework. A federated learning protocol is provided for secure aggregation and analysis of multi-center EEG and fMRI data while maintaining the data sovereignty of the institutions. The system uses SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to provide transparent explanations of risk factors. The impact of high-frequency neural oscillations and functional connectivity patterns on the vulnerability of personality rights is the focus. The reinforcement learning module dynamically optimizes the clinical decision path to achieve actionable governance. Experimental results from a multi-institutional dataset show that the technology achieved 92.3% accuracy in risk prediction and reduced ethical conflicts by 38.7% in simulated clinical workflows. The combined framework not only improves the technical performance of risk assessment, but also improves the application compliance of intelligent neural technology in ethical supervision and regulation. This research lays the foundation for the use of reliable, interpretable and adaptive AI systems in the sensitive environment of BCI neurosurgery.

papers.title: Decentralised Approaches to Training AI Models in Healthcare
papers.abstract: In the last decade, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the healthcare field, particularly medical image analysis, by enabling the automated learning of feature representations from large-scale datasets across a wide range of medical tasks. However, its broader clinical adoption, especially in the imaging context, remains constrained by the difficulty of collecting large, heterogeneous training datasets. Patient data are subject to strict regulatory frameworks, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which impose substantial barriers to multi-centre data sharing and often render large multi-centre centralised training impractical. Furthermore, AI models trained on data from a single or a limited number of institutions are prone to important performance degradation when deployed in unseen clinical environments, owing to variability in acquisition protocols, scanner hardware, and patient populations. Federated Learning (FL) is able to address these concerns by enabling collaborative model training without sharing raw data, thereby preserving privacy and improving exposure to diverse data distributions. Despite its demonstrated effectiveness for image classification and segmentation tasks, the application of FL to medical Image-to-Image (I2I) translation was explored only in the field of cross-modality Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) translation prior to this work. This thesis aims to address this gap by focusing on Synthetic Computed Tomography (sCT) generation as a relevant use case and further supporting the FL in healthcare. In detail, the research work presented in this thesis spanned four interconnected areas: feasibility, efficiency, security, and translational tooling. The feasibility of federated sCT generation was established through multi-centre studies. The first study investigated brain MRI-to-sCT translation across five institutions, giving rise to the FedSynthCT framework. The second extended this framework to head and neck Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT)-to-sCT translation, using four publicly available institutional datasets. In both studies, federated models trained on heterogeneous distributed data achieved stable convergence and consistent generalisation to independent external datasets, without requiring data centralisation or site-specific adaptations. These results confirmed that sCT generation is a viable application domain for FL, and that inter-site data heterogeneity does not preclude effective decentralised collaboration. Practical barriers to FL applicability and deployment were subsequently investigated. Within the FedSynthCT framework, an adaptive parameter-freezing strategy was proposed to substantially reduce the computational demand, and therefore the time and energy required for federated training, in line with the increasingly important principles of Green AI. Furthermore, a security analysis of the FedSynthCT framework revealed that gradient inversion attacks did not represent a viable threat in the evaluated setting, while residual vulnerabilities to membership inference and poisoning attacks were identified, motivating the future adoption of system-level safeguards beyond the federated algorithm itself. The implications of communication-efficiency techniques, including model compression, sparsification, and weight clustering, were further characterised in the context of federated brain tumour segmentation setting, demonstrating that only moderate and well-balanced levels of these techniques can substantially reduce communication overhead while preserving segmentation accuracy. Open-source software tools were developed and released to bridge the gap between research and its application in healthcare. ImageAugmenter, a medical image augmentation extension for the 3D Slicer Imaging Computing Platform, was published to support data preparation for both centralised and federated pipelines. Subsequently, the 3D Slicer extension named ModalityConverter was released to integrate the pre-trained federated I2I models developed throughout this research alongside existing centralised models, enabling their use and further development within a widely adopted medical research environment. The extension also includes an automated quality assessment module, based on a Deep Learning (DL) framework that predicts quantitative sCT Mean Absolute Error (MAE) without requiring ground-truth Computed Tomography (CT) data, thereby supporting direct output validation in a single environment, without requiring specialised infrastructure or programming expertise. The contributions of this thesis confirmed that decentralised learning can be a practically viable paradigm for collaborative medical image analysis and established the methodological, analytical, and software foundation for future multi-centre clinical validation and broader deployment of federated I2I translation in healthcare.

papers.title: Metacampus as the operational backbone for the Unite! Research School 2026 (Report 09/2026)
papers.abstract: This ninth Unite! success story report documents the use of the Unite! federated platform Metacampus as the operational backbone of the Unite! Research School (URS) 2026, which was hosted by Politecnico di Torino at the Sanctuary of Oropa and PoliTO's main campus as the third edition of the initiative. The course environment was designed to support the entire lifecycle of the event—from the application and selection process (383 applications, 151 selected students from all Unite! partner universities) to the delivery of interdisciplinary learning activities across three disciplinary tracks, and finally to the submission and assessment of student work. Rather than relying on separate tools for each stage, the organisers used a single shared digital environment This was structured into dedicated course spaces for disciplinary tracks, plenary sessions and transferable skills activities, with differentiated access rights for applicants, students, teachers and administrative staff. Members of all partner universities accessed the platform using their institutional credentials, which reduced information fragmentation and provided a consistent point of reference for the approximately 70 researchers and professors involved. The report identifies key lessons learned, in particular the need to plan the information architecture in advance, to define user roles and permissions carefully, and to ensure accessible IT support from the beginning. It concludes with ten recommendations for organisers planning similar international educational events, along with technical recommendations for the Unite! Digital Campus, including clearer role distinctions during registration, reusable course structures for recurring events, and improved support for application workflows. The series “Unite! Digital Teaching and Learning Success Story Report” was initiated by Cm.2 Digital Campus, led by TU Graz (Martin Ebner) as part of the idea to collect, spread and enhance the possibilities, usages and lessons learned of teaching and learning offers using the federated learning management system Metacampus in 11/2024 till the end of the current Erasmus+ funding period 10/2026. All reports are available under open license and originally published at the TU Graz repository.
papers.venue: TUGraz OPEN Library (Graz University of Technology)

papers.title: A systematic review on federated learning techniques and applications for advancing industrial resilience and sustainability
AI-Driven Federated Learning Frameworks for Privacy-Preserving Smart Urban Energy Management
papers.abstract: The growing complexity of urban energy systems with smartness requires intelligent solutions that are privacy friendly to manage the distributed energy resources efficiently. This chapter introduces a federated learning model that is AI-powered and in this system, model training is performed in an intelligent grid, micro grid, and IoT-based devices, without the exchange of raw data. The strategy improves accuracy in load forecasting, efficiency of energy use, and lessens the amount of overhead in communication besides maintaining data privacy and security. The framework combines edge computing and state-of-the-art AI to promote scalable and adaptive energy management to add to sustainable, resilient, and human-centric smart city ecosystems.

papers.title: Di-fedDIL: Distributed fault diagnosis of idler bearings of long-distance belt conveyor under cloud-edge resource constraints
papers.abstract: In long-distance belt conveyor systems, idler bearings are widely distributed along the transportation route, making distributed fault diagnosis necessary. A cloud-edge architecture provides a feasible solution by enabling local inference at edge devices and collaborative model training through the cloud. However, distributed idler-bearing diagnosis still faces two major challenges: (1) heterogeneous sensor data across different idlers and time-varying fault features under evolving operating conditions and (2) limited edge computing and communication resources. To address these challenges, this study proposes Di-FedDIL, a distributed fault diagnosis framework for idler bearings under cloud-edge collaboration. The framework consists of the dilated separable attention convolution network (DiSAC-Net), federated learning via contrastive alignment and progressive Euclidean regularization (FedCAP), and dual-anchor incremental learning (DIL). For edge diagnosis, DiSAC-Net performs lightweight feature extraction and online fault inference at edge devices. For federated collaborative learning, FedCAP enables distributed clients to collaboratively learn shared diagnostic knowledge while adapting to heterogeneous local data. For incremental updating, DIL continuously adapts personalized models to evolving operating conditions while balancing new knowledge acquisition and historical knowledge retention. In addition, a hierarchical greedy optimization strategy jointly performs task offloading and bandwidth allocation to reduce diagnostic response time under cloud-edge resource constraints. Experimental results show that Di-FedDIL outperforms the compared federated learning methods. The proposed resource-allocation strategy reduces task completion time by approximately 25% compared with fully local computing. These results demonstrate that Di-FedDIL provides a practical solution for distributed idler-bearing fault diagnosis while improving execution efficiency under limited cloud-edge computing and communication resources.

papers.title: Smart Technologies in Construction and Transportation Infrastructure: A Review of AI, IoT, and Data-Driven Innovations
papers.abstract: While the field of civil engineering has traditionally been dominated by hands-on and experience-based techniques, the advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and data analytics are transforming it. This paper provides a structured outcome-oriented narrative review of the applications of smart technology in two dominant areas: construction management and transportation infrastructure. It is based on 37 peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers, and technical reports from 2015 to 2026 that were selected purposively, without using a registered systematic search. The evidence has been grouped into eight application themes: AI/ML in construction project management; IoT-enabled site and structural monitoring; AI-driven intelligent transportation systems; IoT-based smart pavement and road monitoring; machine-learning-based structural health monitoring; digital twins and blockchain; UAV and computer-vision monitoring; and cybersecurity in smart infrastructure. The reported outcomes represent distinct performance dimensions and are not directly compared: examples include a 0.12% cost variance for AI/ML project models, a concrete strength prediction error within 1–2 MPa alongside a maximum UWB worker positioning error of 1.44 m for an IoT-based system, a 98.6% traffic-monitoring performance for a machine-learning classification model, and a hardhat-detection precision of 93.1% for Faster R-CNN. Themes of AI and IoT integration are most frequently associated with improved prediction, monitoring, and decision support, while digital twins and blockchain are primarily associated with data trust, traceability, and operational latency reduction. Recurring barriers include data interoperability, data security, implementation costs, and metric heterogeneity across literature. This review concludes with a research agenda prioritizing interoperable data standards, edge-AI and federated learning, cybersecurity-by-design, and standardized outcome reporting.
papers.venue: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies

papers.title: Securing the Swarm:
papers.abstract: Since Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms are more widely employed in mission-critical missions, they serve as potential targets of dual-vector attacks, e.g. Denial of Service (DoS) or GPS spoofing attacks that exploit cyber vulnerabilities and physical sensor dependencies, respectively. Most traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) treat these domains independently or use centralized data processing which leads to single points of failure as well as privacy concerns. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents a Multi-Boundary Federated Intrusion Detection System (MB-FIDS) which builds upon disparate cyber-physical defense layers without sacrificing swarm privacy.
