papers.abstract: Split Federated Learning (SFL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for training large-scale deep models on resource-constrained edge devices. Although asynchronous SFL alleviates the straggler bottleneck caused by system heterogeneity, it inevitably introduces two coupled dimensions of inconsistency: horizontal inconsistency across clients and vertical inconsistency between clients and the server. These inconsistencies, further exacerbated by statistical heterogeneity, result in biased activation representations, model divergence, and severe client drift. To address these challenges, we propose CoASFL, an inconsistency-aware asynchronous SFL framework that incorporates a dynamic activation merging mechanism and a consistency-aware model aggregation mechanism. Specifically, CoASFL constructs more consistent activation sequences from heterogeneous clients to alleviate horizontal inconsistency, and dynamically adjusts aggregation weights according to client participation frequencies and progress gaps to mitigate vertical inconsistency. By jointly coordinating activation-level and model-level consistency, CoASFL effectively suppresses inconsistency propagation during asynchronous training. Extensive experiments on an 80-device heterogeneous edge testbed demonstrate that CoASFL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art SFL approaches, accelerating training by 1.61$\times$ to 3.74$\times$ and improving final model accuracy by up to 3.26\% under heterogeneous scenarios.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Domain Generalization in Edge Networks via Dynamic Prototype Regulation
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed paradigm for Internet of Things (IoT) edge networks. However, deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) over wireless edge networks presents distinct challenges: large model parameters increase uplink transmission latency over bandwidth-constrained fading channels, and non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data exacerbates client drift. Existing feature alignment solutions often introduce auxiliary computations that consume time slots allocated for wireless parameter transmission, increasing the likelihood of straggler dropouts under system delay constraints. To address these issues, we propose DPGR-GCAM, a communication-efficient federated domain generalization framework. By employing a dual-parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) architecture, we design a channel-aware tiered transmission mechanism that adaptively truncates payloads to maximize node survival rates under fading conditions. To mitigate client drift, we introduce the Gradient-Conflict Aware Modulation (GCAM) mechanism. GCAM operates within the low-dimensional feature manifold to dynamically resolve multi-objective optimization conflicts with minimal edge computation latency, thereby reducing computation-induced network outages. Experiments demonstrate that DPGR-GCAM improves cross-domain generalization and sustains convergence under network fading scenarios with a 10\% client participation rate.

papers.title: Peer-Relative Trust-Guided Update Screening for Robust Semi-Decentralized Federated Learning under Label-Flipping Attacks
papers.abstract: Trust and reputation mechanisms can reduce the influence of malicious clients in federated learning (FL), but strict update filtering is difficult under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data because honest local updates may temporarily reduce performance on a shared validation proxy. Extending an earlier trust-based semi-decentralized FL (SDFL) framework, this paper operationalizes the trust signals and introduces peer-relative update screening that combines a robust validation-utility score with direction- and norm-based update quality. The method is evaluated with 50 MNIST clients, 20% persistent label-flip attackers, Dirichlet heterogeneity levels of 0.5 and 0.1, 100 communication rounds, and five paired random seeds. Under moderate heterogeneity, the proposed method reaches 98.37% final accuracy while rejecting 95.82% of malicious updates and retaining 90.30% of benign updates; the final benign and malicious trust distributions are completely separated (KS=1.00). Under severe heterogeneity, it reaches 95.25% accuracy, rejects 88.55% of malicious updates, and retains 76.90% of benign updates (KS=0.96). Trust weighting alone preserves slightly higher utility in the most heterogeneous condition, but accepts all malicious submissions. The results therefore distinguish influence mitigation from explicit containment and quantify the utility-selectivity trade-off introduced by screening. The study provides an empirically validated off-chain governance core that can feed blockchain-based audit and incentive layers in SDFL.

papers.title: A model for realizing the transaction value of power data elements in the digital intelligence system
papers.abstract: In response to the demand for data assetization in the power industry under the digital intelligence system, this paper proposes a trading value realization model for power data elements based on artificial intelligence and computing technology. By adopting deep learning, the attribute fusion of data elements is achieved. Based on blockchain-based rights confirmation, trusted transactions, and federated learning technology, cross-domain data security circulation is realized, forming a complete closed loop from data collection, intelligent pricing to value feedback. The results show that this model can enhance data pricing accuracy by 17.6% and transaction efficiency by over 20%, providing a feasible technical route for promoting the establishment of the power data element market and advancing the digitalization process of energy.
papers.venue: International Conference on Computer Vision, Algorithm, and Image Processing (CVAIP)

papers.title: PFedQFT: Personalized Federated Quantum-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Medical Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Medical data remain fragmented across institutional silos because of privacy, governance, and ownership constraints. Federated learning enables medical institutions to adapt large language models (LLMs) collaboratively without transferring raw records. However, independently parameterized low-rank adapters incur repeated parameter and communication costs across Transformer projections, while uniform aggregation may limit adaptation to heterogeneous institutional data. We propose PFedQFT, a quantum-inspired framework for personalized federated fine-tuning with a compact shared adapter. Specifically, PFedQFT constructs reusable orthonormal adaptation bases from compact skew-symmetric generators using a truncated matrix-exponential approximation followed by QR orthonormalization. Compatible projections reuse these bases, while a globally shared full core preserves the flexibility of each projection. Each client further maintains a lightweight private residual operator, whose directions are learned globally and whose coefficients remain local. Experiments on seven public medical tasks and multiple LLM backbones show substantial reductions in trainable parameters and per-round adapter upload volume, with competitive predictive performance on most tasks.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation with User Dropouts in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of users' gradients or model updates without revealing individual values. With user dropouts, correlated random keys protect local gradients while allowing recovery of the desired gradient sum. We consider three phases: key distribution, masked-gradient upload, and mask elimination. Users establish correlated keys, upload masked gradients, and provide additional messages to eliminate residual aggregate masks. Existing information-theoretic schemes typically design mask-elimination communication for a prescribed dropout threshold and evaluate its cost under worst-case dropouts across the masked-gradient upload and mask-elimination phases. Such designs cannot adjust communication to actual dropout scenarios. Moreover, the randomness and communication costs of establishing correlated keys remain largely unexplored. To address these limitations, we formulate an adaptive secure aggregation framework under the T-colluding security constraint and construct a single scheme that supports all feasible dropout scenarios by adapting its communication to the actual number of dropouts. We establish converse bounds on four resources: key randomness, key-distribution communication, masked-gradient communication, and mask-elimination communication. The latter two bounds are characterized for each realized dropout set in the masked-gradient upload phase. The proposed scheme achieves the optimal masked-gradient communication rate for every feasible dropout scenario and the optimal mask-elimination communication rate in almost all feasible regimes. Its key rate and key-distribution communication rate are each optimal or within a factor of two of their respective information-theoretic optima. These results characterize the fundamental randomness and communication costs of secure aggregation with user dropouts.

papers.title: Federated Community Detection in Bipartite Networks
papers.abstract: We study federated spectral estimation when a large matrix is horizontally partitioned across servers that cannot share raw data. We propose FLICKER, a target-specific gradient-based power iteration that recovers a singular direction associated with a prescribed spectral target using only matrix-vector products on local blocks. Different target directions can be recovered independently and in parallel. We establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees and provide a recursive grid-search procedure for spectral target selection. Building on FLICKER, we develop BiFLICKER for federated community detection in bipartite networks, together with a sequential projected variant for nearby or repeated singular directions. Under a sparse bipartite stochastic block model, we show that properly rescaled leading singular values from a reference server provide valid global targets, and that Sequential BiFLICKER achieves a vanishing misclustering rate and exact recovery under stronger sparsity conditions. Simulations show that BiFLICKER remains close to centralized spectral clustering and is more robust than existing federated spectral baselines when local sample sizes are small. On a LastFM user-artist network naturally partitioned by country, Sequential BiFLICKER attains an overall ARI of 0.94 against centralized clustering while revealing cross-country communities with distinct listening profiles.

papers.title: After the Federation: Benchmarking Knowledge Portability to Heterogeneous Newcomers
papers.abstract: Once historical clients become unavailable, a federation must serve newcomers through the artifact it leaves behind. How much of its knowledge remains useful in an architecture chosen afterward? We introduce FEDNBO, a seven-dataset benchmark that separates knowledge supply, policy identification, and private-model compilation under disjoint data roles. Controlled studies expose inflated oracle gains, architecture-dependent transfer reversals, and a gap between teacher accuracy and private-model utility. Ordinary public-response distillation provides a competitive reference without public task labels or newcomer samples: gains over strengthened local training are 23.52 and 16.62 percentage points on 300 CelebA identities and 300 FedEMNIST writers, respectively. In a complete-pipeline FedEMNIST comparison, this reference reaches 97.13% accuracy with 12.4 seconds of compilation per architecture, versus 97.03% and 67.5 seconds for a HeteroFedTTA reconstruction at the same epoch budget. Equal-count public-input interventions extend support sensitivity to trainable visual backbones. Together, these results establish an auditable benchmark and a strong reference for evaluating the utility, cost and reliability of post-federation knowledge transfer.

papers.title: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design
papers.abstract: Abstract Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

papers.title: Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be
Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
papers.abstract: Abstract Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

papers.title: Discovering network resilience formulas with symbolized reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Many complex networks display remarkable resilience under external perturbations, internal failures and environmental changes, yet they can swiftly deteriorate into dysfunction upon the removal of a few keystone nodes. Discovering formulas that measure network resilience offers the potential to prevent catastrophic collapses—from species extinctions to financial crises—with profound implications for real-world systems. Existing resilience metrics are typically designed to characterize topological properties, whereas in many real systems resilience is defined by the dynamics imposed on the network; consequently, metrics that explicitly incorporate dynamical state information are expected to be better suited for identifying keystone nodes in such settings. Here, we report an automatic method for resilience metric discovery, which learns from how machine learning model solves a complicated network dismantling problem and symbolizes its network attack strategies into mathematical formulas. This proposed self-inductive approach discovers a resilience formula that accounts for both topology and dynamics, highlighting how the correlation between node degree and state shapes overall network resilience. Additionally, our approach discovers formulas that refine existing well-established resilience metrics with over 37.5% improvement in accuracy, significantly advancing human understanding of complex networks with machine learning. Complex networks can fail when a small number of critical components are lost. Here, the authors use symbolized reinforcement learning to derive interpretable formulas that identify these components and quantify network resilience.

papers.title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase
papers.abstract: Abstract Soil salinization threatens agricultural production, water management, and ecosystem health. Yet, how increasing aridity will reshape 21st-century soil salinity patterns across drylands, particularly in croplands, remains unclear. Here, we compile a relatively comprehensive global soil salinity dataset from the past two decades, projecting future dryland soil salinity dynamics using climate-driven machine learning models with multiple covariates, including dynamic dryland extent and human influences. Our results show an 8% expansion of global drylands saline soils under increasing aridity by 2100 (SSP5-8.5) relative to 2004–2023. Southwestern US, Mexico, southern Europe, central South America, eastern and southern Africa are highest-risk hotspots. We further show dryland croplands face serious salinization, especially irrigated systems, where half of these newly salinized areas project more than 4.9% (maize), 17.2% (dryland rice), 3.3% (sorghum), and 21.2% (wheat) potential production losses. Our findings inform long-term adaptation strategies to mitigate emerging salinization risks and sustain water and food security.

papers.title: The case for AI degrowth
Audio long read: How to stay smart in the age of AI — the science of critical thinking
Daily briefing: How to rebuild science from ruin
Shallow Probes Are Sufficient for Near-Oracle Personalization Depth Allocation in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Rather than proposing a new federated optimizer, we study whether a small client-specific measurement budget can support cost-aware personalization-depth decisions under a utility that trades Macro-F1 against deployment cost. Exhaustive evaluation of six depths defines an offline oracle that is not deployable. We audit the Probe Sufficiency Hypothesis: three shallow probes (P0--P2) may contain most decision-relevant information for approaching that oracle. FedPBA is a secondary learned instantiation for deep-action extrapolation. On CIFAR-10/100 and patient-disjoint PTB-XL (45 sessions; 900 clients; 2700 evaluations; GroupKFold), training-free greedy probing achieves regret 0.0071 and 98.3 percent oracle recovery, beating metadata-only policies and FedPBA (0.0110 / 97.3 percent). Aggregate shallow-best versus oracle correlation is 0.9818 but falls to 0.578 on deep-oracle rows; PTB-XL deep-oracle cases remain a high-regret boundary without a validated escalation gate.

papers.title: DROD: Dual-Ratio Ordered Dropout for Federated Continual Learning on Heterogeneous Devices
papers.abstract: Federated learning for capacity-heterogeneous clients and federated continual learning are each well studied on their own, but their intersection -- clients holding differently sized models while every client's data stream also drifts over time -- remains underexplored. We study this setting directly, training a ResNet-18 fleet from scratch on Split-CIFAR-100 (10 tasks, class-incremental), and introduce DROD (Dual-Ratio Ordered Dropout), which builds on FjORD's Ordered Dropout by using two independent reduction axes to extract sub-models: a shortcut ratio and a branch ratio. On a shared parameter/FLOP budget ladder, DROD achieves the highest mean accuracy among the heterogeneous-model federated learning strategies we compare. Its advantage over the two strongest baseline geometries persists across every replay-buffer size we test and under ER, DER++, and BiC; under EWC, all three geometries collapse alike.

papers.title: Towards End-to-End Privacy-Preserving AI for Real-Time ECG Monitoring
papers.abstract: Healthcare artificial intelligence is shifting from centralized archives toward distributed pipelines that combine wearables, edge processing, cloud analytics, and multi-institutional learning. In this regime, electrocardiogram (ECG) streams cross multiple trust boundaries, so privacy cannot be reduced to a single transmission control. Existing privacy-enhancing technologies typically secure isolated stages and leave gaps between acquisition, analysis, and institutional collaboration. This doctoral research develops a unified lifecycle framework for end-to-end privacy-preserving ECG AI. Rather than introducing another privacy mechanism, it orchestrates complementary privacy-enhancing technologies across the clinical ECG lifecycle, allocating each mechanism to the trust boundary where its security, computational, and operational properties are most appropriate. Three interoperable modules instantiate the framework: AES with CKKS-based homomorphic statistics for secure monitoring; adaptive chaotic protection for low-latency edge transmission; and federated learning with homomorphic aggregation under heterogeneous partitions. Across prototype monitoring, signal-security analysis, and simulated collaboration, the programme shows that privacy layers can be composed without collapsing diagnostic utility, while exposing overhead and fidelity limits that constrain clinical translation.

papers.title: AdaFedXplain: Adaptive Federated Learning with Explainable AI for Ransomware Detection
papers.abstract: Attacks using ransomware have developed into complex multiphase campaigns that target vital infrastructure, resulting in annual damages of billions of dollars. Conventional detection techniques are ineffective against zero-day variations, and privacy issues are raised by centralized machine learning algorithms. Federated learning allows for cooperative model training without data sharing, however current FL approaches suffer from explainability issues, high communication cost, and non-IID data heterogeneity. In this study, we present AdaFedXplain, an explainable AI-based adaptive federated learning system for ransomware detection. Our approach includes progressive XGBoost complexity to avoid overfitting, a decaying learning rate schedule for stable convergence, and dynamic client grading based on ransomware prevalence and data sufficiency. Using 62,485 real-world ransomware samples from four OS-based non-IID clients, we compare AdaFedXplain against FedAvg, FedProx, and SCAFFOLD. According to experimental data, AdaFedXplain outperforms all baselines with 99.59% detection accuracy and 99.64% F1-score while cutting energy usage by 75%, latency by 65%, and communication overhead by 75%. The ablation investigation demonstrates that every element enhances performance. Security analysts can use SHAP explainability to identify important PE header characteristics that influence detection decisions. Our system provides a collaborative ransomware detection solution that is efficient and interpretable, while reducing privacy risks through federated learnings data-local training paradigm.

papers.title: From Last-Layer to Cross-Layer: One-Shot Joint Classifier Reconstruction for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy. However, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data inevitably introduces classifier bias, leading to significant performance degradation. Existing studies primarily focus on calibrating or reconstructing the classifier after FL training to alleviate this bias. We find that the last-layer representations of the global model are often suboptimal for establishing a global decision boundary. Instead, classifiers constructed based on intermediate-layer representations can achieve superior performance. This finding provides a critical insight into overcoming the performance bottleneck inherent in existing paradigms. Nevertheless, identifying the optimal layer without auxiliary datasets or prior knowledge remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we propose FLARE (Federated Cross-Layer Joint ClAssifier REconstruction) which rethinks classifier reconstruction from a cross-layer perspective and generalizes ridge regression to jointly exploit cross-layer representations, thereby surpassing the performance of any individual layer. Specifically, after FL training, clients perform only a single forward pass to extract class-conditional statistics from predefined layers. The server aggregates these statistics to construct a joint cross-layer ridge classifier, where an adaptive coupling coefficient regulates cross-layer correlations, thereby facilitating the integration of complementary discriminative information. Extensive experiments across 11 datasets, 8 model architectures, and diverse data heterogeneity scenarios demonstrate that FLARE, as a plug-and-play post-processing method, improves accuracy by 11.35% with only one additional communication round.

papers.title: PCHMR: Empowering and Benchmarking Human Mesh Recovery in Privacy-Constrained Real-World Settings
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning directly on user-side data is an effective way to improve the performance of widely adopted data-driven human mesh recovery (HMR) models. However, doing so for existing HMR methods often assumes aggregating user-side data from real-world HMR-deployed devices to a central training server, posing a significant privacy risk as sensitive human images are transmitted. How can human mesh recovery be evaluated and improved in privacy-constrained real-world settings? We study this question through a benchmark in which state-of-the-art HMR models are trained with federated learning and a secure-aggregation variant, neither of which centralizes raw images, and evaluated across a wide range of client-scale and data-heterogeneity settings. We document that common HMR training pipelines are built around centralized data access and quantify how representative HMR backbones behave when that assumption is removed. Furthermore, to study the data bottleneck of privacy-constrained HMR training, we propose DePoser, a local annotation and fine-tuning pipeline enhanced with depth foundation models, with which collaboratively trained HMR models can be locally tailored to the end user's distribution. On in-the-wild data, fine-tuning on DePoser annotations improves personalization accuracy, measured against DePoser-generated pseudo-ground truth. This benchmark aims to support future work on privacy-constrained HMR models and their real-world deployment and evaluation.

papers.title: A Multi-Step Inertial ADMM Algorithm for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning has recently emerged as an important paradigm for large-scale distributed model training, which can be naturally formulated as a class of distributed learning problems. The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is a widely used approach for solving such problems. However, its practical performance is often hindered by significant communication overhead and system heterogeneity. In this paper, we propose a multi-step inertial ADMM algorithm, called MiFedADMM, for federated learning. The proposed method leverages multiple historical iterates on the server side to construct a higher-order extrapolation after each aggregation to accelerate the convergence behavior. Under mild assumptions, we establish convergence results for the single-step variant of the proposed method and derive an O(1/K) convergence rate. Numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and improved performance of the proposed method compared with existing approaches.

papers.title: Frequency-Domain Membership Inference Does Not Beat Confidence Thresholding: A Band-Resolved Analysis of Why
papers.abstract: A widely repeated account of membership inference holds that models lean on fine-grained detail for samples they have memorized, so degrading an input's resolution should expose membership through how quickly a prediction falls apart. We test that account band by band. A monotone family of zero-phase low-pass filters is applied to each query image, the target's confidence on its original prediction is read at every step, and the resulting decay is scored in a dozen ways. Two federated ResNet-18 targets are studied, one trained normally and one pushed to a 45.1-point generalization gap. The account does not survive. On the normally trained target the best profile score reaches an AUC of 0.513 against 0.537 for a single confidence threshold, and on the overfit target 0.735 against 0.943. A search over 1206 candidate scores, with direction chosen on a held-out half and a fitted combination as an upper bound, produces no score that beats the threshold in either regime. The failure has a mechanism: the mean confidence gap between members and non-members grows as detail is removed, exactly as the hypothesis predicts, but the spread grows faster, so discriminability falls from the first step onward. Decomposing each image into phase and magnitude shows why no band-localized operation can work, since the advantage travels with image structure, surviving at 0.567 when the phase is kept and collapsing to 0.492 when only the magnitude is. Membership is a whole-image identity effect rather than an accumulation of spectral energy in any band, and defenses aimed at high-frequency reliance are aimed at the wrong target.

papers.title: StarMind: Challenges and Opportunities in Orbital Computing
papers.abstract: Space-based artificial intelligence (AI) is moving beyond isolated onboard processing toward constellation-scale computing over optical inter-satellite links (OISLs). Yet current infrastructures remain fragmented, making end-to-end (E2E) coordination across heterogeneous and multi-vendor systems difficult. This article examines the StarMind vision and develops a reference framework for distributed orbital computing. It organizes the system into five layers and defines six standardizable interfaces that link mission intent to resource conditions and trustworthy result delivery. The framework also clarifies the operational constraints that determine whether orbital cooperation is worthwhile. In a representative synthetic aperture radar/interferometric SAR (SAR/InSAR) case study, the framework reduces E2E latency to 41-min, compared with 61-min for localized onboard computing and 146-min for ground-based processing. This gain does not rely on faster processors in orbit. Instead, it comes from reducing contact waiting and urgent Earth downlink traffic through resource-aware task placement and gateway selection. Feasibility analysis shows that the proposed framework is more effective when source datasets are large, output products are compact, and optical inter-satellite link capacity is sufficient. When these conditions are absent, conventional processing may remain preferable. Finally, we discuss research opportunities in joint task partitioning and cross-domain orchestration, hierarchical federated intelligence, and large model-enabled intelligence to advance an interoperable space-ground computing continuum.

papers.title: Permeability heterogeneity controls fluid migration and microseismicity evolution in The Geysers geothermal field, California
papers.abstract: Fracture networks directly govern the efficiency of geothermal energy extraction and play a critical role in fluid migration and microearthquake generation. Using deep learning and Markov clustering, we build a high-resolution microseismic catalog covering the past decade for The Geysers geothermal field, California. Our observations reveal distinctive clustering patterns and inferred fracture systems tightly correlated with injection operations. Source mechanism analyses and pore pressure simulations indicate that the inferred connected fracture network provides pathways for rapid and directional pore pressure diffusion, highlighting that heterogeneous permeability controls the localized migration of fluids and the associated microseismic response. Our study highlights the importance of continuous and integrated seismic monitoring for ensuring the sustainability of long-term reservoir development and exploitation. Continuous seismic observations and numerical simulations reveal that, over the past decade, fluid migration and microseismic responses at The Geysers geothermal field have been primarily controlled by heterogeneous permeability.

papers.title: Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify
papers.abstract: Deciphering the highly coupled regulatory circuits that drive cellular dynamics remains a fundamental goal in biology. However, capturing the multi-scale time-lagged dynamics and combinatorial regulatory logic of gene regulation remains challenging. Here we present scMagnify, a deep-learning-based framework that leverages chromatin accessibility and gene expression via Granger causality to reconstruct and decompose multi-scale gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Diverse benchmarks demonstrate scMagnify’s favorable performance. scMagnify employs tensor decomposition to identify combinatorial TF modules and their activation profiles across multiple time-lags. We applied scMagnify to human hematopoiesis and mouse pancreas development, where it recovered known lineage-driving regulators and provided further insights into the combinatorial logic underlying cell fate decisions. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify’s intercellular communication module mapped key signaling-to-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes. In summary, scMagnify provides a robust computational framework for dissecting the multi-scale regulatory logic that governs complex biological processes in development and disease. Chen and colleagues present scMagnify, a framework that uses single-cell multi-omic data to reconstruct and decompose time-lagged gene regulatory networks. The study analyses regulatory programs associated with development and disease.

papers.title: De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain-as-prompt deep learning framework
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial lipopeptides (AMLPs) represent a promising solution to global antibiotic crisis, yet their precision design remains challenging due to the inability of current computational models to account for N-terminal fatty acid modification. Here we develop a deep learning-driven AMLP model for de novo design of AMLPs by integrating a chain-as-prompt mechanism with domain-adaptive transfer learning, effectively bridging the representation gap between peptide sequence and lipid-induced bioactivity. Using the AMLP model, 2657 evolutionarily selected RiPP-derived core peptide sequences from 96,911 bacterial genomes are inspiringly designed for virtual lipidation with seven N-terminal fatty acid chains (C6–C18) followed by predictive screening, generating 6197 candidate sequences. Notably, we find that both high KRH rate ( ≥ 0.3) and common fatty acid tails (C12 and C16) are also critical for further selection of candidate AMLPs, resulting in 289 sequences. Then, 46 are randomly synthesized, with 44 showing antimicrobial activities (a positive rate of 95.7%). The lead antibiotic LP630 exhibits broad-spectrum activities against typical Gram-positive, Gram-negative and mycobacterial strains by targeting multiple bacterial cell membrane components, and demonstrates potent therapeutic efficacy in murine wound infection models. Our study provides a streamlined and universal paradigm for deep learning-enabled high-throughput discovery of novel lipopeptide therapeutics. Authors present their chain-as-prompt deep learning framework, which identifies antimicrobial lipopeptides that show efficacy against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens in laboratory and animal model.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Dual-Stage Latency Optimization for Closed-Loop 6G V2I Digital Twins
papers.abstract: Wireless Digital Twins are emerging as a key enabler for predictive network control in 6G Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) systems. However, closed-loop V2I DTs face two dual-stage communication bottlenecks arising from model parameter exchange for V2I DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic delivery after each reconstruction. This paper proposes a closed-loop dual-stage End-to-End (E2E) latency optimization framework that integrates Compressed Personalized Federated Learning with a unified Large-Language-Model-guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approach. A CPFL-enabled decision-oriented V2I DT is first constructed by jointly predicting Path Loss (PL) and Quality-of-Experience (QoE)-oriented Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Then the framework comprises two temporally coupled but latency-wise distinct optimization stages: Stage I minimizes the joint Uplink (UL) and Downlink (DL) E2E transmission latency of compressed shared backbone's parameters, and Stage II minimizes the service-aware E2E latency of multi-service V2I traffic. As the two stages share aligned agent roles and action space, we develop a unified Semantic-Aware Guidance-Enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization framework, in which the LLM acts as a training-time semantic planner that provides high-level traffic splitting and power allocation guidance to reduce inefficient exploration, while the MARL agents execute feasible low-level actions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables efficient V2I DT reconstruction and significantly reduces both E2E latency for DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic. The proposed SAGE-MAPPO supports cross-stage policy reuse by sequentially solving the two stages within each DT update cycle, which accelerates convergence relative to the existing baselines and facilitates timely DT updates in dynamic V2I scenarios.

papers.title: FederatedBytes: Tokenizer-Free, Byte-Level Small Language Models for Efficient Multimodal Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a powerful machine learning framework that allows building a global model from the contributions of multiple, distributed clients, while ensuring the privacy of their local data. However, its heavy computational and communication overheads challenge its use for contemporary AI workloads such as natural language processing (NLP) and multimodal analysis. For this reason, this paper presents a novel small language model that leverages byte-level text and multimodal data processing, enhanced by a linear attention mechanism, to enable manageable Federated Learning of NLP and multimodal analysis tasks. The proposed model, nicknamed FederatedBytes, manages to process text and any other data types, including images, by treating its input as a mere sequence of bytes, while its lean linear attention mechanism allows abating the overall memory and computational footprint. To prove the effectiveness of the proposed model we have carried out an extensive performance evaluation on sentiment analysis tasks in multilingual and multimodal settings over the Multilingual Amazon Reviews and ScienceQA datasets. The experimental results show that FederatedBytes has been able to outperform comparable models such as ByT5 and LSTM, achieving higher accuracy while significantly reducing memory and communication overheads.

papers.title: Bridging Compressed Communication and Local Steps via Spectral Method in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of complex models across large-scale networks of edge devices while keeping data localized. However, data heterogeneity and high communication overhead remain fundamental bottlenecks. Recently, the spectral optimizer Muon has demonstrated remarkable advantages over Adam-like methods in centralized training. While recent efforts have attempted to transition Muon to FL, naive integrations into traditional architectures fail short. Crucially, existing approaches do not support the the communication compression and local steps --- the two foundational techniques of efficient FL. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel spectral FL method that utilizes both local updates and compression. We establish rigorous convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, notably eliminating the restrictive bounded heterogeneity condition. Empirical evaluation on standard image classification benchmarks validates the efficiency and robustness of our approach.

papers.title: TALLOP: Joint Optimization of Local Training and Communication Compression for Time-Constrained Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Minimizing the wall-clock time required to reach a target accuracy is crucial in federated learning (FL), where many applications require frequent model updates as data distributions evolve over time. Nevertheless, in heterogeneous environments, slow clients with limited computational and communication capabilities can delay global synchronization, forcing faster clients to wait and increasing the overall training time. To mitigate this straggler effect, recent studies have introduced per-round time constraints and adapted client workloads within the available time. However, these approaches primarily focus on local computation, whereas communication can become a major bottleneck in communication-limited environments, motivating the joint optimization of training workload and communication compression. Although previous studies have explored such joint optimization, determining an effective training--communication balance under a fixed per-round time budget remains challenging, as the resulting model performance depends on both training progress and compression-induced degradation. We therefore propose TALLOP, which jointly optimizes the local training workload and communication compression under per-round time constraints. TALLOP predicts the training loss achievable under different computation budgets from the early-stage mini-batch loss trajectory (LENS), and estimates the degradation caused by communication compression using a compression-error model (CLEN). TALLOP combines these predictions to select the training-communication allocation that minimizes the post-compression loss under the given round time constraint. Experiments in heterogeneous FL environments show that TALLOP generally achieves competitive or improved time-to-accuracy compared with approaches that optimize only local training or neither, although the benefit over training-only adaptation depends on the setting.

papers.title: Client-Aware Security Adaptive Early Exit Vision Transformers for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) trains a shared model across data-owning clients without centralizing raw data, but client data difficulty and compute budgets can differ. We study local early-exit Vision Transformer (ViT) inference, where an intermediate classifier may return a prediction before the final Transformer stage. The proposed method replaces one global acceptance threshold with a client-specific base threshold from label entropy and shallow-exit confidence, then adjusts each input using predictive entropy, confidence, top-two class margin, and exit depth. Aggregation uses only clients that updated a parameter. Security-aware routing reaches 88.70% CIFAR-10 accuracy with 32.0% depth saving and 73.7% ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy with 30\% saving. On matched six-client non-IID CIFAR-100, full-depth accuracy is 72.28% versus 68.20--71.80% for four heterogeneous-FL baselines; robustness-aware routing reaches 70.01% with 32.55% saving.

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence reveals spatially divergent effects of global change on mammals
papers.abstract: Abstract Understanding how global change reshapes species distributions remains a central challenge in ecology, yet most global assessments treat environmental drivers as static, uniform, or aggregate influences. This obscures where, why, and how specific drivers generate ecological risk or opportunity. Here, we apply explainable machine learning to assess how climate averages, variability, extremes, and land cover are projected to reshape future distributions of 1,992 terrestrial mammals. Using Shapley Additive Explanations with species distribution models, we quantify the directional contribution of 16 environmental drivers and track how these contributions change over space and time. We propose two ecological diagnostics, directional turnovers and favorability shifts, that reveal where drivers switch from favorable to unfavorable, or the reverse, and where their influence strengthens or weakens without sign reversal. While not designed to infer causation, our framework assesses whether projected spatial patterns align with ecological expectations. We show that climate extremes impose intense but spatially restricted impacts, temperature-related drivers dominate exposure patterns, particularly for specialist species, and the same driver can impose risk in one region while creating opportunity in another. By decomposing projected biodiversity change into driver-specific signatures, our framework advances biodiversity forecasting toward a more actionable understanding of ecological risk and opportunity.

papers.title: PhD students who write dissertations with AI less likely to stay in academia
A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria
papers.abstract: Abstract Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 + P2 plasmid pool. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction. Across single-strain trajectories, combined plate-reader and flow-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity- and variance-dependent weight change. At the single-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary. In mixed populations and co-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic-tac-toe lessons. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear-classifier architectures. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights.

papers.title: History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI
An Alternating Minimization Algorithm for Federated Sparse Orthogonal Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an alternating minimization algorithm for federated sparse orthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization (ONMF) with emphases on controlling client drift. To reduce communication frequency, clients perform multiple local updates between communication rounds, biasing updates toward their respective local objectives and giving rise to client drift, particularly under data heterogeneity. In federated sparse ONMF, global nonsmooth regularization further complicates drift control, as proximal mappings generally do not commute with averaging. To address these challenges, we develop an effective optimization algorithm that introduces variable splitting to decouple proximal operator evaluation from communication, allowing clients to handle joint sparsity regularization locally. In addition, the algorithm incorporates a correction term into the local gradients to adjust the update directions and mitigate client drift. We theoretically establish that the proposed algorithm achieves sublinear convergence to a bounded residual error under some mild conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate favorable convergence behavior on a synthetic dataset and competitive clustering performance on real-world multi-view datasets.

papers.title: Local Epochs as Optimal Stopping: Theory and Evidence in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: How long should each client train before communicating? Federated learning usually answers with a fixed, hand-tuned number of local epochs, yet an extra epoch helps only while the loss it removes outweighs the client drift it adds. We cast local training as finite-horizon optimal stopping: a client trains while the next epoch's expected loss reduction exceeds its priced squared drift. We prove that this one-stage look-ahead threshold is optimal whenever stopping decisions are nested, derive closed forms for geometric and power-law returns, and show that an estimated rule loses utility only through wrong-signed decisions. Epoch-level evidence supports the model's structure (geometric diminishing returns and additive drift) and reveals a simple regularity: the stage of training, not the client, sets the budget. The resulting rule, FedStop, is never more than one point below tuned FedAvg in mean accuracy. Where its budgets vary, it raises worst-decile accuracy by 4-8 points over tuned FedAvg and an adaptive-interval baseline, and every one of these gains remains significant after a Holm correction. Against the client-side stopping rules ALT and FLASH, it has the highest CIFAR-10 worst decile on every seed and is level elsewhere. It stays stable where per-client early stopping collapses, and each stopping decision takes constant time.

papers.title: NOMAI: Scalable Federated Learning with Private Weights
papers.abstract: The twin goals of privacy-preserving federated learning (FL) -- harnessing distributed data while protecting the parties who contribute it -- demands three properties: model privacy, data privacy, and integrity. Achieving all three in a realistic deployment -- with a single coordinator and millions of users -- remains an open challenge that prior work has yet to fully resolve. We present NOMAI, the first scalable MPC-based FL system to provide all three guarantees simultaneously. NOMAI operates under an honest-majority assumption in the semi-honest model, with an extension to the malicious-with-abort setting. At its core, NOMAI combines a multi-committee MPC architecture with packed Shamir secret sharing, enabling SIMD-style secure computation that scales far beyond what monolithic n-party protocols can support. We further introduce ML-aware optimizations and new cryptographic primitives that substantially reduce per-user overhead. Our evaluation shows NOMAI is practically deployable at unprecedented scale: it reduces per-user computation to just <350 ms (semi-honest) and <700 ms (malicious) for per iteration of training MNIST, achieving three orders-of-magnitude improvements over prior work while seamlessly supporting populations of over 106 users. This demonstrates, for the first time, that MPC-based FL can meet the scale demands of real-world systems without compromising on privacy or integrity.

papers.title: Sparse Federated Echo State Networks for Time-Series Classification via Smooth-L1 Regularization
papers.abstract: Echo State Networks (ESNs), as lightweight implementations of reservoir computing, provide efficient solutions for temporal data processing in resource-constrained environments. While standard ESNs offer computational efficiency, their dense readout layers inflate the stored model and the per-sample inference cost. This paper introduces a Smooth-L1 regularized ESN (SL1ESN) that promotes sparsity in the readout layer while preserving differentiability for gradient-based optimization. The method employs a twice-differentiable Smooth-L1 approximation compatible with Newton's method, which we exploit both for centralized training and for a second-order (Newton-step) federated aggregation scheme. Under a single fixed shrinkage threshold shared by every dataset and both settings, experiments on seven time-series classification benchmarks show that SL1ESN learns readouts that are 77-95% sparse in the centralized setting and 75-95% sparse in the federated one. On five of the seven benchmarks, the mean accuracy of the sparse readout over ten seeds differs from that of the stronger dense baseline by at most 0.7 points in the centralized setting and 1.6 points in the federated one, differences of the same order as the seed-to-seed variation, while on the remaining two it trails by 2.4-5.8 points. The second-order federated update converges in only a few rounds. The resulting sparsity compresses the stored model, the per-sample inference cost, and the server-to-client broadcast by a comparable factor. These results demonstrate the practical value of sparse readouts for edge computing and IoT deployments.

papers.title: FIRM: Fisher-Informed Retention Merging for Federated LLM Unlearning
papers.abstract: Federated LLM unlearning addresses targeted knowledge removal when forget and retain data remain distributed across private clients and are inaccessible to the server. The resulting locally trained adapters encode conflicting objectives, making their aggregation fundamentally different from conventional federated optimization. A key failure mode is magnitude explosion, whereby unnormalized cross-client aggregation increases the merged update magnitude and degrades retained utility under stronger unlearning. We propose FIRM (Fisher-Informed Retention Merging), a single-round framework for stable and retention-aware server-side aggregation. FIRM uses client-local Fisher statistics as a unified sensitivity signal to construct a Fisher-normalized base merge and impose explicit control over retain-sensitive parameters. Its second-order retention projection admits a unique minimum-distance solution, while the corresponding dual scales with the number of retain clients rather than the model dimension. Experiments across WMDP, TOFU, and MUSE-HP using Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B show utility gains at comparable forgetting on WMDP and MUSE-HP, with metric-dependent trade-offs on TOFU. Controlled comparisons support benefits of the combined base merge and additional retention correction at selected operating points.

papers.title: Personalized Projected Ascent for Federated Stackelberg Optimization
papers.abstract: Federated minimax problems, such as distributionally robust optimization and adversarial training, include an inner maximization variable built from each client's local data. These variables differ in meaning and dimension from one client to the next, so averaging them across clients, as standard federated minimax methods do, is ill-posed. We therefore study a federated minimax problem where the minimization variable $\mathbf{x}$ is shared and aggregated, while each client retains the maximization variable $\mathbf{y}_i$ (personalized). Because these applications constrain $\mathbf{y}_i$ to a compact convex set, we analyze projected ascent directly. We show that, in the nonconvex-concave regime, this projected personalized scheme attains the standard sublinear rate. In the nonconvex-PL regime, however, it hits a stepsize-invariant noise floor due to stochastic $\mathbf{y}_i$ updates. To mitigate this, we propose VR-SGDA, incorporating a variance-reduced ascent step where each client maintains a private variable snapshot. By evaluating current and snapshot gradients on the same sample, the constant variance is replaced by a vanishing drift under a two-timescale regime. VR-SGDA eliminates the noise floor, attaining sublinear leading rates while preserving personalization and projection. Experiments on subpopulation-robustness and NLP adversarial training confirm both the worst-group robustness benefits and the two-timescale tracking mechanism.

papers.title: FedPix: Learning What to Share with Less Leakage in Federated Intelligence
papers.abstract: Existing federated intelligence paradigms primarily focus on how models are trained or aggregated, while overlooking a more fundamental question: \textbf{what information should leave the client?} Existing methods often share model updates that users cannot easily inspect, or data representations that may reveal sensitive information. Moreover, generating these representations can be computationally expensive for resource-constrained clients. We observe that image classification does not require all the visual details needed to reconstruct the original image. This suggests that clients could share less information while preserving task performance. However, learning what to preserve is challenging when the server cannot access raw client data. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{FedPix}, which learns to share compact, visually inspectable images instead of model updates or intermediate features. The key idea is to use the shared representations themselves to learn what information should be preserved and what can be discarded. By balancing task utility and reconstruction resistance, FedPix enables the server to improve the representations without accessing raw client data, while keeping client-side computation lightweight. Extensive experiments on BloodMNIST, CIFAR-10, FashionMNIST, and MNIST demonstrate that FedPix achieves strong reconstruction resistance, with reconstruction PSNR as low as 6.87~dB and synthetic PSNR as low as 6.74~dB. Meanwhile, FedPix reduces client runtime by up to 96.0\% (from 1223~s to 49~s on CIFAR-10), while maintaining competitive classification accuracy of 99.18\% on MNIST, 89.97\% on FashionMNIST, 82.24\% on BloodMNIST, and 65.63\% on CIFAR-10.

papers.title: Federated Art Chase: Privacy Leakage and Data Poisoning in Federated Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly used to adapt a pretrained, centrally fine-tuned model to data that remain on user devices, beyond training a model from scratch. In this report, prepared for the 4th Federated Machine Learning International Summer School, we study the privacy and integrity of this approach with a reproducible pipeline. An ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV4-Conv-Small model is fine-tuned centrally on ten Quick, Draw! classes (97.50% test accuracy) and then adapted with head-only FedAvg over ten non-IID clients, which raises client training accuracy from 90.34% to 91.49% while preserving global accuracy. We evaluate four adversarial scenarios. First, from a single one-step client update, an honest-but-curious server recovers the complete private label set, but its reconstructions follow class prototypes rather than the private drawings (mean SSIM 0.130). Second, from a one-round FedAvg aggregate, label-count recovery falls from 87.5% with one client to 75.0% with five and ten clients, below the 80.0% of an uninformed uniform guess. Third, under FedAvg, a backdoor injected by 30%, 50%, and 100% of the clients reaches an attack success rate (ASR) of 21.9%, 31.3%, and 54.7% at a cost of at most 0.8 percentage points of clean accuracy, whereas label flipping is effective only when most of the source-class data are relabeled. Fourth, FLTrust with a root set retained from centralized fine-tuning lowers the backdoor ASR to 1.8% and 4.0% at 30% and 50% malicious clients and the label-flipping ASR from 12.6% to 0.8% without measurable clean-accuracy loss, but provides no protection when every client is malicious. The report closes with a live session in which participants draw, fine-tune, and poison the model through Indigma's FedMaestro orchestrator. Code and executed notebooks, runnable on Google Colab, are at https://github.com/Indigma-Innovations/fl-summer-school.

papers.title: Initiating Removal from Operational Symptoms in Federated Vehicular Networks
papers.abstract: Connected vehicles train a driving model through federated learning (FL) and drive with it, so a faulty contribution often surfaces only as a delayed symptom on the road. Federated unlearning (FU) assumes that a removal request names what to forget. A symptom names no vehicle or round, and aggregation has already spread its cause across the fleet. We propose \underline{A}ggregation-\underline{T}ime \underline{O}perational-evidence \underline{N}eutralization of \underline{E}ffects (\method{}), which makes unlearning a term of the FL aggregation rule. \method{} projects everyday driving errors and reported symptoms onto a subspace spanned by recent global increments. It propagates the surviving effect of every contribution with curvature estimated from these increments and scores all contributions in one backward pass. A two-tier correction suppresses suspected effects in every round and eliminates confirmed ones after a one-round probe. We prove that backward scoring matches forward scoring and that the elimination is exact when training is flat outside the subspace. On three driving datasets, \method{} leaves 43\% to 61\% less residual harm than the strongest baseline in eight of nine settings while staying within 0.36 points of full retraining in utility.

papers.title: StratFL: Countering Covert Model Poisoning Attacks with Strategic Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Advanced persistent threats (APTs) are a major concern in federated learning (FL) deployments in critical sectors such as healthcare, and finance. Traditional defense mechanisms fail to contain APTs due to their intermittent attacking behavior. This paper addresses a specific type of APT called covert model poisoning (CMP) where the attacker intermittently injects poisoned model updates in a covert manner. The interaction between the FL server and a CMP attacker is modeled as an imperfect repeated game where both players cannot observe each other's actions. A novel adversarial search algorithm called StratFL is designed alongside novel belief update algorithms at both the server and adversary. Experiments are designed using MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets to evaluate and compare StratFL's performance against state-of-the-art methods. Empirical convergence of belief update algorithms is demonstrated across various security vignettes. At the same time, StratFL is found to exhibit an improved accuracy of 10% compared to state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: SPADE-KD: Peer-to-Peer Collaborative Learning under Heterogeneous Settings
papers.abstract: Peer-to-peer collaborative learning is an emerging distributed deep learning paradigm that eliminates the need for a central aggregator and disseminator, avoiding the single-point-of-failure and bottleneck issues they can bring. Many such approaches use parameter averaging, requiring clients to have homogeneous model architectures, whereas others use knowledge distillation as an alternative while leaning on shared public data or centralized control infrastructure. Many of these approaches also make a one-size-fits-all assumption, i.e., jointly training a single, globally optimal solution for all clients, when in reality, clients' underlying data distributions might differ such that a globally optimal solution may not be locally optimal for all clients. To enable collaborative learning in environments with both model architecture and data distribution heterogeneity, we present SPADE-KD -- a fully decentralized model distillation framework that optimizes collaboration towards personalized rather than global performance. SPADE-KD leverages two mechanisms -- adaptive distillation and utility-driven peer selection. Adaptive distillation modulates the strength of each incoming model transfer by the performance advantage of the incoming model compared to the native model measured by their task losses, such that a client will distill more aggressively from incoming models that outperform it on its own local data. Utility-driven peer selection uses the loss-informed utility derived from adaptive distillation to rank prospective partners, focusing on exchanges that measurably improve the local model while suppressing low-utility transfers. Using federated classification tasks, we demonstrate that SPADE-KD consistent outperforms naive decentralized distillation with lower loss and faster convergence and that its individual components are more effective together than independently.

papers.title: Spatial targeting and expansion prevention offer effective pathways to protect African maize from parasitic weeds
papers.abstract: Parasitic weeds (Striga spp.) threaten food security for over 300 million Africans dependent on maize, yet economic impact estimates vary widely due to high uncertainties, limiting strategic planning and interventions. We developed a spatially-explicit framework overcoming data scarcity through integrated agroecological similarity mapping, machine learning, and stochastic modeling to quantify Striga economic impacts across African maize production systems. Our analysis resolves decades of uncertainty, revealing annual losses of US$1.04 billion (95% confidence interval: US$0.94–1.15 billion) with high spatial concentration: less than 6% of infested areas generate half the economic losses. Agricultural expansion represents the primary future risk, potentially tripling losses by 2050 as Striga colonizes new areas. Interventions achieve maximum impact through a dual strategy: spatial targeting of high-loss zones coupled with prevention in agricultural expansion areas. This targeted approach outperforms uniform intensification, providing a blueprint for managing agricultural pests in data-scarce regions. Parasitic weeds damage maize harvests across Africa, but their economic cost has been unclear. This study estimates about US$1 billion in annual losses, concentrated in hotspots; targeted control and spread prevention could help protect maize

papers.title: Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors
papers.abstract: Abstract High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application. We developed surrogate models trained on $$760$$ 760 CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions (e.g., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration), and local spatial descriptors (e.g., distance to the feeding point). Among various methods, attention-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy (test $${{{\rm{R}}}}^{2}\approx 0.91$$ R 2 ≈ 0.91 ), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond-scale inference—up to a million-fold speed-up compared to CFD. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real-time optimization and digital-twin frameworks in bioprocessing. Our results demonstrate that data-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control.

papers.title: ArXiv versus AI slop: will capping preprint submissions work?
Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models
papers.abstract: A prevailing view holds that although neuroscience historically inspired AI, its role in the recent evolution of AI, driven by the scaling of foundation models, is minor. We challenge this perspective by establishing a biological analogy between simplified dendritic neuron models and the attention mechanisms central to AI foundation models. We show that AI attention mechanisms bear direct mappings to internal neuronal complexities arising from dendritic organization, rather than to the mere inter-neuronal connections of simple point neurons. This re-conceptualization not only offers a neuroscience-informed perspective for understanding core AI methodologies beyond their formulation as abstract mathematical operations, but also paves the way for neuro-inspired foundation models that leverage neuroscientific insights to sustainably advance modern AI beyond scaling laws. As an example of this paradigm, we introduce a dendritic-inspired complexity framework, and design a hybrid-attention foundation model with dendritic-inspired sparse computation, which enhances memory capacity while reducing computational demands. Our model supports a 50M context window-equivalent to roughly 40 volumes of Shakespeare-demonstrating superior long-term memory capabilities. This work pioneers a paradigm that harnesses intra-neuronal dynamics to drive sustained advances in modern AI, while also offering a potential route to understanding dendritic computational mechanisms. How insights from neuroscience can inform future AI foundation models is an active area of exploration. Here, the authors show that AI attention mechanisms resemble dendritic computations within individual neurons rather than interactions between neurons, inspiring a dendritic-inspired model with improved long-term memory and reduced computational cost.

papers.title: Is AI eroding PhD students’ critical thinking and analysis skills?
Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes
Hybrid DeepXAI Fusion Network for Interpretable Big Data Analytics and Secure Cloud Decision-Making Systems
papers.abstract: Big data analytics supports modern intelligent systems, but model complexity and limited transparency can undermine interpretability, trust, and security in decision-making. This paper presents the Hybrid DeepXAI Fusion Network, a deep learning framework that integrates temporal, relational, and contextual features with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) mechanisms. The architecture combines one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNNs) for temporal feature extraction, Transformer encoders for contextual modeling, and graph neural networks (GNNs) for inter-feature dependency analysis. An attention-based fusion mechanism integrates these representations. Class Activation Mapping (CAM) and an explanation loss are incorporated to improve interpretability and explanation consistency. The framework is designed for deployment in a federated cloud architecture, using homomorphic encryption and blockchain-based auditing to support data privacy and accountability. Experimental evaluations across healthcare, finance, and energy datasets report 98.42% accuracy, 97.9% precision, 98.1% recall, and a 98.0% F1-score, outperforming the evaluated CNN-LSTM, Transformer-only, and XGBoost baselines. Under projected gradient descent (PGD) adversarial perturbations, the model reportedly retains accuracy above 91.5%. Scalability experiments report throughput of 80,000 messages per second with latency below 200 milliseconds. These results suggest that the proposed framework has potential for interpretable and secure cloud-based decision-support systems.

papers.title: FUSE: Fairness-aware Update Screening against Byzantine Exploitation in $q$-Fair Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Client-level fair federated learning, in the form of $q$-fair federated learning ($q$-FFL), agnostic federated learning, or tilted empirical risk minimization, has emerged as an attractive solution to equalize utility across heterogeneous clients. This paradigm grants high-loss clients greater relative influence, while a central server aggregates their loss-weighted updates into a single shared model. Yet, the Byzantine robustness of $q$-fair federated learning has been largely neglected, leaving the server unable to tell legitimate fairness-induced amplification from malicious update scaling. To address this critical gap, we formalize the problem of Byzantine-robust $q$-fair federated learning under an \emph{update-only interface}, in which the server observes nothing but the fairness-scaled client updates. Our analysis under shared class-conditional label skew shows that fairness scaling preserves the nonnegative class-mixture structure of honest updates, while replacing their unit-sum constraint by a client-dependent radial scale. Moving beyond magnitude-based screening, we show that this warped geometry supplies two complementary tests, one radial and one structural, that a single norm cannot provide. We then introduce FUSE, a structure-aware robust aggregator that uses a small trusted labeled dataset for coefficient recovery, scale and cone-consistency screening, and post-screening step-size control. Across four benchmarks and seven Byzantine attacks, FUSE improves seed-wise worst-attack accuracy over the strongest baseline on each benchmark by 3.9--30.1 percentage points, while largely preserving the influence of the high-loss honest clients that fairness is meant to protect.

papers.title: FedRIC: Heterogeneity-Aware Federated Learning with Hard Deadline Constraints in Open RAN
papers.abstract: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RANs) bring intelligence to disaggregated RANs through virtualized platforms and open interfaces, but the stringent latency budgets of the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) and heterogeneous traffic conditions make real-time deployment costly. Centralized learning is ill-suited to the RIC due to its computational burden, timing constraints, and communication overhead, motivating Federated Learning (FL) as a distributed alternative. We formulate FL in O-RAN as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Program (MINLP) that minimizes communication cost and learning time under heterogeneity in User Equipment (UE) compute, traffic, and channel conditions, and decompose it into a UE Assignment (UA) subproblem and a Computation and Bandwidth Allocation (CBA) subproblem. We then propose FedRIC, a heterogeneity-aware FL framework combining compressed gradient descent, slice-aware resource allocation, and multilevel hierarchical aggregation. Experiments show that FedRIC outperforms FedCOM, FedAvg, and QFedAvg in convergence rate, communication cost, and latency.

papers.title: A Large-Dimensional Analysis of Least-Squares Federated Learning via Generalized Total Variation Minimization
papers.abstract: Federated learning over decentralized networks inherently trades off the suppression of local finite-sample noise through collaboration against the bias that collaboration introduces between heterogeneous nodes. We study this tension by performing a large-dimensional analysis of Generalized Total Variation Minimization with least-squares models. Using tools from random matrix theory, we show that Lipschitz observations of the global GTVMin solution concentrate in large dimensions, universally for any underlying network structure. We provide exact analytic expressions for the asymptotically precise performance under both i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. Gaussian mixture distributions on a fixed network. For the latter, these expressions quantify how regularization balances local adaptation against collaboration. Our theoretical results are confirmed by experiments on synthetic and real-world data.

papers.title: Adaptive and Proximal Federated Optimization for Transferable Network Intrusion Detection
papers.abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) based on deep learning often fail to detect attack classes that are absent from training data, limiting their robustness against zero-day threats. This property called transferability across attack classes, remains underexplored especially in federated learning (FL) settings where data heterogeneity and client drift pose additional challenges. Prior work (TabFIDS) showed that FedAvg combined with bootstrapping and temporal averaging improves transferability for cross-device NIDS. In this paper, we explore whether other federated optimizers can do better. We compare two optimizers inspired by FedAdam and FedProx against the FedAvg baseline on the CIC-IDS 2017 dataset using an 11-client federated setup, sweep 10 hyperparameter configurations, and contrast two data-balancing strategies: bootstrapping and SMOTE. Using the count of client pairs whose transferred-model accuracy exceeds 70% as our primary metric (following TabFIDS), the proximal optimizer with a strong regularization term yields 48 transferable pairs versus 42 for FedAvg, while the adaptive optimizer with an aggressive server learning rate yields 46 pairs. SMOTE improves per-pair accuracy over bootstrapping but reduces breadth, revealing a depth-vs-breadth trade-off: high accuracy on a few client pairs versus moderate accuracy across most. These results indicate that the choice of federated optimizer, the rule by which client updates are regularized and aggregated into the global model, is very important for federated NIDS.

papers.title: Safe-FCL: Continual Risk Awareness and Fine-Grained Safety Aggregation for Federated Continual Learning of LLMs
papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning enables large language models (LLMs) to learn collaboratively from distributed client data, but malicious client updates can compromise global model safety. As federated tasks evolve, changing malicious update patterns challenge the ability of existing defenses to maintain reliable risk detection over time. To address this challenge, we propose Safe-FCL, a framework integrating continual risk awareness with fine-grained safety aggregation for federated continual learning of LLMs. Specifically, the Continual Risk Awareness (CRA) mechanism learns emerging risk patterns across sequential tasks and constrains detector updates using a protective subspace derived from historical features, mitigating forgetting of previously learned malicious patterns while adapting to new risks. To translate risk awareness into aggregation-level safety control, the Fine-Grained Safety Aggregation (FGSA) mechanism combines client-level risk assessments from CRA with module-level deviations from historical update behavior to adaptively regulate aggregation contributions, suppressing potentially malicious updates while minimizing unnecessary restrictions on benign updates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Safe-FCL outperforms current SOTA methods, improving global-model Rule and MD-Judge scores in federated continual learning by 0.41% and 0.64%, respectively, while increasing average risk recognition accuracy by 2.01%.

papers.title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
papers.abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1–3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4–10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2–6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11–15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts.
